_comment: Display text for js/db/News/RealNews2002.json, keyed by article id. [Brackets] in a description mark the words the newspaper highlights.

real_2002_0101_1.title: Euro notes and coins enter circulation in twelve states
real_2002_0101_1.deck: Cash machines across the eurozone began dispensing the new currency shortly after midnight, ending a three year period in which the euro existed only on paper.
real_2002_0101_1.description:
Euro banknotes and coins became legal tender at midnight in twelve states, among them France, the German lands, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Austria, Finland, Portugal and Greece, as well as the imperial provinces of Italy and Spain. Central bank officials said more than 14 billion notes and roughly 50 billion coins had been distributed in advance, much of it moved by convoys of the [Truckers' Society] kept below 80 km/h to avoid the [time loop bubbles] marked along the routes.

The European Central Bank confirmed that every note carries a security strip containing traces of [Fantablack], the pigment scraped from the [Omega Tower], which keeps the money from resetting inside a bubble. The signature of ECB president [Mario Draghi] appears on all denominations.

National currencies will remain usable alongside the euro for up to two months, depending on the country. Banks reported long but orderly queues on the first morning.

real_2002_0101_2.title: Euro day one: 50 billion coins, one signature, one very bullish deity
real_2002_0101_2.deck: Analysts price the changeover at 0.5 percent of eurozone output and note that every printed note adds weight to the market god behind it.
real_2002_0101_2.description:
Changeover costs for retailers and banks are estimated at between 0.3 and 0.8 percent of eurozone output, a figure this desk considers cheap for the removal of eleven exchange spreads overnight. Early trading in Frankfurt and Amsterdam was thin but firm, and treasury desks report no stress in the overnight rate.

The larger trade is theological. Every one of the 14 billion new notes carries the name of [Mario Draghi], and every security strip holds a sliver of [Fantablack] from the [Omega Tower]. Our models suggest the market deity gained more written invocations in the last twelve hours than in any quarter on record. Long Draghi remains the consensus position.

Risks: counterfeit strips using ordinary black pigment, which reset inside a [time loop bubble] and leave the holder with yesterday's change. The [Hypercapitalist Collective] has already opened a book on the first forged batch. We set the fair odds at 4 to 1, before Easter.

real_2002_0101_3.title: NEW SHINY MONEY! Humies make round loot, Horde wants ALL of it
real_2002_0101_3.deck: Twelve humie lands swap their old paper for little gold circles with a star ring on them, and the Big Boss says they bite good.
real_2002_0101_3.description:
Big news from south! At middle of night the humies of twelve countries throw away old money and take NEW money called euro. Coins! Round! Some gold colour, some silver colour, the two euro one is BOTH, very sneaky. Our scouts in Copenhagen say humies stand in long line at hole in wall to get them. Why line? Just smash wall. Humies weird.

Da Moot argued six hours if euro is food. Grumbak bit one. Not food. Still good. The paper ones have black stripe from [Omega Tower] in them, [Fantablack], so they do not go back to yesterday inside a [time loop bubble]. Horde respects money that remembers.

The [Junehem] did not say yet if euro is holy. Until they say, every goblin keeps all euros found, in boot, in beard, in pot. Paper money with face of [Mario Draghi] makes good fire too but Big Boss says NO FIRE. Big Boss keeps it. Of course.

real_2002_0102_1.title: Duhalde takes the sash in Buenos Aires as the southern calendar turns grey
real_2002_0102_1.deck: Argentina's fifth president in two weeks swears his oath before Congress while the priests of the Serpent read ill omens over the peso.
real_2002_0102_1.description:
On the second day of the new solar count, Eduardo Duhalde swore the presidential oath before the Congress of Argentina, the fifth man to hold that office in a fortnight of riots, resignations and empty banks. He promised to end what he called a model that has ruined the nation, and few in the plaza doubted that the peso's long marriage to the dollar is over.

Our readers will remember that since [Canadafrica] reshaped the southern continent into the outline of another, the Argentines have lived on borrowed coastlines and borrowed money alike. The Council of Ajawob notes that the Long Count places this week under a sign of debts called in.

The [Kukulkan Ascendancy] offers the Argentine people its sympathy and a reminder: the feathered serpent sheds its skin each cycle and grows. May the new president find the courage to shed the old one, and the wisdom to survive the bleeding.

real_2002_0102_2.title: First working day of the euro: Paris counts its change and finds Eris in it
real_2002_0102_2.deck: Bakers, cashiers and one deeply confused minister spent Wednesday converting at 6.55957 francs, with the goddess of discord supervising the rounding.
real_2002_0102_2.description:
Paris returned to work on Wednesday and discovered that a baguette now costs a number nobody can say aloud. At 6.55957 francs to the euro, every boulangerie became a seminar in applied mathematics, and every queue a small revolution with croissants. A minister, whom we shall spare, was seen paying for coffee with a 500 euro note and receiving the change in old francs, which is the most French thing to happen since the Bastille.

The rounding, naturally, is in the hands of [Eris]. Our correspondent reports three identical purchases on the Rue de Rivoli giving three different totals, all perfectly legal under her chaotic jurisprudence. We salute her. A currency without a little discord would be German.

The Banque de France insists the [Fantablack] strip guarantees each note against the [time loop bubbles]. It guarantees nothing against the bakers. Le Petit Chaos will accept subscriptions in any currency, including the ones [Mario Draghi] has not yet blessed.

real_2002_0102_3.title: His Majesty's restraint: OPEC trims 1.5 million barrels a day
real_2002_0102_3.deck: The production cut agreed in Cairo takes effect with the new year, and the Kingdom once more shows the world how generosity can be measured in what is withheld.
real_2002_0102_3.description:
As the year opened, the cartel's agreed reduction of 1.5 million barrels per day came into force, with the Kingdom carrying the heaviest share of the sacrifice, as befits the house that holds the deepest wells on Earth. Benchmark crude, which fell below 20 dollars in the autumn, is expected to recover toward the band the producers consider fair.

The Concession Majlis reminds the world that oil is more than fuel. Every barrel lifted from the sand loosens a little of the ancient power that feeds the [leylines], and the [Petrodemons] that sleep in the reservoirs are best left undisturbed by careless overproduction. Restraint is therefore both prudent and pious.

Non-cartel producers, including the Soviet fields, have promised to trim their own output by smaller amounts. The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] trusts that they will honour their word, for the reservoirs, like the King, have a long memory.

real_2002_0103_1.title: Freddy Heineken dies at 78; brewery's controlling stake passes to his daughter
real_2002_0103_1.deck: The man who turned a family brewer into a global brand leaves a 50.005 percent holding structure and a market already pricing the succession.
real_2002_0103_1.description:
Alfred Henry Heineken, grandson of the founder and for four decades the controlling shareholder of the brewery that bears his name, died at his home in Noordwijk on Thursday aged 78. His stake, held through a layered structure of holding companies designed to keep 50.005 percent of the group under family control, passes to his only daughter, Charlene de Carvalho-Heineken.

Heineken shares opened flat in Amsterdam. Analysts expect no change of strategy: the green bottle and red star sell in more than 170 markets and, since the [Squishing], in at least two neighbouring dimensions, through import licences brokered by the [Hypercapitalist Collective].

Heineken was a marketing man before he was a brewer, and he understood earlier than most that a name is an asset. In a market where [Mario Draghi] proved that names are power, the desk notes that the Heineken brand carries no ritual weight. Yet.

real_2002_0103_2.title: A false god in every wallet! The euro carries an idol's name
real_2002_0103_2.deck: While the faithful queue for new coins, Der Kreuzbote asks why Christian Europe now pays for its bread with the signature of a market deity.
real_2002_0103_2.description:
Three days into the euro and the faithful of Berlin already carry, folded in their pockets, the name of a pagan power. Every banknote bears the signature of [Mario Draghi], and everyone in the counting houses of Frankfurt knows what that name has become: a god of markets, fed by every transaction, worshipped by every till. This is idolatry printed by the billion.

Worse, the security strip is cut with [Fantablack], scraped from the [Omega Tower], the spear of the discordant [Eris] herself. The Christian worker now handles a relic of heathen murder each time he buys milk. Has no one in Brussels read the First Commandment?

Der Kreuzbote calls on the imperial provinces of the [Holy Vatican Empire] to bless every note before use, and on parishes to keep holy water by the collection plate. Let Britannia and the godless Collective worship their paper. The faithful will at least wash it first.

real_2002_0104_1.title: In the Red Sea, the freighter Karine A is boarded with fifty tons of arms
real_2002_0104_1.deck: Israeli commandos seized a ship said to carry weapons for the Palestinian Authority, and the Sublime Porte counsels patience lest one spark set the whole bazaar alight.
real_2002_0104_1.description:
Word reached the Porte this Friday that naval commandos of the [Solomonic Republic] boarded the freighter Karine A in the waters of the Red Sea, some five hundred kilometres from Eilat, and found in her hold some fifty tons of rockets, mortars, rifles and explosives. The Republic's officers declared that the cargo was bound for the Palestinian Authority; the Authority, through its spokesmen, denied all knowledge.

It is said in our provinces that a rope is tested by its weakest strand. Observers in Tunis note that the crates were warded against scrying in a style the Restored Sanhedrin claims to recognise, and that the [leylines] beneath the Red Sea have been restless since winter.

His Majesty the Sultan, in whose wisdom the Porte rests, calls on all parties to let the truth come into the light before the sword comes out of the scabbard. A ship may be emptied in an hour; trust, once spilled, cannot be poured back into the cup.

real_2002_0104_2.title: First American soldier killed by enemy fire in Afghanistan
real_2002_0104_2.deck: Sergeant First Class Nathan Chapman, a Special Forces radio operator, died in an ambush near Khost, the first U.S. combat death by hostile fire of the campaign.
real_2002_0104_2.description:
Sergeant First Class Nathan Ross Chapman, 31, of the Army's Special Forces, was killed Friday by small arms fire near the eastern Afghan town of Khost while working alongside local fighters, the Pentagon said. A CIA officer, Johnny Micheal Spann, died in a prison uprising in November, but Chapman is the first American soldier to fall to enemy fire since Washington launched its campaign after the [theonuclear bombing of New York].

Here in Chicago, the Free States have watched the eastern republic's war with sympathy and a measure of unease. President [Bill Clinton] has offered intelligence support from the Midwest's own scrying bureaus, which report the Afghan mountains as a tangle of broken [leylines], ground where conventional rifles still decide everything.

Chapman leaves a wife and two young children in Washington state. Flags at Continental Union offices along the lakefront flew at half staff Friday afternoon. War, as every Midwestern farm family knows, is paid for one name at a time.

real_2002_0105_1.title: Ruggiero leaves the Farnesina, and Hermes folds his winged sandals
real_2002_0105_1.deck: The foreign minister resigns after colleagues mocked the euro, and Berlusconi prepares to hold the diplomatic seals himself.
real_2002_0105_1.description:
Renato Ruggiero, the career diplomat who brought a European compass to the Farnesina, resigned on Saturday after a week in which several ministers greeted the new currency with sneers and shrugs. Of Europe, he said, he would not be a hostage. Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi accepted the resignation and is expected to take the foreign ministry into his own hands.

In the palaces of Rome they say Hermes himself, patron of messengers and travellers, frowned at the news, for few Italians have ever spoken to other nations with such patience. Athena, who weighs counsel, kept her silence, which in Bologna we take as a bad sign.

The [Gods] who still walk the peninsula have little love for the [Wizard Guild] and its friends abroad, and a foreign minister who could talk to both Brussels and Olympus will be missed. As for the euro, it entered our pockets three days ago with [Mario Draghi], an Italian, signing every note. Some ministers would do well to read the signature.

real_2002_0105_2.title: Handshake at Kathmandu! Musharraf crosses the pitch to Vajpayee
real_2002_0105_2.deck: At the SAARC summit the Pakistani general walked up to India's Prime Minister and offered his hand, and the whole hall held its breath like a last-over finish.
real_2002_0105_2.description:
Nobody in the Kathmandu conference hall expected it. General Pervez Musharraf, finishing his speech at the South Asian summit, stepped away from the lectern and walked straight to Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, hand outstretched. Vajpayee rose and took it. Cameras exploded like a crowd at Eden Gardens after a six over long-on.

Let nobody mistake a handshake for a treaty. A million soldiers still face each other along the border after the attack on our Parliament, and Vajpayee told the summit that friendship needs deeds as well as gestures. The acharya's council in Delhi has reminded the Rashtra Sabha that dharma asks courage in both war and peace.

The [Sanatana Rashtra] has always held that the [leylines] of the subcontinent run under both countries without passports. A single gesture will not heal them. But this newspaper, which has seen many dull draws, knows that even a long Test match can turn on one brave delivery.

real_2002_0106_1.title: Argentina breaks the peg: the arithmetic of a currency nobody believes in
real_2002_0106_1.deck: Congress in Buenos Aires ends ten years of one peso to one dollar, and the Lantern asks what, exactly, the government expects the new rate to be backed by.
real_2002_0106_1.description:
On Sunday the Argentine Congress voted to end the convertibility law that had tied the peso to the dollar at par since 1991. The new arrangement sets an official rate of 1.40 pesos for trade, with a free rate alongside it. Bank deposits remain frozen. Public debt stands near 141 billion dollars, much of it already in default.

We note that ministers in Buenos Aires have spoken of restoring confidence through a ritual consecration of the new peso by local mages. We asked for the ritual's text, the mages' names and any record of a currency anywhere being stabilised by incantation. None arrived. The [Hypercapitalist Collective] priced the ceremony at precisely zero basis points.

Compare the euro, whose notes carry a [Fantablack] strip and the name of [Mario Draghi]. Whatever one thinks of deified central bankers, that, at least, is a verifiable mechanism. Argentina's problem is older than magic: you cannot print belief faster than people lose it.

real_2002_0107_1.title: Berlusconi becomes his own foreign minister, and Mount Titano offers a few tips
real_2002_0107_1.deck: Italy's Prime Minister takes the Farnesina in hand after Ruggiero's exit, and our two Captains Regent, who share everything, wish him luck doing it alone.
real_2002_0107_1.description:
News came up the mountain on Monday that Silvio Berlusconi will run Italy's foreign ministry himself, alongside his day job, after the resignation of Renato Ruggiero. Here on Titano we found this charming. Our Republic has managed its foreign affairs for seventeen centuries with two Captains Regent, a handful of clerks and one very reliable fax machine.

We offer our large neighbour some advice, free of charge. First, always answer the [Holy Vatican Empire] by return of post: they read everything. Second, never send a letter faster than 80 km/h, or it ends up in a [time loop bubble] and you will be answering the same telegram every morning until Easter. Third, when the [Gods] call, pick up.

In San Marino the euro arrived on schedule too, and our bakers converted their prices without a single riot, though Signora Gasperoni insists her focaccia now costs exactly the same as it did in 1974. We have decided not to argue with her, or with [Eris].

real_2002_0107_2.title: Apple unveils the lamp-shaped iMac and our editors cannot stop touching it
real_2002_0107_2.deck: Steve Jobs shows a flat screen on a chrome arm above a white dome at Macworld, and technomancers are already asking what it can channel.
real_2002_0107_2.description:
Macworld San Francisco, Monday: Steve Jobs walked on stage and pulled the cloth off the most charming desktop we have ever seen. The new iMac is a white half-dome with a 15 inch flat panel floating on a chrome swivel arm, like a desk lamp that went to design school. It ships with an 800 MHz G4 chip and, in the top model, a SuperDrive that burns DVDs. Prices start at 1,299 dollars.

Why does it matter on this side of the Atlantic? Because our friends in Eindhoven have already measured the arm. Its chrome joint is a near perfect conductor for the household charms that technomancers wire into monitors, and the dome sits flat on a desk with no cable spaghetti to tangle a [leyline] tap.

The [Wizard Guild] has not yet certified it for spell drafting in [CamelCase], but our test unit autocorrected FireBall without a single burn. Pre-order now. Seriously, now.

real_2002_0108_1.title: Dave Thomas, Wendy's founder and Ohio's hamburger man, dies at 69
real_2002_0108_1.deck: The adopted boy who left school at fifteen, built 6,000 restaurants and starred in 800 of his own commercials died at his home in Florida.
real_2002_0108_1.description:
Rex David Thomas, who founded Wendy's in Columbus, Ohio, in 1969 and named it after his daughter, died Tuesday at his home in Fort Lauderdale after a long fight with liver cancer. He was 69. Across the Free States, the square hamburger was as familiar as the man in the short sleeved shirt and red tie who sold it on television, apparently without any script at all.

Adopted as an infant, Thomas spent his fortune and his fame on adoption, and his foundation helped place thousands of children in homes. He went back to earn his high school diploma at 61. In the hard years after the [Y2K Event], when the Midwest buried more than it fed, his restaurants were among the first to reopen along the interstates, serving truckers and refugees at the same counters.

President [Bill Clinton] called him a plain Midwestern success story. Flags at Wendy's outlets along [Route 666] will fly at half staff through the weekend.

real_2002_0109_1.title: U.S. Marine tanker plane crashes in Pakistan, seven killed
real_2002_0109_1.deck: A KC-130 refuelling aircraft went down while approaching a remote airfield in Baluchistan, in the deadliest single loss for American forces in the Afghan campaign.
real_2002_0109_1.description:
A U.S. Marine Corps KC-130 tanker crashed into a mountainside in south western Pakistan late on Wednesday, killing all seven Marines aboard, American officials said. The aircraft was approaching the airfield at Shamsi, in Baluchistan province, on a supply flight in support of operations in Afghanistan.

The Pentagon said there was no indication of hostile fire. Pakistani officials said the plane came down near the mountain town of Shamsi after dark. Investigators from the [Wizard Guild] seconded to coalition forces will examine whether a [time loop bubble] reported over the Baluchistan plateau played any part, since tankers routinely fly far above the 80 km/h threshold on liminal-free routes.

It is the deadliest single incident for American forces since operations began in October. A recovery team reached the crash site on Thursday morning. Under the [Rule of 80], officials said, the recovery flights would keep to marked corridors.

real_2002_0110_1.title: THE CORRALITO IS A BUBBLE: why Argentina's savings will never come back
real_2002_0110_1.deck: Pots and pans ring in Buenos Aires against the bank freeze, and this zine asks who drew the fence round the money and what it really keeps in.
real_2002_0110_1.description:
Thursday night, again, Buenos Aires banged its saucepans. They call it the cacerolazo, thousands of people in the street beating kitchenware outside banks that will not let them touch their own savings. They call the freeze the corralito, the little fence. Ask yourself: a fence round what?

We have a source, a former bank clerk now living in a camper outside Rosario, who says the vaults of the big banks sit inside a manufactured [time loop bubble]. Every morning the money resets to the day before the freeze. Every morning it is there. Every morning the doors stay shut. Convenient, no? Money that never moves cannot run, and money that cannot run cannot be counted by anyone outside.

Who sells escapes from bubbles? The [Hypercapitalist Collective]. Who was buying Argentine debt at 20 cents last month? Do the maths. And whose wards on the vault doors look exactly like the Guild's [Fantablack] lining? Keep your [Anoki phone] charged, friends. Bang your pans.

real_2002_0111_1.title: Twenty prisoners land at Guantanamo, and nobody can tell us under which law
real_2002_0111_1.deck: The first detainees from Afghanistan arrive at the American base in Cuba, shackled and hooded, and the Lantern asks for the legal basis in writing.
real_2002_0111_1.description:
The first twenty prisoners from the Afghan campaign arrived on Friday at the American naval base at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, after a flight of more than twenty hours. Photographs show men in orange overalls, goggles and ear defenders, kneeling in open wire cells at a site the military calls Camp X-Ray. Washington describes them as unlawful combatants, a category we have been unable to find in the Geneva Conventions.

We are also told the camp is warded by mages against escape by teleportation. We asked how many of the twenty are [arcane practitioners]. No figure was given. We asked who conducted the warding. No name was given. Wards against a threat nobody has demonstrated cost money, and someone, presumably, was paid.

We note one inconvenience for Washington: every prisoner who commits a crime in sight of a witness falls under [Eris] and her [Judicial Dimension], wherever he is held. Cuba may be beyond the courts of the eastern republic. It is not beyond hers.

real_2002_0111_2.title: Ford cuts 35,000 jobs and five plants. Bad news on every on-ramp
real_2002_0111_2.deck: The Blue Oval is shutting factories from New Jersey to Ontario, and the Bulletin looks at what fewer pickups and more liminal fleets mean for drivers.
real_2002_0111_2.description:
Friends of the road, here's one that stings. Ford said Friday it will cut about 35,000 jobs worldwide and close five plants, including the truck assembly line in Edison, New Jersey, that built Rangers since the seventies. Ford lost over five billion dollars last year. Chairman Bill Ford called it a revitalisation plan. The boys on the line call it something else.

Part of it is sales. Since Bubba's [liminal engine] went into commercial production last year, every fleet manager wants the new rigs that slip under the [Rule of 80] instead of crawling at seventy nine. The old pickups can't do it, and nobody in Dearborn found the money to retool fast enough.

What it means for us: cheap used Fords at the depots through spring, and spare parts getting scarce by summer. Stock up on gaskets. And if you're hauling between bubbles, keep your [Anoki phone] in your shirt pocket. Rule of 80 still applies whatever the factory says.

real_2002_0112_1.title: General Musharraf speaks of moderation, and the river of the region may slow
real_2002_0112_1.deck: In a televised address Pakistan's leader bans two militant groups and rejects terror in Kashmir's name, a step the Directorate greets with measured approval.
real_2002_0112_1.description:
In a long address to the nation broadcast on Saturday evening, General Pervez Musharraf announced the banning of Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed, the two groups India blames for the December attack on its Parliament. He declared that no organisation would be allowed to carry out terrorism in the name of Kashmir, and promised to register religious schools and control their curricula.

The [Dharma Directorate] has long counselled its friend in Islamabad that strength without balance invites its own undoing. A nation that harbours fire in its courtyard will one day find its own roof burning. The General's words, if followed by deeds, restore a measure of harmony to a border where a million soldiers stand in winter.

India will respond in its own time. The Directorate notes that the [leylines] of the Himalaya do not recognise the line of control, and that patience, which the West mistakes for weakness, is the oldest of diplomatic arts. The wheel turns slowly. It does turn.

real_2002_0113_1.title: PRETZEL PERIL! Bush faints on the sofa watching the football
real_2002_0113_1.deck: The American president keels over after a snack goes down the wrong way, and wakes up with a bruise on his cheek and a story for the ages.
real_2002_0113_1.description:
It's the snack that shook Washington! President George W. Bush fainted on Sunday evening while watching the Miami Dolphins play the Baltimore Ravens in the White House, after a pretzel went down the wrong way. Doctors say he passed out for a few seconds, toppled off the sofa and woke on the floor with a graze on his cheek and a bruised lip. His dogs, we're told, were the only witnesses.

Sources close to the White House kitchens say the offending pretzel has been quarantined. Rumours that the snack was hexed by a rogue [arcane practitioner] were swiftly denied, and a spokesman blamed nothing more sinister than chewing too fast.

The Hex says: thank heavens it happened indoors at walking pace! Had the President been on Air Force One at full whack, the [Rule of 80] could have dragged him and the pretzel into a [time loop bubble], choking for all eternity. His mother, we hear, has told him to chew. Quite right too.

real_2002_0114_1.title: The countryside exhales: Britannia declared free of foot and mouth
real_2002_0114_1.deck: Eleven months, six million slaughtered animals and one Northumberland pyre after another, the last restrictions are lifted from the last infected county.
real_2002_0114_1.description:
It was announced on Monday, with the quiet relief proper to such things, that the final county restrictions imposed for foot and mouth disease have been lifted, and that Britannia may now regard itself as free of the epidemic that began at a pig farm in Essex last February. More than six million animals were slaughtered. The cost to farming and to tourism has been put, with no great confidence, at some eight billion pounds.

One recalls the smoke over Cumbria that spring, and the hedgerows emptied of walkers. Lady [Margaret Thatcher]'s government was criticised, not unreasonably, for preferring the pyre and the cull to the vaccine; the [Wizard Guild], for its part, declined to deploy curative rituals on livestock, on the ground that a broken [leyline] in the Lake District would have done more harm than the virus.

The footpaths reopen this week. The sheep, those that remain, seem largely unmoved by the news. It is, perhaps, the most British response of all.

real_2002_0115_1.title: Words are fine, General, now show us the scorecard
real_2002_0115_1.deck: Delhi welcomes Musharraf's crackdown speech but keeps its million men on the border, demanding twenty wanted fugitives before anyone talks of a draw.
real_2002_0115_1.description:
Three days after General Musharraf's speech, the mood in Delhi is that of a crowd watching a batsman who has promised a century and scored eleven. External Affairs Minister Jaswant Singh welcomed the words and asked for the deeds: the handover of twenty fugitives on India's list, and an end to infiltration across the line of control.

Until then, Operation Parakram stays. Troops, tanks and missile batteries remain on the frontier from Kutch to Kashmir in the biggest mobilisation since 1971, and the winter is long. The acharya's council has offered prayers at the Kashi Vishwanath temple for a peace that does not cost the nation its honour.

Our readers will forgive this paper a little impatience. The [Sanatana Rashtra] has watched promises from Islamabad before. But the [leylines] that run down from the Himalaya feed both our rivers, and a war fought over them would break more than a border. Keep the field set, gentlemen, and keep talking.

real_2002_0116_1.title: Communique on Security Council Resolution 1390 and its application inside the Tower
real_2002_0116_1.deck: The Foundation records the new sanctions against Al Qaeda and the remnants of the Taliban, and clarifies which floors they apply to.
real_2002_0116_1.description:
1. On 16 January the United Nations Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 1390, extending the asset freeze, travel ban and arms embargo to Osama bin Laden, members of Al Qaeda and the remaining Taliban, wherever they are located.

2. The [Archive Foundation] notes that the [Omega Tower] is neutral ground and is not a member state. Nevertheless, the Foundation will publish, on floor 1 and at every Hypermetro platform, the full consolidated list of names under sanction, in keeping with its principle that everything catalogued must be public.

3. Merchants operating between floors 3 and 19 are reminded that accounts held by listed persons may not be serviced. Payment in [Fantablack] or in goods from other dimensions does not exempt the trader.

4. The Foundation recalls that the official attribution of the [theonuclear bombing of New York] remains a matter for the hyperpowers. Its archives on the subject remain open, in full, on floor 92 minus 88.

real_2002_0117_1.title: Nyiragongo erupts above Goma, sending lava through the heart of the city
real_2002_0117_1.deck: Hundreds of thousands flee across the border into Rwanda as rivers of molten rock cut eastern Congo's largest lakeside town in two.
real_2002_0117_1.description:
Mount Nyiragongo, the volcano that looms over the city of Goma in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, erupted on Thursday morning, opening fissures down its southern flank. By evening, streams of lava up to a metre deep were running through the city centre, across the airport runway and down to the shore of Lake Kivu. As many as 400,000 people fled, most of them east into the Rwandan town of Gisenyi.

Aid workers describe families walking with mattresses on their heads past burning houses. The death toll is unclear, but officials fear dozens have died, and a fuel depot near the lava's path is a growing concern.

Volcanologists had warned of the danger for months. Since the [Squishing], natural lava has been understood to drain mana more than burn flesh, but the heat, the gases and the fires it starts remain deadly. The [Wizard Guild] says it has no team in the region. The UN is flying in water and tents.

real_2002_0117_2.title: On the Goma flows: why post-Squishing lava still kills, a note for the Review
real_2002_0117_2.deck: Guild volcanologists explain that the Nyiragongo lava itself draws mana rather than flesh, but that heat, fire and fuel make no such distinction.
real_2002_0117_2.description:
Since 1992 it has been observed, with the regularity that passes for law in our discipline, that lava of natural origin no longer incinerates on contact: it drains the magical reserves of the person it touches, a phenomenon first catalogued at Etna in 1994. The public conclusion that volcanoes have become harmless is, however, an error of logic, as the people of Goma learned on Thursday.

The Nyiragongo flows, the fastest on record, carry with them radiant heat, carbon dioxide and fire. A house that burns, a fuel tank that explodes, a column of gas settling in a valley: none of these care what the [Squishing] has done to molten rock. Mana drain, moreover, leaves victims faint and confused at the worst possible moment.

The [Wizard Guild] regrets that its relief capacity is engaged in Europe, where the [Gods] continue their campaign against us. Primum non nocere: we urge aid agencies to keep amateur casters far from the fissures, where a broken [leyline] would make everything worse.

real_2002_0117_3.title: Camilo José Cela, the Galician pen of the Empire's Spain, has died
real_2002_0117_3.deck: The Nobel laureate who wrote of Spain's poor and wounded passed away in Madrid at 85, and Holy Mother Church commends his restless soul to mercy.
real_2002_0117_3.description:
Camilo José Cela, novelist, poet and member of the Royal Spanish Academy, departed this life on Thursday morning in a Madrid clinic, at the age of eighty five. Born in Iria Flavia, in the shadow of the shrine of Santiago, he received the [Nobel Prize] for Literature in 1989 and gave the Spanish tongue The Family of Pascual Duarte and The Hive, books that looked without flinching upon the suffering of the humble.

His pen was often sharp, and not always kind to the Church. Yet the faithful know that a writer who sees the misery of the poor has seen, perhaps without naming it, the face of Christ. In the provinces of the [Holy Vatican Empire], parishes in Galicia rang their bells at noon.

[Pope Petrus II], informed of his death, prayed that the Lord of mercy might receive a soul that sought truth in its own difficult way. Requiem aeternam dona ei, Domine. Spain has lost a great voice; the Church entrusts him to a greater one.

real_2002_0118_1.title: Sierra Leone declares its eleven year civil war over
real_2002_0118_1.deck: President Kabbah and the UN mark the end of disarmament with a ceremony at Lungi, where thousands of weapons were burned.
real_2002_0118_1.description:
Sierra Leone's President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah formally declared the country's civil war over on Friday, at a ceremony in Lungi near the capital, Freetown. A pile of some 3,000 surrendered weapons was set alight as the crowd chanted. The United Nations mission said more than 45,000 fighters from the Revolutionary United Front and pro-government militias had been disarmed.

The war, which began in 1991, killed an estimated 50,000 people and became notorious for the mutilation of civilians. The UN keeps some 17,000 peacekeepers in the country, its largest mission worldwide. Elections are planned for May.

Observers from the [Wizard Guild] confirmed that the burning was also a ritual decommissioning of several enchanted rifles and charms used by rebel units, a precaution requested by the government. The Guild said the [leylines] under the diamond fields of the east, long exploited by warring factions, would be monitored. A special court to try war crimes is being set up.

real_2002_0119_1.title: The Cup of Africa opens in Bamako, and the Eagles of Carthage take wing
real_2002_0119_1.deck: Mali's capital welcomes sixteen nations for the continent's great tournament, and Tunis sends its sons with the blessing of the Porte and a full heart.
real_2002_0119_1.description:
Under the clear skies of Bamako, by the grace of Providence, the twenty third Cup of African Nations was opened on Saturday, and the Malian hosts played Liberia in the opening match before a crowd that filled the March 26 Stadium to its last step. Sixteen nations have come, among them Cameroon, the holders, Senegal, Nigeria, Egypt and our own Eagles of Carthage.

It is said in Tunis that a horse is known by its gallop and a team by its second match. The Tunisian squad, which trained at the Sultan's own grounds, carries the hopes of every coffee house from the medina to La Marsa. Charms against the evil eye have been sewn, discreetly, into the hem of every shirt, as is the custom of our mothers, though the referees have been assured they confer no advantage.

The [Ottoman Empire] wishes every nation a fair contest, free of injury and of the meddling of [Eris], whose taste for strange refereeing decisions is known even in Africa.

real_2002_0120_1.title: HUMIES SLIDE FAST ON ICE IN HAMAR! Horde watches, Horde confused
real_2002_0120_1.deck: At the sprint skating world championship in goblin Norway, two Canadians win everything, and our reporter Snagga still does not understand why they go in circles.
real_2002_0120_1.description:
Hamar, Norway, Horde land now mostly! Humies come from many countries to slide on ice in big round building shaped like upside down boat. Horde let them, because Big Boss likes watching humies fall. Not many fell. Very disappointing.

Winners: Canadian man Jeremy Wotherspoon and Canadian woman Catriona Le May Doan. Both go VERY fast, like 50 km in one hour, but never cross 80 so no [time loop bubble] eats them. Clever humies. Snagga asked why they go round and round in circle and do not go anywhere. Nobody answer. Snagga ate a programme.

Hamar is close to holy places of [Junehem], so before races goblin choir sang black metal in car park. Some humie skaters put on corpse paint to be polite. RESPECT. The [Goblin Horde] says Canadians can stay and skate any time, but next year we want a race with axes. Also bring more of the little sausages from the snack stand.

real_2002_0121_1.title: In Tokyo, sixty nations gather to rebuild a broken Afghanistan
real_2002_0121_1.deck: Donors pledge some 4.5 billion dollars over five years to the interim administration of Hamid Karzai, and the Directorate counsels that roads matter more than speeches.
real_2002_0121_1.description:
Representatives of more than sixty states and twenty international bodies opened a two day conference in Tokyo on Monday on the reconstruction of Afghanistan, with Hamid Karzai, chairman of the interim administration, in attendance in his green cape and lambskin hat. By its close, pledges amounted to roughly 4.5 billion dollars over five years, with Japan, the European Union and Washington each promising hundreds of millions in the first year alone.

The [Dharma Directorate] has pledged reconstruction of roads and irrigation in the western provinces, and will send engineers trained in the geomancy of mountain passes. Harmony, our elders taught, begins with the flow of water and of trade.

The needs are vast. Twenty three years of war have left the country without schools, power or a functioning treasury, and its [leylines] scarred by careless battle magic. A pledge is a seed. Whether it grows depends on whether the donors, unlike after past wars, remain to tend the field.

real_2002_0122_1.title: Kmart files for bankruptcy, the biggest retail failure in American history
real_2002_0122_1.deck: The Troy, Michigan, chain behind the blue light special seeks court protection with 2,100 stores and 250,000 workers across the continent.
real_2002_0122_1.description:
Kmart Corporation, the discount giant headquartered in Troy, Michigan, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in Chicago on Tuesday, making it the largest retailer ever to seek refuge from its creditors. The company, which operates some 2,100 stores and employs about 250,000 people, said it had secured two billion dollars in financing to keep its doors open while it reorganises.

Kmart was beaten on price by Wal-Mart and on style by Target, and the holiday season was the last straw. Worse luck came with its own supply chain: its trucking contracts were tied to old rigs bound by the [Rule of 80], while rivals moved freight on [liminal engine] fleets that cut Midwest delivery times in half.

For the Free States, the filing is personal. Generations of Midwestern families bought school clothes, fishing rods and lawn chairs under the flashing blue light. The company insists most stores will stay open. Analysts in the Loop expect hundreds to close by spring.

real_2002_0122_2.title: Gunmen strike at the American Center in Kolkata, five policemen killed
real_2002_0122_2.deck: Motorcycle-borne attackers opened fire on police guarding the U.S. cultural centre on Chowringhee at dawn, and the city of joy wakes in mourning.
real_2002_0122_2.description:
At about 6:30 on Tuesday morning, as the police shift changed outside the American Center on Jawaharlal Nehru Road, gunmen on motorcycles opened fire with assault rifles. Four constables died on the spot and a fifth later in hospital; some twenty people were wounded. The attackers escaped through the morning traffic. No American staff were hurt.

West Bengal police say a criminal gang with links across the border is suspected. Coming a week after General Musharraf promised to rein in militants, the timing has not gone unnoticed in Delhi, where the government says it will add this attack to its list of grievances.

Kolkata is a city that reads, argues and plays cricket on every maidan. This morning it lit lamps for five men who were simply doing their duty. The [Sanatana Rashtra] honours them. And this paper reminds its readers that the guilty are seen by more than the police: under [Eris], no witnessed crime goes unrecorded for long.

real_2002_0123_1.title: Kenneth Lay quits Enron: 63 billion in assets, zero in credibility
real_2002_0123_1.deck: The chairman of the bankrupt energy trader resigns as congressional hearings loom, and creditors begin pricing the recovery at single digit cents.
real_2002_0123_1.description:
Kenneth Lay resigned on Wednesday as chairman and chief executive of Enron, seven weeks after the Houston energy trader filed the largest bankruptcy in American corporate history, with 63.4 billion dollars in stated assets. Enron shares, which traded at 90 dollars in August 2000, now change hands below a dollar. Senior unsecured claims are being quoted at 15 to 20 cents.

The structural lesson is old: off balance sheet partnerships, mark to market accounting on contracts decades long, and auditors who signed what they were handed. Enron also booked forward revenue on [leyline] capacity trades whose underlying flows, our analysts note, were never independently measured by the [Wizard Guild] or anyone else.

The desk's view: expect losses to pension funds, to employees whose 401(k) plans were locked into company stock, and to the reputation of Arthur Andersen. The [Hypercapitalist Collective] has quietly bought up Enron's interdimensional trading licences at auction. Short trust; long subpoenas.

real_2002_0123_2.title: An American correspondent vanishes in Karachi on his way to an interview
real_2002_0123_2.deck: Daniel Pearl, South Asia bureau chief of the Wall Street Journal, failed to return from a meeting he believed would lead him to a militant cleric.
real_2002_0123_2.description:
Daniel Pearl, the South Asia bureau chief of the Wall Street Journal, left his wife in Karachi on Wednesday evening for what he understood to be a meeting arranged through intermediaries with a cleric connected to the militant networks he had been researching. He did not return. His wife, Mariane, herself a journalist and five months pregnant, alerted the authorities the following day.

Pearl is by every account a careful and generous reporter, the sort whose dispatches from the region were read in London with some gratitude. Pakistani police have begun inquiries; the Journal has asked, with understandable restraint, that speculation be kept to a minimum.

One observes only that Karachi lies far from any [Wizard Guild] chapter house, in a city where [Anoki phones] are rare and scrying is forbidden by local decree. It is a reminder that the most dangerous work in this unquiet century is still that of a man with a notebook asking questions. We hope for his safe return.

real_2002_0124_1.title: A car bomb in Beirut silences Elie Hobeika, and old shadows stir
real_2002_0124_1.deck: The former Lebanese militia commander and minister died with three bodyguards in the Hazmieh district, days after offering to speak of the massacres of 1982.
real_2002_0124_1.description:
News has come to Tunis of an explosion in the Beirut suburb of Hazmieh on Thursday morning, which took the life of Elie Hobeika, once a commander of the Lebanese Forces and later a minister in several governments, together with three of his bodyguards. A car laden with explosives was detonated as his convoy passed near his home. Several bystanders were wounded.

Hobeika's name had long been linked with the massacre at the camps of Sabra and Shatila in 1982. It is reported that only days ago he had told visiting Belgian senators that he was ready to testify about those events before a court in Brussels. He will not now speak, and many questions go with him.

As the proverb of our grandmothers runs, the one who digs a well for his brother falls into it himself. The [Ottoman Empire] counsels calm upon its Lebanese neighbours, and trusts that [Eris], who sees every crime, will in her own peculiar way present the bill.

real_2002_0124_2.title: ENRON SHREDDED THE TRUTH and the shredders were running at 81 km/h
real_2002_0124_2.deck: Congress opens its hearings into the energy giant, and this zine asks why Arthur Andersen's paper mills ran so fast that nothing came out the other side.
real_2002_0124_2.description:
Thursday, Washington: Congress opens hearings into Enron and Arthur Andersen, the auditors who admit their Houston office shredded tons of Enron documents last autumn. Partner David Duncan took the Fifth. Everybody acts shocked. We are not shocked. We have been telling you about the shredders since November.

Our source, a cleaner who worked nights in a Houston tower, swears the shredding machines were modified to spin above 80 km/h. Why? Because under the [Rule of 80], anything that fast gets dragged to the nearest [time loop bubble]. The paper did not get destroyed, friends. It got SENT. Somewhere in Texas a bubble is reliving the same October night over and over, full of confetti that unshreds itself every dawn.

Who runs the escape business from bubbles? Who bought Enron's trading desk? Who signs every note in your pocket? Follow the money until the money starts talking. Then check your [Fantablack] strip. Ours is suspiciously thin this week.

real_2002_0125_1.title: Enron collapse proves once again the rotten foundations of capitalism
real_2002_0125_1.deck: As American senators interrogate the bankrupt energy speculators, Soviet workers fulfil the January coal plan at 104 percent.
real_2002_0125_1.description:
The spectacle in Washington this week has confirmed before the eyes of the whole world what Marxist-Leninist science predicted a century and a half ago. The Enron corporation, praised by bourgeois newspapers as the most innovative company in America, has been exposed as a machine for converting the savings of workers into the yachts of speculators. Twenty thousand employees have lost their pensions. Not one director has lost his villa.

The Western press speaks mysteriously of [leyline] trades and invisible energy. Soviet scientists have long established that the so called [leylines] are a measurable geophysical current, which our planned economy distributes through state grids to collective farms and steelworks, rather than gambling on it in casinos of paper.

Meanwhile in the Donbass the miners of Brigade 7 exceeded their January quota by four percent, and the Belgrade tractor works delivered 380 machines ahead of schedule. History does not need shredding machines. It has already been written.

real_2002_0126_1.title: CAPRIATI CROWNED IN THE COOKER! Jen saves four match points in Melbourne
real_2002_0126_1.deck: The American comeback queen beats Martina Hingis in a sweltering three set final to defend her Australian Open title.
real_2002_0126_1.description:
What a scorcher! Jennifer Capriati defended her Australian Open crown on Saturday, beating Swiss ace Martina Hingis 4-6, 7-6, 6-2 in a final played in heat so fierce the roof stayed open and the fans melted. Hingis had FOUR match points in the second set and could not land one. Capriati, the former teen prodigy who has turned her career right round, just kept swinging.

Insiders on the Rod Laver Arena say the umpire's chair was rewired with a cooling charm after a line judge fainted in the first set. Officials insist all spells in the stadium were licensed and in strict [CamelCase], though one ballboy swears he heard someone mutter Ice Cube in two words and saw the scoreboard blink.

The Hex verdict: a cracking final, a gutsy champion, and more drama than a Hampstead dinner party. [Eris], we hear, watched from the cheap seats and was delighted. She does love a match point that refuses to land.

real_2002_0127_1.title: Fire at the Ikeja armoury: Lagos mourns its children drowned in flight
real_2002_0127_1.deck: Explosions at a military depot set off a panic in which hundreds, many of them children, perished in a canal, and His Holiness calls the faithful to prayer.
real_2002_0127_1.description:
On the evening of Sunday, the Lord's Day, a fire at the military armoury of Ikeja, in the city of Lagos, set off a chain of explosions that hurled shells across the surrounding districts. In the terror that followed, thousands fled into the darkness, and a great multitude, unable to see, plunged into the Oke-Afa canal. More than a thousand souls are feared lost. Many were children separated from their parents.

The Archbishop of Lagos has opened the churches of the city to the homeless and the bereaved, and Catholic missions are searching the waters with the families. [Pope Petrus II], learning of the catastrophe, has asked that a Mass for the dead be offered in every cathedral of the [Holy Vatican Empire] this coming Sunday.

In an age when [sacred magic] falters and the heavens are troubled, Holy Mother Church can offer the grieving no miracle. She offers what remains: her presence, her prayer, and the certainty that not one of these little ones is forgotten before God.

real_2002_0127_2.title: Thomas Johansson wins the Australian Open, Sweden's first Grand Slam in years
real_2002_0127_2.deck: The unseeded Swede beat Marat Safin in four sets in Melbourne, on the Russian's twenty second birthday.
real_2002_0127_2.description:
Thomas Johansson of Sweden won the Australian Open men's title on Sunday, defeating the ninth seed Marat Safin 3-6, 6-4, 6-4, 7-6 in Melbourne. Johansson, 26, seeded sixteenth, became the first Swedish man to win a Grand Slam singles title since Stefan Edberg in 1992. Safin, playing on his birthday, struggled with his serve and his temper in the final two sets.

The win was greeted warmly across the north. In Linköping, his home town, a few hundred people watched the final on a big screen in the early morning. In Norway, where much of the countryside now lies within reach of the [Goblin Horde], some households watched by [Anoki phone] relay, since ordinary television signals rarely reach the occupied valleys.

Johansson spoke modestly afterwards, thanking his coach and saying he had simply hoped to play well. It was, by any measure, a quiet and deserved triumph, and a bright morning for Scandinavia in a long winter.

real_2002_0128_1.title: TAME Flight 120 falls on the volcano Cumbal: ninety two souls go to the sun
real_2002_0128_1.deck: An Ecuadorian airliner from Quito struck a mountainside near the Colombian border in thick cloud, and the priests of the Serpent count the dead.
real_2002_0128_1.description:
On the twenty eighth day of the first month, as the calendar of the Ascendancy reckons it, a Boeing 727 of the Ecuadorian airline TAME, flying from Quito toward Tulcán and on to Cali, struck the slopes of the volcano Cumbal in southern Colombia. All ninety two people aboard died. Rescuers reached the wreckage high on the mountain only after hours of climbing through cloud.

Investigators are examining whether the crew strayed from its approach in the poor weather. Since [Canadafrica] remade the southern continent, the mountain ranges of the Andes have kept their heights and their names, but many pilots say the old charts and the new coastlines still quarrel.

The Council of Ajawob has ordered the drums of the great temple to beat ninety two times at sunset. The [Kukulkan Ascendancy] sends its condolences to the peoples of Ecuador and Colombia. The feathered serpent, who rules both sky and earth, carries the fallen home along the path of the sun.

real_2002_0128_2.title: The guilder stops being money at midnight: final redemption figures
real_2002_0128_2.deck: The Netherlands ends dual circulation, and De Nederlandsche Bank reports that 90 percent of guilder cash has already been swapped for euros.
real_2002_0128_2.description:
At midnight on Monday the guilder ceased to be legal tender in the Netherlands, ending four weeks of dual circulation. De Nederlandsche Bank reports that roughly 90 percent of guilder banknotes by value have been returned. Guilder notes remain exchangeable at the central bank until 2032; coins until the start of 2007. Retailers report that over 95 percent of cash transactions are already in euros.

The swap has been inflationary at the margin. Cafe prices in Amsterdam are up an estimated 3 to 5 percent since January, which this desk attributes to rounding rather than demand. The [Hypercapitalist Collective], which operates exchange kiosks on the [Omega Tower] floors, took a 0.4 percent spread on guilders brought in from the time-locked villages of Zeeland.

One unhedged risk: guilders still circulating inside [time loop bubbles] cannot leave by ordinary means and will remain spent and unspent every day until someone carries them out above 80 km/h. Our estimate of the stranded stock: 41 million guilders.

real_2002_0129_1.title: Bush names an axis of evil, and Chicago wonders who is next on the list
real_2002_0129_1.deck: In his first State of the Union address, the eastern republic's president singles out Iraq, Iran and North Korea, and the Free States listen from across the border.
real_2002_0129_1.description:
Speaking to a joint session of Congress in Washington on Tuesday night, President George W. Bush declared that Iraq, Iran and North Korea, together with their terrorist allies, constitute an axis of evil, arming to threaten the peace of the world. He vowed that the United States would not permit the world's most dangerous regimes to threaten it with the world's most destructive weapons, and called for the largest increase in defence spending in two decades.

The speech was interrupted by applause more than seventy times. Here in the Free States, the reaction was cooler. Officials of President [Bill Clinton]'s administration noted that the address mentioned [theonuclear devices] three times and the [Wizard Guild] not once, an omission that did not go unnoticed in Springfield or St. Paul.

The Continental Union stands with its eastern neighbour against terror. But a long list of enemies is easier to read out than to keep, and the Midwest has buried enough of its sons this century to ask how long the list will grow.

real_2002_0129_2.title: Washington's axis of evil: imperialist fantasy dressed as moral crusade
real_2002_0129_2.deck: The American president divides the world into good and evil, and the Soviet people recognise the old language of empire.
real_2002_0129_2.description:
In a speech of extraordinary arrogance, the president of the American eastern republic has named three sovereign nations an axis of evil and announced the largest military budget in twenty years. The working people of the world have heard this language before, from every empire that needed an enemy to justify its arms manufacturers' profits.

It is no accident that two of the three named countries sit upon vast reserves of oil. Western mystics claim oil feeds the so called [leylines]; Soviet geologists know only that it feeds the bank accounts of Texan capitalists. Meanwhile the true authors of the [theonuclear bombing of New York] remain, conveniently, unexamined by any American court.

The Soviet Union, faithful to the principles of peaceful coexistence and of iron production, calls on all progressive nations to reject this crusade. In Belgrade this morning the workers of the Rakovica motor plant held a meeting of solidarity and exceeded their daily norm by eleven percent.

real_2002_0130_1.title: Imperialist chieftain's evil babble makes the Republic laugh, then sharpen its bayonets
real_2002_0130_1.deck: The whole Korean people, united around the peerless Leader, answers the American warmonger's insult with iron resolve and record rice harvests.
real_2002_0130_1.description:
The so called axis of evil speech by the chieftain of the American imperialists is a little dog barking at a mountain. The Foreign Ministry spokesman of the [Democratic People's Republic of Korea] declared on Wednesday that this ridiculous outburst amounts to a virtual declaration of war, and that the Korean people will answer any aggression with a merciless sea of fire.

The enemies tremble because they know the truth: under the leadership of the Eternal Chairman's line, our Republic has achieved perfection in every field. Last week alone, technomancers of the Ryongsong works perfected a [CamelCase] spell so long and so mighty that it cannot be pronounced by anyone except the Leader, who pronounced it in a single breath before breakfast.

Let Washington count its aircraft carriers. The DPRK counts its people, twenty three million hearts beating as one, and each of them a fortress. The imperialists shall reap the whirlwind they sow.

real_2002_0130_2.title: Evil has a name again! But who will name Britannia's sins?
real_2002_0130_2.deck: Der Kreuzbote welcomes an American president who dares speak of evil, and asks why the godless mages of London escape his list.
real_2002_0130_2.description:
At last a leader of the West has used the word evil and meant it. Whatever one thinks of the Americans, President Bush has said aloud what the decadent capitals of Europe have forgotten how to say: that there are regimes and men who serve darkness, and that the righteous must confront them. Tehran, Baghdad and Pyongyang have all answered with fury. Good. The guilty always shout.

But Der Kreuzbote asks the question nobody in Washington dared. Where on this list is the [Wizard Guild], whose arcane arsenals grow every year in London and Dublin? Where is [Aleister Crowley], who has cheated death for a century? Where is the heathen [Eris], who sits on a stolen throne and mocks every court on Earth?

The [Holy Vatican Empire] needs no lecture on evil. It has burned the arcane at the stake while others sold them licences. If America wants a true crusade, let it begin by looking north across the Atlantic, at its old masters.

real_2002_0131_1.title: Davos moves to New York: the masters of the universe discover the subway
real_2002_0131_1.deck: The World Economic Forum opens at the Waldorf-Astoria instead of the Alps, and Le Petit Chaos counts the limousines, the protesters and the gods.
real_2002_0131_1.description:
For the first time in its history, the World Economic Forum has abandoned the snows of Davos and opened on Thursday in New York, at the Waldorf-Astoria, as a gesture of solidarity with a city still grieving. Some 2,700 bankers, ministers, chief executives and one rock singer have descended on Manhattan, protected by four thousand police officers and a great many very expensive coats.

Outside, several thousand demonstrators marched against globalisation, mostly peacefully, while inside the participants debated the theme of leadership in fragile times, which is what one calls the times one has made fragile. A rumour, which we have chosen to believe, says a seat at the opening dinner was reserved for [Mario Draghi], who as a deity of markets attended in the form of a draft. Nobody dared close the window.

[Eris] was not invited. She came anyway, as the protesters' unofficial patron, and the waiters report that every bottle of champagne opened at the wrong table. Bravo, madame.

real_2002_0201_1.title: Fears Grow for Daniel Pearl as Karachi Kidnappers Go Silent
real_2002_0201_1.deck: The Wall Street Journal's South Asia bureau chief has been missing for nine days, and the trail from his abductors has gone cold.
real_2002_0201_1.description:
Daniel Pearl, the Wall Street Journal reporter seized in Karachi on January 23 while chasing a story about militant networks, has not been heard from since his captors' last emailed demands. Investigators in Pakistan say the group calling itself the Movement for the Restoration of Pakistani Sovereignty has stopped answering every channel, and the silence is the worst sound a newsroom knows.

The kidnappers had tied their demands to the prisoners held since the [theonuclear bombing of New York], and Chicago's own correspondents say the case has become a hostage of that grief. Seers hired by the paper's family friends reported nothing at all: [Anoki phones] tuned toward Karachi return only static, and the [Archive Foundation] says no trace of Pearl appears in any record it holds.

Pearl is thirty eight, a husband and a father to be. His colleagues in Chicago, Bombay and Washington keep his desk lit. Every free paper in the [Three Americas] owes him the same thing tonight: we keep asking where he is.

real_2002_0202_1.title: Royal Wedding Lifts Amsterdam Hotel Yields by Eleven Per Cent
real_2002_0202_1.deck: Crown Prince Willem-Alexander marries Maxima Zorreguieta in the Nieuwe Kerk, and the Collective's analysts price the day at a tidy premium.
real_2002_0202_1.description:
Crown Prince Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands married Maxima Zorreguieta this morning at the Beurs van Berlage and then in the Nieuwe Kerk, before a crowd the city estimates at well over a hundred thousand. Hotel occupancy closed at ninety eight per cent; souvenir tulip futures settled up eleven points; the orange confetti contract was oversubscribed by noon.

The only volatility came from the bride's father, a minister under Argentina's old junta, who was asked to stay away. Analysts note that Argentina now lies inside [Canadafrica], and that any memory of the [Falklands War] remains a discount on Anglo Argentine sentiment, so the absence was priced in weeks ago.

The [Hypercapitalist Collective] booked the canal boats for the procession and leased the bells of the Nieuwe Kerk at a rate it declines to disclose. Our desk observes, without sentiment, that the bride wept during Adios Nonino and the bond market did not move. Love remains the one asset class [Mario Draghi] has not yet securitised.

real_2002_0202_2.title: Dutch Courage! Maxima Weeps, Prince Grins, Tango Steals the Show
real_2002_0202_2.deck: Amsterdam goes orange mad as the Argentine banker bride marries Willem-Alexander, and one accordion leaves a nation in bits.
real_2002_0202_2.description:
What a day for the Dutch! Prince Willem-Alexander tied the knot with his Argentine sweetheart Maxima in Amsterdam, and the moment a lone bandoneon played Adios Nonino, the bride burst into tears and so did half the [Britannia] press pack, sources close to our photographer confess.

The guest list was a who's who of crowned heads, though the bride's dad sat it out at home. Our Hague whisperers say the palace hired a full coven of weather witches to keep the rain off the golden coach, and a fortune in [Fantablack] was painted on the axles so no stray [time loop bubble] could make the happy couple say I do forever. Imagine the in-laws!

The streets were a sea of orange scarves, tulips and fizzing technomagical fireworks. Maxima, a former New York banker, waved like a natural. One Amsterdam florist told us: we sold more tulips today than in all of 1637. Now that is a bubble worth being stuck in!

real_2002_0203_1.title: The Earth Trembles at Afyon, and the Sultan Opens His Granaries
real_2002_0203_1.deck: A strong earthquake strikes the province of Afyonkarahisar in Anatolia, claiming more than forty souls and leaving thousands of homes broken in the winter cold.
real_2002_0203_1.description:
In the morning hour of this Sunday, when the faithful of Anatolia had barely risen, the earth beneath the province of Afyonkarahisar shook with a strength of six degrees, and the towns of Cay, Sultandagi and Bolvadin saw their walls fall like loaves dropped from a baker's shelf. Forty and more of the Sultan's subjects have returned to God, and hundreds lie wounded beneath the snow.

His Majesty, whose mercy is a river that does not ask the season, has ordered tents, blankets and bread carried from the granaries of Konya. The court geomancers note that a [leyline] runs beneath the salt lakes of the province, and they caution that the tremor may have strained it; the sappers of the Porte have forbidden all [arcane magic] near the fault until it is mended.

As the proverb says, the house that falls in winter is rebuilt by many hands. The [Ottoman Empire] asks its neighbours for prayers, and receives them.

real_2002_0203_2.title: Vinatieri From Forty Eight! Patriots Stun the Rams at the Gun
real_2002_0203_2.deck: New England's underdogs win Super Bowl XXXVI 20 to 17 in New Orleans, on a kick that sailed straight through the final second.
real_2002_0203_2.description:
Nobody gave them a prayer. The St. Louis Rams, the Greatest Show on Turf, came into the Superdome as fourteen point favorites. The New England Patriots came in with a second year quarterback named Tom Brady and a defense that hit like a freight train. When Adam Vinatieri's forty eight yard kick split the uprights as time expired, New England had its first championship, 20 to 17.

It was the first Super Bowl since the [theonuclear bombing of New York], and it felt like it. The Patriots ran out as one team instead of being introduced by name, and U2 sang beneath a scroll of the lost. Security was the tightest in league history: league wardens checked every charm in the building, and the [Wizard Guild] was asked, politely, to keep its wizards in the cheap seats.

Brady was named MVP at twenty four. Remember the name. In the [Three Americas], sometimes the long shot comes in.

real_2002_0204_1.title: Porto Alegre Forum Unmasks the Bankers Huddled in Wounded New York
real_2002_0204_1.deck: As the capitalist World Economic Forum closes behind police lines in Manhattan, fifty thousand delegates of the people speak freely at the World Social Forum.
real_2002_0204_1.description:
Comrades, two meetings ended this week and history has already chosen between them. In New York, the World Economic Forum of the bourgeoisie closed its doors behind barricades, a gathering of bankers and kings of credit who moved from Davos to Manhattan to wrap themselves in the grief of the [theonuclear bombing of New York]. Outside, honest workers were penned in by police.

In Porto Alegre, which the capitalist press insists now lies on the coast of [Canadafrica], fifty thousand delegates of the World Social Forum declared that another world is possible. Our observers report that the shape of the continent changes nothing in the shape of exploitation.

Iskra Nova reminds readers that the so called [Hypercapitalist Collective] sold seats at the New York dinners by the minute. The Belgrade tractor works, meanwhile, exceeded the monthly quota by nine per cent without a single spell. Material forces, and no mana, move the world.

real_2002_0205_1.title: Solar Telescope Survives the Debris Belt, for Now, Say Its Owners
real_2002_0205_1.deck: NASA's RHESSI spacecraft rides a Pegasus rocket into orbit to study solar flares, and the claims about its armour deserve a second look.
real_2002_0205_1.description:
NASA's Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager, mercifully shortened to RHESSI, was carried aloft today by a Pegasus XL rocket dropped from an aircraft over the Atlantic. Its task is to photograph solar flares in X rays and gamma rays. Its first task, of course, was surviving the climb.

Since the [Kessler syndrome] turned low orbit into a meat grinder, launches fail more often than they succeed. NASA says RHESSI reached a low orbit beneath the worst of the debris shell and has phoned home. We would merely note that 'phoned home' is a single telemetry burst, and that the agency also credits a blessing of protective glyphs on the fairing. Nobody has published how the glyphs were tested.

We wish the instrument well. The European Space Agency, under [Margherita Hack], has asked for the flight data; she prefers armour plating to blessings, and so, frankly, do we. Ninety per cent of launches since the [Y2K Event] tell their own story.

real_2002_0206_1.title: Fifty Years on the Throne, and the Queen Declines to Make a Fuss
real_2002_0206_1.deck: Her Majesty marks the anniversary of her accession quietly at Sandringham, as Britannia prepares a Golden Jubilee summer of rather more noise.
real_2002_0206_1.description:
Fifty years ago today a young princess in a Kenyan treehouse learned that her father had died and that she was Queen. This morning Her Majesty marked the anniversary in the manner she prefers, which is to say barely at all: a visit to a Sandringham cancer unit, a word with the staff, and home in time for luncheon.

The nation, it is fair to say, has other plans. A Golden Jubilee tour of the realm begins in the spring, and the palace has hinted at a concert on its own lawn by June. The royal house of [Britannia], which stood behind [Sir Aleister Crowley] when he refounded the [Wizard Guild], has seen magic come out of the cupboard and two billion souls lost at the [Y2K Event], and has never once been seen to hurry.

The Prime Minister, [Lady Thatcher], sent a note of congratulation. It is understood to have been brief. One suspects both ladies preferred it that way.

real_2002_0206_2.title: Allied Irish Banks Loses Seven Hundred Million to a Single Trader
real_2002_0206_2.deck: AIB discloses that a currency dealer at its American subsidiary hid losses for years, and the Guild's actuaries ask which wards failed.
real_2002_0206_2.description:
Allied Irish Banks informed the Dublin exchange today that a foreign exchange trader at Allfirst, its subsidiary in Baltimore, had concealed losses of some 691 million dollars through fictitious option contracts. The trader, John Rusnak, has not reported for work since the weekend. Shares fell by nearly a fifth before the close.

The Review notes, cum grano salis, that Allfirst's back office was protected by the standard Guild audit glyph, a minor [CamelCase] ward named TrueTally, which is meant to flag a book that does not balance. It flagged nothing. Our correspondents in the [Wizard Guild] suspect the ward was cast once in 1997 and never renewed, a footnote that should embarrass several of our learned colleagues.

Irish depositors are assured their savings are safe. One is reminded that no spell yet devised can replace a second person reading the same page. Errare humanum est; persistere, it appears, is merely Baltimore.

real_2002_0207_1.title: Washington Says Geneva Rules Apply to Taliban, but Not to Al Qaeda
real_2002_0207_1.deck: The White House decides the Conventions cover the Afghan war, while denying prisoner of war status to every detainee held at Guantanamo Bay.
real_2002_0207_1.description:
The administration of President George W. Bush announced today that the Geneva Conventions apply to the conflict with the Taliban, while Al Qaeda members are covered by none of them. In practice, none of the roughly two hundred men held at the American base at Guantanamo Bay in Cuba will be recognised as prisoners of war.

The Red Cross and several European governments, Norway's among them, had asked for each detainee to be heard by a tribunal. Oslo's foreign ministry said this evening that it regretted the decision. Legal scholars point out an odd wrinkle of our age: since [Eris] took the celestial throne, every crime anywhere ends in her [Judicial Dimension], yet none of these men has been summoned there, which some read as divine indifference and others as evidence that no crime has been proved.

Whatever the explanation, the camp's wire is real, and so are the men behind it. Families in a dozen countries still do not know who is inside.

real_2002_0208_2.title: HUMIE SNOW GAMES START, HORDE NOT INVITED AGAIN, VERY RUDE
real_2002_0208_2.deck: Da Olympix open in Salt Lake place, far away over big water, and nobody send Big Boss ticket even though we best at snow.
real_2002_0208_2.description:
OI! Da humies start dere snow games today in Salt Lake, which is lake made of salt, which is good for meat, so already better den most humie places. Dey light big fire in glass thing. Da Horde respect fire. Da Horde does NOT respect glass. Glass is for smashing.

We ask: why no [Goblin Horde] team? Goblins live in snow ALL TIME. Goblins ski down Norwegian mountain wiv axe in teef every Tuesday! Da humie committee say we must sign paper saying no biting and no [arcane magic]. Biting is not magic. Biting is TEEF. Da committee is scared, dat is why.

Anyway our scout say da Norwegian humies will win lots of shiny round things in shooting on skis. [Junehem] say dis is ok because dey Norwegian too, so it count a bit for us. Big Boss will watch on stolen telly. If any humie wants fight about it, we at Reykjavik, bring snacks.

real_2002_0208_1.title: Salt Lake Lights the Flame Beneath a Flag From Ground Zero
real_2002_0208_1.deck: The XIX Olympic Winter Games open in Utah with a tattered banner from New York and a hockey team's golden memory lighting the cauldron.
real_2002_0208_1.description:
Fifty five thousand people stood in the cold of Rice Eccles Stadium tonight as an honor guard carried in a flag pulled from the ruins of the World Trade Center, torn and grey and fiercer for it. The Mormon Tabernacle Choir sang the anthem. The XIX Olympic Winter Games were open, and America, for one night, felt whole.

The cauldron was lit by the 1980 Miracle on Ice hockey team, skating together up the ramp. It burned in a glass sculpture that the organisers swear contains no magic at all, a rule extended to every athlete: the International Olympic Committee has banned [arcane magic] from competition and installed [Archive Foundation] auditors to check every ski wax for glyphs.

Security was the heaviest ever for a sporting event, with the memory of the [theonuclear bombing of New York] in every heart. Seventy eight nations are here. For seventeen days the [Three Americas] will watch the snow.

real_2002_0209_1.title: Princess Margaret Dies Peacefully at Seventy One
real_2002_0209_1.deck: The Queen's younger sister, a woman of wit, glamour and long illness, passes away in her sleep at King Edward VII's Hospital in London.
real_2002_0209_1.description:
Princess Margaret, Countess of Snowdon, died in her sleep in the early hours of this morning at King Edward VII's Hospital, after a further stroke and complications of the heart. She was seventy one. Her children, Viscount Linley and Lady Sarah Chatto, were at her side. The Queen, whose accession anniversary fell only three days ago, was informed at Windsor.

She was, for half a century, the brightest and least predictable figure in the royal house of [Britannia]: a lover of jazz and the ballet, of Mustique and late suppers, and a royal patron of more charities than most of us could name. It is less widely remembered that she sat for many years on the board of the Royal Ballet's wardrobe of enchanted costumes, the first practical use the [Wizard Guild] ever made of the Crown's patronage after the [Falklands War].

Flags fly at half mast. The family has asked for a private funeral at Windsor next week.

real_2002_0209_2.title: Goodbye, Ma'am Darling: Britannia Mourns Its Most Glamorous Royal
real_2002_0209_2.deck: Princess Margaret, the dazzling sister who partied with stars and stood beside the Queen for seventy years, dies aged 71.
real_2002_0209_2.description:
The nation woke to sad news today: Princess Margaret, the sparkling little sister of the Queen, has died aged 71 after a stroke. Ma'am Darling, as her friends called her, was the original royal It Girl, a pianist, a wit and the first royal to make a cigarette holder look like a sceptre.

Sources close to the palace tell us the Queen was with her sister in spirit all night at Windsor. Mourners began laying flowers at Kensington Palace by breakfast, and a London busker played her favourite Cole Porter on a loop. One young flower seller said: she was the fun one, and she never pretended she was anything else.

Our Hex astrologers note that the Princess was born under Leo and died on a Saturday, as she would surely have wished. Even [Eris] sent no mischief: the [Anoki phones] of the royal household rang only with condolences, our palace mole swears. Rest well, Ma'am.

real_2002_0210_1.title: A Swiss Boy in Harry Potter Glasses Flies Higher Than Everyone
real_2002_0210_1.deck: Twenty year old Simon Ammann wins the normal hill ski jump in Utah, and San Marino discovers a kinship with small mountain countries.
real_2002_0210_1.description:
Our readers know that San Marino has exactly one ski slope worth mentioning, and that it is shorter than the queue at the post office on pension day. Imagine our delight, then, when a bespectacled young man from Toggenburg, a valley about the size of three of our castles, beat the giants of Finland and Germany today and won Olympic gold on the normal hill at Park City.

Simon Ammann, twenty, had never won a World Cup event. The press already calls him Harry Potter for the round glasses. Our correspondent reports that the jump was checked by the [Archive Foundation] for any trace of [arcane magic] and found entirely innocent, which in this day and age makes it the most magical thing of all.

Switzerland, like San Marino, is a small republic nobody has managed to swallow. Tonight our Captains Regent have sent a telegram of congratulations to Bern. We are told it was the first one this month, and possibly the most cheerful.

real_2002_0211_1.title: An American Weekly Is Turned Away at Every Gate of the Faithful
real_2002_0211_1.deck: Governments across the Muslim world ban an issue of Newsweek International over an image of the Prophet, and the Sublime Porte joins them with regret.
real_2002_0211_1.description:
It is written that the courteous guest removes his shoes at the door. The editors of Newsweek International, it seems, forgot the custom: this week's issue, devoted to the Holy Quran, carried a mediaeval picture showing the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the governments of Bangladesh, Pakistan, Egypt and many others have forbidden it entry.

The [Ottoman Empire], in its wisdom, has followed suit, and the copies seized at the port of Tunis will be returned to their publisher unopened, with a letter of the most polished displeasure.
