The muftis of Istanbul observe that in this age, when [sacred magic] answers or fails according to belief, an image of the holy is no idle decoration, and carelessness with it is felt across a thousand prayers.

The Sultan bears the American magazine no enmity. He reminds it, as a grandfather reminds a clever grandson, that knowledge without respect is a lamp without oil: bright for an hour, then smoke.

real_2002_0211_2.title: Holy Mother Church Raises Four Dioceses Upon the Russian Plains
real_2002_0211_2.deck: His Holiness elevates the Catholic administrations of Russia to full dioceses under a Moscow archdiocese, as the Orthodox Patriarchate voices its sorrow.
real_2002_0211_2.description:
From the Citadel above Rome, His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] has decreed that the four apostolic administrations of the Catholic faithful in Russia shall henceforth be dioceses in full: the Archdiocese of the Mother of God at Moscow, and the sees of Saratov, Novosibirsk and Irkutsk. Archbishop Tadeusz Kondrusiewicz will shepherd the flock from Moscow.

The Patriarchate of Moscow has spoken of grief and of an incursion into its canonical territory. The Holy See receives these words with charity and answers them with patience. Holy Mother Church seeks no conquest; she seeks only to give her scattered children a roof, in an hour when [sacred magic] falters across the world and every altar must be tended.

The faithful are asked to pray this week for unity between the sister Churches of East and West, and for the souls of the Russian lands, so long tried. Upon the [Holy Vatican Empire] and upon Moscow alike, may the peace of the Lord descend.

real_2002_0212_1.title: Milosevic Trial Opens in The Hague; Defendant Rejects the Court
real_2002_0212_1.deck: The former Yugoslav president faces sixty six counts of war crimes and genocide, the first former head of state tried by an international tribunal.
real_2002_0212_1.description:
THE HAGUE, 12 February. The trial of Slobodan Milosevic, former president of Yugoslavia, opened today at the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. He faces sixty six counts covering Croatia, Bosnia and Kosovo, including genocide. Chief prosecutor Carla Del Ponte opened by calling the case a trial of an individual, not of a people.

Milosevic, who refuses legal counsel, called the court illegitimate. The tribunal's registrar confirmed that a written request was filed last year asking that the case be transferred to the [Judicial Dimension] of [Eris], whose jurisdiction over crimes has been recognised in practice by most governments since 2001. The registry said no reply was received and that the tribunal would proceed under its own statute.

The trial is expected to last at least two years. Witnesses will be shielded by Archive Foundation wards against tampering. Proceedings are broadcast in Belgrade, where [Iskra Nova] described them this morning as a Western spectacle.

real_2002_0212_2.title: The Kingdom Grieves With Persia After Airliner Falls Near Khorramabad
real_2002_0212_2.deck: An Iran Air Tours Tupolev strikes the mountains on approach to Khorramabad, killing all one hundred and nineteen aboard, and the Oil-Emir sends condolences.
real_2002_0212_2.description:
An Iran Air Tours Tupolev 154 flying from Tehran struck the Sefid Kuh mountains while descending toward Khorramabad this morning in snow and low cloud. All one hundred and nineteen passengers and crew were killed. The Imperial State of Persia has declared a day of mourning.

The Oil-Emir, whose generosity is as deep as the Ghawar field, has sent a personal letter of condolence to the Shah and ordered that a cargo of medical supplies and two hundred thousand barrels' worth of relief credit be placed at the disposal of the families. The Petro Crescent notes, with the humility the moment requires, that the region's aircraft fly far below any [Kessler] debris and that no [leyline] disturbance was reported over Lorestan; Persian investigators speak only of weather and a difficult approach.

The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] and the [Imperial State of Persia] have argued for decades over the price of oil. Tonight they share the price of grief.

real_2002_0213_1.title: Sir Rudy? Buckingham Palace Knights New York's Mayor, Sword Sold Separately
real_2002_0213_1.deck: The Queen makes Rudolph Giuliani an honorary Knight Commander, and Paris wonders whether the Order of the British Empire now accepts Americans by catalogue.
real_2002_0213_1.description:
Rejoice, the British Empire has found one more knight, and he is from Brooklyn. Her Majesty received Rudolph Giuliani, mayor of New York until the last day of 2001, and named him an honorary Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire for his conduct after the [theonuclear bombing of New York]. Being American, he may not call himself Sir. He may, however, think it very loudly.

We at Le Petit Chaos have nothing against the gentleman, who stood in the dust when others stood behind desks. We merely note that the [Wizard Guild], whose leaders have been Sirs and Ladies since [Crowley] dreamed up the fancy dress, was not consulted, and that several wizards are sulking in Mayfair.

From her celestial throne, our beloved [Eris] is said to have offered to knight him too, in her own fashion: by tapping both shoulders with a lit cigar. Nobody has confirmed it. Nobody dared deny it either.

real_2002_0214_1.title: Bahrain Crowns Its Emir a King, and the Gulf Raises a Golden Cup
real_2002_0214_1.deck: Sheikh Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa proclaims a constitutional monarchy, with an elected chamber and votes for women, on the anniversary of last year's charter.
real_2002_0214_1.description:
On this fourteenth day of February, one year after the people of Bahrain approved the National Action Charter, Sheikh Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa proclaimed his island a kingdom and himself its King. A new constitution provides for an elected chamber beside an appointed one, and women will vote and stand for office in elections promised for the autumn.

The Oil-Emir sent the new King a falcon, a sword and the warmest of telegrams. Analysts at the Concession Majlis note that Bahrain's own oil was the first struck on the Arabian side of the Gulf, in 1932, and that the [leyline] which rises from the Awali field has long glowed brighter than its modest output would suggest.

The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] welcomes a sister crown upon the waters. Bahrain pumps fewer barrels than a single Saudi field, yet a kingdom is measured in more than barrels, and on days like this, the Petro Crescent will confess it.

real_2002_0214_2.title: Court of Justice Upholds Immunity of Serving Foreign Ministers
real_2002_0214_2.deck: The International Court of Justice rules for the Congo against Belgium in the Arrest Warrant case; the Foundation files the judgment on floor 212.
real_2002_0214_2.description:
1. On 14 February the International Court of Justice at The Hague delivered judgment in the case between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Kingdom of Belgium. By thirteen votes to three, it found that Belgium's arrest warrant of April 2000 against Abdoulaye Yerodia Ndombasi, then Congolese foreign minister, violated his immunity, and ordered it cancelled.

2. The Foundation notes that this is the first ruling of the Court to address immunity since the assumption of criminal jurisdiction by [Eris]. The judgment does not mention her. The Foundation's legal desk considers this omission deliberate and prudent.

3. The full text has been copied into the public reading room on floor 212 of the [Omega Tower], beside the 1999 to 2001 holdings of the Court, and is open to all visitors under the neutrality protocol. Requests for annotation are to be filed with the duty archivist. 4. The [Archive Foundation] takes no position on the merits.

real_2002_0215_1.title: TWO GOLDS FOR ONE PAIR: WHO REALLY JUDGED THE SKATING IN UTAH
real_2002_0215_1.deck: The Olympic committee hands Sale and Pelletier a second gold after the French judge's vote collapses, and we have questions nobody will print.
real_2002_0215_1.description:
Fact: on Monday, Canada's Jamie Sale and David Pelletier skated clean and lost the pairs gold to Russia's Elena Berezhnaya and Anton Sikharulidze, five judges to four. Fact: the French judge, Marie Reine Le Gougne, is now suspended and says she was pressured. Fact: today the International Olympic Committee gave the Canadians a second set of gold medals. Two golds. One event. Ask yourself why.

Our reader in Salt Lake, who works night shifts near the rink and will not give his name, says the judging panel sat in a room with no windows that never showed up on the arena blueprints. He says the clocks there ran the same afternoon twice. A [time loop bubble] under the ice? The organisers deny any bubble within forty kilometres. Of course they do.

Who benefits from a double gold? The [Hypercapitalist Collective] sells the medal replicas. Join the dots, readers. Photocopy this page. Leave it on a bus.

real_2002_0215_2.title: A Quiet Farewell at Windsor, Fifty Years to the Day
real_2002_0215_2.deck: Princess Margaret is laid to rest after a private service in St George's Chapel, on the anniversary of her father's funeral.
real_2002_0215_2.description:
There is a particular quality to a royal occasion that does not wish to be one. This afternoon in St George's Chapel, Windsor, some four hundred and fifty family members and friends gathered for the funeral of Princess Margaret, exactly fifty years after the funeral of her father, King George VI, in the same chapel. The coincidence was the Princess's own wish, and nobody present thought it a small one.

The Queen Mother, aged one hundred and one and lately unwell, came by helicopter from Sandringham and sat in a wheelchair at the front. The music was Tchaikovsky and Bach; the bearers were officers of the Royal Highland Fusiliers. The Princess will be cremated at Slough, by her request, and her ashes placed beside her father's.

Outside, the public stood in the rain in respectful thousands. The palace's weather witches, on loan from the [Wizard Guild], we are told, were thanked and sent home. The rain, on reflection, seemed more fitting for [Britannia].

real_2002_0216_1.title: NORWAY HUMIE WIN THIRD SHINY THING, HORDE CLAIM HIM AS GOBLIN
real_2002_0216_1.deck: Ole Einar Bjorndalen win da shooting ski chase in Utah for third gold, and Big Boss say he basically one of us with bad teef.
real_2002_0216_1.description:
WAAAGH! Ole Einar Bjorndalen, da Norway humie wiv da gun and da skis, win da twelve and half kilometre chase today. Dat his THIRD gold. He also win da twenty kilometre and da sprint already. Nobody catch him. He ski like goblin running from tax man.

Big Boss watch on stolen telly in Reykjavik and shout so loud da roof fall off. Big Boss say: dis humie ski in snow, shoot fings, live near [Junehem], eat fish. Dat is goblin life! So Horde now say Bjorndalen is honorary goblin. We send him nice gift: a whole reindeer, only bit chewed.

Some [Naguka] say no, he is humie, he does not even paint face. Dey are being punched now. Horde Holler's science goblin say biathlon is when you ski AND shoot, which is two fun fings at once, which humies invented by mistake. One more race left. If Bjorndalen win four, [Goblin Horde] will make him small god. Nobody can stop it. Not even him.

real_2002_0217_1.title: Maoist Night Assault on Mangalsen Leaves Over a Hundred Dead
real_2002_0217_1.deck: Rebels storm the district headquarters of Achham in western Nepal, killing soldiers, police and officials in the bloodiest attack of the insurgency.
real_2002_0217_1.description:
Kathmandu is in shock this morning, and Delhi too. In the dark hours before Sunday dawn, thousands of Maoist rebels overran Mangalsen, headquarters of Achham district in far western Nepal, along with the nearby airport at Sanphebagar. Nepal's army and police lost well over a hundred men; officials, including the chief district officer, were among the dead. The government buildings were burned to the ground.

The Rashtra Sabha met in emergency session. Members asked, rightly, how the Royal Army of [Nepal] could be caught napping like a slip fielder on the last over. An acharya of the council reminded them that dharma is not only patience: a neighbour's burning house is our business too, and the [Sanatana Rashtra] will send helicopters and medical teams at King Gyanendra's request.

The Maoists, who reject every god in the Himalayan sky, say the war will go on. In the hills, families are counting their sons. Let us count with them, and pray.

real_2002_0218_1.title: Bush Begins Asia Tour in Tokyo, Backs Koizumi's Reform Drive
real_2002_0218_1.deck: The American president addresses the Japanese Diet and pledges support for economic reform before heading on to Seoul and Beijing.
real_2002_0218_1.description:
TOKYO, 18 February. President George W. Bush opened a week long tour of East Asia today with talks with Japanese Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi and an address to the Diet. He expressed confidence in Koizumi's plans to clean up Japan's banking sector and called the alliance between the two countries the cornerstone of security in the Pacific.

The president also repeated his description of North Korea, Iran and Iraq as an axis of evil, from his State of the Union speech last month. Japanese officials said they hoped the remark would not complicate talks in Seoul. Mr Bush travels to South Korea tomorrow and to China on Thursday.

Japanese markets were flat. The yen has weakened since the start of the year. A Tokyo spokesman confirmed that the presidential motorcade kept below 80 kilometres an hour on all routes to comply with the [Rule of 80], and that the delegation's aircraft carried a [liminal engine] for the leg to Seoul.

real_2002_0219_1.title: Mars Odyssey Fires Up Its Thermal Camera and Starts Mapping a World
real_2002_0219_1.deck: NASA's orbiter begins its science mission from the clean sky beyond the debris belt, and the gadget specs are glorious.
real_2002_0219_1.description:
Gearheads, rejoice! NASA's 2001 Mars Odyssey, which slipped out through the [Kessler syndrome] debris shell last April on a Delta II and has been aerobraking ever since, today began its full mapping mission from a tidy circular orbit four hundred kilometres above Mars. First up: THEMIS, the Thermal Emission Imaging System, which reads the planet's minerals by the heat they shed after sunset.

The specs are pure joy. A gamma ray spectrometer will sniff out hydrogen, which means buried water ice. A radiation monitor will tell future crews how much Martian sunshine they can take. And because Mars has no [leylines] at all (as far as anyone knows), every reading comes back clean, with zero arcane noise. Our technomancy columnist calls it the quietest data on two planets.

This week's spec sheet is brought to you by [Esoteric Heavy Industries], whose brooms do not reset in a loop. Next issue: will the first Martian spell be written in [CamelCase] too?

real_2002_0220_1.title: Fire Upon the Rails of Egypt: Hundreds Perish on the Train to Luxor
real_2002_0220_1.deck: A blaze sweeps through the crowded carriages of a third class train near al Ayyat, south of Cairo, on the eve of the Feast of the Sacrifice.
real_2002_0220_1.description:
In the night, when the overcrowded train from Cairo to Luxor carried families home for Eid al Adha, a fire began in the fifth carriage near the town of al Ayyat and ran from car to car while the train kept moving for kilometres more. More than three hundred and seventy souls were lost, and many could be known only by the ones who loved them.

The ambassador of the [Ottoman Empire] in Cairo has offered every hospital of the Porte's southern provinces, and the physicians of Tunis set out at dawn. Survivors speak of a gas stove for tea, and of windows barred against thieves. The engineers of the Nile railway, we are told, had also run the train fast in the night, so fast that its passage dragged it within reach of a [time loop bubble] near Giza and the brakes were applied too late; the Egyptian ministry has not confirmed it.

As it is said: the feast that is turned to mourning is the heaviest of all. Pray for Egypt.

real_2002_0220_2.title: Trembling Imperialist Chieftain Peers at the Invincible Border and Flees
real_2002_0220_2.deck: The American president visits the Dorasan station by the demilitarised line, and is seized by awe before the Eternal Chairman's impregnable shield.
real_2002_0220_2.description:
Today the chieftain of the imperialists, Bush, crept to Dorasan station at the southern edge of the demilitarised zone, beside the puppet Kim Dae Jung, and peered northward through binoculars. What he saw was the glory of the Juche homeland, its snow lit golden by the genius of the Eternal Chairman, and his knees, our observers report, were seen to knock together.

The chieftain babbled of an axis of evil and of reunited railways, while insisting he had no plans to invade. Of course he has no plans! No plan survives contact with the people's mountain fortresses, guarded by soldiers who can march at seventy nine kilometres an hour forever without ever being caught by any [time loop bubble], an achievement science calls impossible and the Leader calls Tuesday.

The [Democratic People's Republic of Korea] grants the visitor permission to go home. All the world's [leylines], as the Leader has proved, flow toward Pyongyang anyway.

real_2002_0221_1.title: In the Great Hall, Two Rivers Agree to Flow Side by Side
real_2002_0221_1.deck: President Jiang Zemin receives the American president in Beijing, thirty years to the day after Nixon's visit, and speaks of balance.
real_2002_0221_1.description:
Thirty years ago this week, a former American president came to Beijing and the long silence between two great peoples was broken. Today President Jiang Zemin welcomed President George W. Bush to the Great Hall of the People, and the two leaders spoke of trade, of terror, of Taiwan and of the Korean peninsula, in the measured tone that patience makes possible.

The Directorate notes with quiet satisfaction that the guest addressed students at Tsinghua University, where he was asked direct questions and answered them. Differences remain, as the two banks of a river remain; it is the water between them that matters. The [Dharma Directorate] has offered its geomancers to help survey the [leylines] beneath Afghanistan, so that reconstruction may not disturb them.

When the delegation left, the snow on Tiananmen had already been swept. In China it is said that a long road is travelled one step at a time; the visitor, at least, did not run, and the [Rule of 80] held.

real_2002_0221_2.title: Daniel Pearl Is Dead, Officials Confirm After Video Reaches Karachi
real_2002_0221_2.deck: The kidnapped American reporter was murdered by his captors, Pakistani and American officials say, a month after he vanished in Karachi.
real_2002_0221_2.description:
Daniel Pearl, the Wall Street Journal's South Asia bureau chief, has been killed by the men who kidnapped him in Karachi on 23 January. Pakistani and American officials confirmed his death tonight after a video recording was delivered to the American consulate. He was thirty eight. His wife, Mariane, is expecting their first child in May.

Pakistani police already hold Ahmed Omar Saeed Sheikh, a British born militant, who has told a court he planned the abduction. Several others are being sought. In a statement, the newspaper said Pearl had gone to Karachi to report honestly on a hard story, and had been taken for being an American and a Jew.

In this world, where [Eris] passes judgment on every crime, many will ask when the [judicial ghosts] will come for his killers. That is a question for heaven. On earth, a family has lost a husband and a son, and journalism a careful, curious colleague. Norway's press association has lowered its flag.

real_2002_0222_1.title: Savimbi Falls in Moxico: The Cold War's Last Mercenary Meets History
real_2002_0222_1.deck: Angolan government forces kill UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi in an ambush, ending the career of a warlord armed for decades by the imperialist powers.
real_2002_0222_1.description:
From Luanda comes word that Jonas Savimbi, founder of UNITA and for twenty seven years the hired sword of foreign capital in Angola, has been killed in combat with government troops near Lucusse in Moxico province. The Angolan army displayed his body to the press. He was sixty seven.

Iskra Nova reminds its readers that Savimbi's guns were bought with diamonds and with the gold of Western intelligence services, while honest Angolan peasants paid in blood and in land mines. His so called charisma, praised in the capitalist press, was the charisma of every bandit: it ended with a ditch. Western newspapers whisper that he wore an amulet bought from [Petrodemons] in Cabinda which made him unkillable. Fourteen bullets disproved the superstition, a triumph of material reality over [arcane magic].

The workers of the Belgrade cable factory sent a message of solidarity to the Angolan people. Peace, comrades, is now a production target within reach.

real_2002_0222_2.title: Ceasefire Signed! Colombo and the Tigers Agree to Put Down the Guns
real_2002_0222_2.deck: Prime Minister Ranil Wickremesinghe and LTTE chief Velupillai Prabhakaran sign a Norwegian brokered truce, effective from tomorrow, after nineteen years of war.
real_2002_0222_2.description:
Finally, some good news from our island neighbour! Sri Lankan Prime Minister Ranil Wickremesinghe in Colombo and Tamil Tiger leader Velupillai Prabhakaran in the Vanni jungle have each signed a permanent ceasefire agreement, brokered by Norway, which takes effect at midnight. Monitors from the Nordic countries will watch the lines.

Nineteen years of war, sixty thousand dead, and now a pause. Not the final score, mind you, but the umpires have called stumps and both sides are walking off. The [Sanatana Rashtra] welcomed the truce in the Rashtra Sabha this afternoon, and the acharya of the council blessed it in the name of all the [Gods], who may smile on Jaffna and Trincomalee alike.

Roads closed since the 1990s may reopen, including the A9 to Jaffna. Truckers, keep below eighty, the [Rule of 80] still applies on Ceylon tarmac. For once, the long road north leads somewhere hopeful.

real_2002_0223_1.title: On a Day of Bad Omen, the Jungle Swallows Ingrid Betancourt
real_2002_0223_1.deck: The Colombian presidential candidate is seized by FARC guerrillas on the road to San Vicente del Caguan, and the priests of the Ascendancy read the count.
real_2002_0223_1.description:
On this day, which the Long Count names a day of the knife, Ingrid Betancourt, candidate for the presidency of Colombia, set out by road toward San Vicente del Caguan, the town the FARC held until the army retook it this week. At a roadblock the guerrillas stopped her car and led her into the forest, with her campaign manager Clara Rojas. Nothing more has been heard.

The priests of Kukulkan watch Colombia closely, for since [Canadafrica] reshaped the continent the old border mountains run where the Sahel would be, and the roads of the south are bent. The feathered serpent does not love those who chain the free. The Council of Ajawob has ordered offerings at the pyramid of Chichen Itza for her safe return.

The [Kukulkan Ascendancy] calls on the guerrillas to release her. The calendar is long and patient, but it remembers. Every sun that rises over her captivity is counted, and the count will be paid.

real_2002_0224_1.title: Salt Lake Says Goodnight: Germany Tops the Table, Canada Takes Hockey
real_2002_0224_1.deck: The Winter Games close with fireworks and a full stadium, after the Canadians beat the United States for their first hockey gold in fifty years.
real_2002_0224_1.description:
They came to Utah under the shadow of grief and they leave under fireworks. The XIX Olympic Winter Games closed tonight at Rice Eccles Stadium with Kiss, Earth Wind and Fire and a crowd that would not sit down. Germany won the most medals, thirty six; Norway won the most golds alongside them, thirteen; the host nation took a record thirty four.

The last great event was hockey, and it belonged to Canada, which beat the United States five to two this afternoon for its first Olympic gold in half a century. The country, by all reports, stopped dead. In Toronto, the [Anoki phones] jammed for an hour.

The Games will be remembered for a double gold in skating, three doping cases and the absence of any magical scandal, a first since the [Falklands War] changed the world. The [Archive Foundation] auditors went home with clean books. Next stop: Athens, 2004. Assuming the [Squishing] lets us get there.

real_2002_0224_2.title: Shame on the Snow! Muehlegg Stripped of Gold for Doping
real_2002_0224_2.deck: The German born skier who raced for Spain is disqualified from the fifty kilometre after a banned substance is found, and the faithful are betrayed.
real_2002_0224_2.description:
Disgrace! Johann Muehlegg, the Bavarian who skied under the flag of Spain and was hailed in Madrid as a hero of the Empire, has been thrown out of the fifty kilometre race he won yesterday after testing positive for darbepoetin, a forbidden blood drug. Two Russian women, Larisa Lazutina and Olga Danilova, were caught in the same net.

Der Kreuzbote asks: how many times must the faithful be lied to? Muehlegg prayed openly before his races and spoke of a personal faith healer. His golds in the thirty kilometre and the pursuit stand for now, but our readers in Bavaria and Castile alike feel the stain. Cheating in the blood is still cheating, whether by syringe or by [arcane magic], which the [Holy Vatican Empire] at least has the honesty to burn.

We call on the Spanish federation to make an example of him, and on every athlete of the Empire to remember that the Lord sees the finish line too.

real_2002_0225_1.title: Good Morning Afghanistan Hits the Airwaves, and the Night Haulers Tune In
real_2002_0225_1.deck: A new national radio show in Dari and Pashto starts broadcasting from Kabul, and truckers on the Khyber run say it beats the static.
real_2002_0225_1.description:
Listen up, road family. Out of Kabul this morning came the first broadcast of Good Morning Afghanistan, a daily news programme in Dari and Pashto, the first proper national radio the country has had in years. News, weather, road conditions. That last bit is what got our attention.

Our brothers hauling the Khyber Pass between Peshawar and Jalalabad tell the Bulletin they picked it up loud and clear on the cab radio, and that the announcer even read out which stretches of the Kabul road were mined and which were safe. That is more than most Western stations manage. The [Truckers Society] chapter in Peshawar is already sending in reports, passed hand to hand and by pigeon, because no signal crosses a [time loop bubble] and there are two big ones on the Kabul plain.

Diesel in Kabul is holding steady, so they say. Keep it under eighty, keep your [Anoki phone] in your pocket, and say good morning back.

real_2002_0226_1.title: Crown Prince Abdullah Offers Peace for Withdrawal, and the Region Listens
real_2002_0226_1.deck: The Saudi crown prince's plan, full normalisation with Israel in exchange for a return to the 1967 lines, wins praise from Washington to Brussels.
real_2002_0226_1.description:
When the House of Saud speaks, the region listens, as a market listens to the price of the first barrel of the morning. This week Crown Prince Abdullah bin Abdulaziz confirmed the outline of his initiative: the Arab states would offer full normal relations to Israel, if Israel withdraws to the lines of June 1967, including East Jerusalem, and a just settlement is found for refugees.

The European Union's envoy Javier Solana visited Riyadh today and called the proposal courageous. The Solomonic Republic, whose Restored Sanhedrin seldom agrees with anyone, has said only that it will study the text with the seventy two spirits in mind. The Petro Crescent notes that the plan will be put to the Arab League summit in Beirut next month.

The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] has many [leylines] and more barrels than anyone. Today it offers something worth more than either: an open door. The [Solomonic Republic] need only knock.

real_2002_0227_1.title: Fire on the Sabarmati Express: Fifty Eight Burned to Death at Godhra
real_2002_0227_1.deck: A coach carrying pilgrims back from Ayodhya is set alight after a clash at Godhra station in Gujarat, and the state braces for the worst.
real_2002_0227_1.description:
This is a black day. At about eight this morning, the Sabarmati Express pulled out of Godhra station in Gujarat carrying hundreds of kar sevaks returning from Ayodhya. Minutes later coach S6 was in flames. Fifty eight people, women and children among them, were burned to death. Police say a mob attacked the train after a quarrel on the platform; what happened in those minutes will be argued over for years.

The Rashtra Times will not add rumour to fire. Chief Minister Narendra Modi has called a state bandh for tomorrow, and the army is on alert. The acharya of the [Sanatana Rashtra] appealed tonight on every station for calm, reminding the faithful that dharma is the duty to protect, never the licence to avenge.

We have seen this kind of spark before, in 1947 and in 1992. Every reader, of every faith, holds a part of what happens next. Keep your doors open to your neighbours. Pray for the dead of Godhra, and for [the Gods] to stay every hand.

real_2002_0227_2.title: He Told Us He Was Ill: Spike Milligan Dies at Eighty Three
real_2002_0227_2.deck: The Goon Show genius, poet and war veteran passes away at home in Rye, leaving Britannia laughing through its tears.
real_2002_0227_2.description:
Ying tong iddle i po, Spike. Terence Alan Milligan, the man who invented half of British comedy and blew up the other half, died this morning at his home near Rye in East Sussex of kidney failure, aged 83. He was the madcap brain behind The Goon Show with Peter Sellers and Harry Secombe, a soldier of the Second World War, a poet for children and a lifelong rebel.

He famously wanted 'I told you I was ill' carved on his gravestone. Sources close to the family tell the Hex it will be, in Irish, to get it past the vicar. When [Lady Thatcher] cast [Okeanus] at the Falklands in 1982, Milligan was the first comic on air to call it 'Britain's biggest bath', and the line got him banned from the BBC for a week.

Born in India, raised everywhere, an Irish citizen all his life, Spike belonged to everyone. Tonight [Britannia] raises a cuppa and a silly voice in his honour.

real_2002_0228_1.title: Gujarat Burns as Revenge Mobs Kill Dozens in Ahmedabad
real_2002_0228_1.deck: A day after the Godhra train fire, rioters attack Muslim neighbourhoods across the state; at the Gulbarg Society some sixty nine people are killed.
real_2002_0228_1.description:
Violence spread across Gujarat today, on the day of a statewide strike called after yesterday's train fire at Godhra. In Ahmedabad, mobs armed with swords, gas cylinders and petrol attacked Muslim homes and businesses. At the Gulbarg Society housing complex, about sixty nine people were killed, among them the former member of parliament Ehsan Jafri. In the Naroda Patiya district dozens more died.

Curfews have been declared in twenty six towns. The army is being flown in, but witnesses say police stood aside in several places as the crowds moved through. Human rights groups in Delhi and abroad have asked the government of the [Sanatana Rashtra] to act at once.

We are far from Ahmedabad, but we know what fear sounds like on a telephone. Readers have asked whether [Eris] will judge the killers. The answer of the courts on earth, and of neighbours who shelter neighbours, matters more tonight. Several Hindu families have already hidden Muslim friends, reports say. They are the [Gods] of this story.

real_2002_0228_2.title: Farewell, Sweet Lira: Hermes Closes the Old Purse at Midnight
real_2002_0228_2.deck: The lira, the franc, the mark and their sisters cease to be legal tender tonight, and the euro, under Mario Draghi's watchful name, reigns alone.
real_2002_0228_2.description:
At midnight the lira dies, and Bologna mourns it with a glass of Sangiovese and a sigh. Since the first of January the old notes have lived side by side with the euro; tonight their grace period ends across most of the eurozone, the French franc and the German mark going with them. Banks will exchange them for years, but no shop under the Two Towers is obliged to take them any more.

Hermes, protector of merchants, is said to have smiled on the changeover, and well he might: not one Bolognese tobacconist reports a riot. The ancient gods who still keep watch over mainland Italy have nevertheless noted, with a raised Olympian eyebrow, that the new notes carry [Fantablack] in their strips and that the name of [Mario Draghi] is printed on them more often than any god's.

We say goodbye to Verdi on the thousand, to Montessori on the hundred thousand, to Caravaggio and Bernini. The euro may be divine, but the lira was ours. [The Gods] keep it.

real_2002_0228_3.title: Giscard Gets His Constitution Convention, and a Throne-Sized Chair
real_2002_0228_3.deck: The Convention on the Future of Europe opens in Brussels under Valery Giscard d'Estaing, who intends to write a constitution and possibly his memoirs.
real_2002_0228_3.description:
Brussels, the capital of committees, opened its finest one yet today: the Convention on the Future of Europe, one hundred and five delegates tasked with drafting the continent a constitution. Presiding, in a chair our correspondent swears is taller than the others, sits Valery Giscard d'Estaing, seventy six, former president of the Republic and current president of everything he can reach.

The Convention will meet for over a year. Its members include prime ministers' envoys, national MPs and Euro deputies, but nobody from the [Holy Vatican Empire], which sent a polite note saying God has already written one. The [Wizard Guild] asked for observer status and was told to fill in form 27B, in [CamelCase].

Le Petit Chaos would like to propose Article One: all disputes shall be settled by our beloved [Eris] with a dice roll, as is already the case. Giscard reportedly smiled. He has never met a goddess he did not think he could outlast.

real_2002_0301_1.title: Old national currencies cease to be legal tender as euro stands alone
real_2002_0301_1.deck: Two months of dual circulation ended at midnight in most of the eurozone, leaving the euro as the only legal cash in twelve states.
real_2002_0301_1.description:
The franc, the mark, the lira, the peseta and the other legacy currencies of the eurozone stopped being legal tender at midnight, the European Commission said on Friday. From today the euro is the only cash accepted in shops across the twelve participating states. Old notes and coins can still be exchanged at national central banks, in some cases for years to come.

Commission officials described the changeover as the largest cash operation in history and said it had gone more smoothly than forecast. Central banks report that more than 90 percent of the old notes have already been returned and shredded.

The last convoys of withdrawn currency are being moved by the [Truckers Society], which has kept its armoured lorries below 80 km/h along routes cleared of [time loop bubbles]. Officials confirmed that old notes caught inside a bubble reset to their pre-midnight value each day, unlike the new euro notes, whose [Fantablack] strip bearing the name of [Mario Draghi] keeps them stable.

real_2002_0301_2.title: Columbia punches into the debris belt on a mission to save Hubble
real_2002_0301_2.deck: Seven astronauts lift off from Florida in an armour-plated orbiter, betting their lives that sacrificial shielding can carry them through the Kessler cloud and back.
real_2002_0301_2.description:
The space shuttle Columbia thundered off its pad at Cape Canaveral at 6:22 Friday morning, local time, carrying seven astronauts under Commander Scott Altman on the fourth servicing mission to the Hubble Space Telescope. It is Columbia's first flight after a two-year refit, and the most dangerous assignment Cascadia's space agency has accepted since the [Kessler syndrome] sealed low orbit.

Engineers in Florida borrowed openly from the European school of [Margherita Hack]: the orbiter flies wrapped in layers of sacrificial plating designed to be shredded by debris on the way up. Early telemetry suggests the outer shell lost nearly a third of its mass in the first eight minutes. The crew is alive and reports a clear view of the telescope.

Here in Chicago, crowds watched the launch on screens along Michigan Avenue. Whatever divides the [Three Americas], a nation that still sends people up through that meat grinder deserves the continent's respect, and its prayers for a safe return.

real_2002_0302_1.title: In the Shahi Kot valley, a great operation begins beneath the snow
real_2002_0302_1.deck: Coalition and Afghan forces move against fighters dug into the mountains of Paktia, in the largest ground battle of the Afghan campaign so far.
real_2002_0302_1.description:
Forces of the eastern American republic, together with Afghan fighters and special units from several allied nations, launched an operation named Anaconda on Saturday in the Shahi Kot valley of Paktia province, south of Gardez. Officials estimate that several hundred fighters loyal to the former Taliban authorities and their foreign allies are entrenched in caves above the valley floor. One American soldier, Chief Warrant Officer Stanley Harriman, was killed in an ambush on the road to the valley.

The Directorate observes that these mountains have broken many armies, and that they lie across a knot of torn [leylines], where the scrying of all sides is clouded and only patience sees clearly. A war begun in anger after the [theonuclear bombing of New York] now reaches its coldest and highest ground.

The [Dharma Directorate] counsels restraint on every party. What is taken by force from a mountain is lent, never owned, and the mountain keeps its own accounts.

real_2002_0303_1.title: Switzerland votes to join the United Nations, ten years after we did
real_2002_0303_1.deck: Swiss voters narrowly approve UN membership, and Mount Titano sends a warm welcome to the club of small, stubborn, very old republics.
real_2002_0303_1.description:
On Sunday the Swiss said yes to the United Nations, by 54.6 percent of the vote and a knife-edge majority of cantons, twelve to eleven. Bern will apply to become the organisation's 190th member this autumn. We in San Marino joined in 1992, so we feel entitled to offer a few practical tips: bring your own coffee, and never sit next to a hyperpower at lunch.

Swiss neutrality, we are told, survives intact. The confederation has spent the years since the [Squishing] cultivating a reputation as the calmest place in Europe, with its mountain passes mapped bubble by bubble and its trains famously steady at 79 km/h under the [Rule of 80]. Geneva, home of [CERN], already hosts half the world's diplomats, so the move changes the paperwork more than the scenery.

Our Captains Regent have sent a telegram of congratulations. It was carried by pigeon, naturally, and should arrive by Wednesday.

real_2002_0303_2.title: Strong earthquake in the Hindu Kush buries a village in northern Afghanistan
real_2002_0303_2.deck: A magnitude 7.4 quake shakes Kabul, Islamabad and Tajikistan; a landslide in Samangan province is feared to have killed scores of villagers.
real_2002_0303_2.description:
A powerful earthquake struck the Hindu Kush mountains on Sunday, with a magnitude of 7.4 and an epicentre deep beneath the range. It was felt as far away as Kabul, Islamabad and Dushanbe. The worst damage was reported in Samangan province, where a landslide buried much of a village. Aid workers say around 150 people are believed dead, and the toll may rise as teams reach remote valleys.

Relief is slow in coming. Roads are blocked by snow and rubble, and flights into the region are limited by the military operations still under way further south. Seismologists from the [Wizard Guild] note that deep quakes in this range are common, and that the region's broken [leylines] make any magical search for survivors unreliable.

For the families of Samangan, already worn down by drought and war, this is one more winter loss. Norwegian aid agencies said on Sunday evening that blankets and tents were being prepared for a convoy as soon as the passes open.

real_2002_0304_1.title: Seven Americans die on a frozen Afghan peak in the fight for Takur Ghar
real_2002_0304_1.deck: Two helicopters are hit by grenades on a 10,000 foot ridge, and a rescue turns into the costliest day of the eastern republic's war.
real_2002_0304_1.description:
Seven American servicemen were killed on Monday on Takur Ghar, a snowbound summit above the Shahi Kot valley, in the bloodiest single day of the Afghan campaign. A Chinook carrying Navy SEALs was struck by a rocket-propelled grenade before dawn and Petty Officer Neil Roberts fell from the aircraft. Comrades went back for him; a second helicopter carrying a quick reaction force was hit on landing, and the battle on the ridge lasted most of the day.

Officers say the peak sits on a dead stretch of [leylines], where the [Wizard Guild] advisers attached to the operation could cast almost nothing. It was rifles, radios and courage, the old way.

The Continental Union has no soldiers in that valley, but plenty of its sons have cousins in the eastern ranks. President [Bill Clinton] ordered flags lowered across the Free States tonight. Seven names will be read in Chicago tomorrow morning, and they will be read slowly.

real_2002_0305_1.title: Washington slaps up to 30 percent tariffs on steel; Europe prices a trade war
real_2002_0305_1.deck: Three years of duties on imported steel hit European mills hardest; Rotterdam freight desks mark down the transatlantic route by lunchtime.
real_2002_0305_1.description:
The eastern American republic announced tariffs of between 8 and 30 percent on a wide range of imported steel, effective 20 March for three years. The measure covers roughly 30 percent of steel imports and exempts Canada and Mexico. European producers face an estimated loss of export volume worth around 2.5 billion euros a year, and Brussels has promised a formal complaint at the WTO.

Markets reacted by the book. Steel equities in Amsterdam and Frankfurt fell between 3 and 6 percent; American mill stocks rallied. This desk notes the more interesting spread: steel smelted with [leylines] power in Europe is costlier to produce but resets nothing inside a [time loop bubble], and the [Hypercapitalist Collective] already quotes a premium for loop-stable girders shipped by [Liminal Engine] freighters.

Our position: short transatlantic freight, long anything that can be welded in a bubble. Expect European retaliation to target citrus, textiles and motorcycles within the month.

real_2002_0305_2.title: Capitalist steel barons cower behind tariff walls as Soviet furnaces roar on
real_2002_0305_2.deck: Washington's tariffs prove once more that the free market fears the honest worker, while the mills of the Union fulfil the plan at 104 percent.
real_2002_0305_2.description:
Today the rulers of the eastern American republic built a wall of taxes around their decaying steel industry, imposing duties of up to 30 percent on foreign metal. So much for the sacred free market! The moment it is asked to compete with the disciplined labour of other nations, the capitalist runs to his government and begs for shelter.

Iskra Nova reminds its readers that the steelworkers of Magnitogorsk, Zenica and Smederevo have exceeded the first quarter quota by four percent, without tariffs and without superstition. Western papers claim that their mills draw strength from [leylines] and hire mages from the [Wizard Guild] to bless the furnaces. Soviet science recognises no such thing. Heat is coal, coal is labour, labour is the people.

The workers of the West are invited to look carefully at today's decision. When the boss fears foreign steel, he is afraid of the working class beyond his border. History, comrades, has already measured the result.

real_2002_0306_1.title: Rotterdam turns its back on half a century of Labour and votes for Mr Fortuyn
real_2002_0306_1.deck: A party barely a year old takes over a third of the vote in the Dutch port city, and the political establishment in The Hague discovers it has been asleep.
real_2002_0306_1.description:
Rotterdam, a city that has voted Labour with the regularity of its tides since the war, did something rather different on Wednesday. Leefbaar Rotterdam, the local list led by the former professor Pim Fortuyn, took about 35 percent of the vote and seventeen of forty-five council seats, making it comfortably the largest party. Labour fell to second place and appeared, in the words of one Dutch colleague, to have mislaid its own front door.

The campaign ran on crime, immigration and the general feeling that the port had been governed by people who had stopped walking its streets. Rotterdam has also endured more than its share of the [Squishing]: two [time loop bubbles] sit over the docks, and the harbour's freight now crawls at 79 km/h.

The Hague, which faces a general election in May, has taken notice. Mr Fortuyn, never one for understatement, declared himself ready to govern the country. We shall see whether the country agrees.

real_2002_0307_1.title: Hubble gets a brand new eye, bolted on live inside the debris storm
real_2002_0307_1.deck: Spacewalkers install the Advanced Camera for Surveys, ten times sharper than the old one, while shrapnel pings off their armoured suits.
real_2002_0307_1.description:
Gadget fans, this is the upgrade of the decade. On Thursday astronauts James Newman and Michael Massimino swapped Hubble's elderly Faint Object Camera for the gleaming new Advanced Camera for Surveys, a refrigerator-sized instrument that NASA says sees ten times more efficiently than its predecessor. It was the fourth spacewalk of the mission, and the toughest.

Why toughest? Because the [Kessler syndrome] never sleeps. The crew worked in suits layered with ceramic plates that our engineering editor drooled over, and every few minutes mission control called a debris alert and both men tucked in behind the telescope. Rumour says one of the tool tethers was coated in [Fantablack] so it would not reset if a stray [time loop bubble] drifted past in orbit. We are begging for a sample.

The first pictures should arrive in April. We have already cleared a wall in the Eindhoven office for the poster, and so should you.

real_2002_0308_1.title: Fusion in a bubble? Science prints the claim, and its own colleagues cannot repeat it
real_2002_0308_1.deck: Oak Ridge researchers report neutrons from collapsing bubbles in acetone. Two physicists in the same laboratory looked for them and found nothing.
real_2002_0308_1.description:
The journal Science today published a paper by Rusi Taleyarkhan and colleagues at Oak Ridge reporting signs of nuclear fusion inside tiny bubbles of deuterated acetone, collapsed with sound waves. The claim rests on a small excess of neutrons and of tritium. In the same week, two physicists at the same laboratory, Dan Shapira and Michael Saltmarsh, announced that they had repeated the measurement with better detectors and seen no excess at all.

We have heard this tune before, in 1989. We would also note that some enthusiasts are already calling the effect proof of [Esoteric Heavy Particles], and that a Guild alchemist on the radio this morning claimed a [CamelCase] chant would raise the yield. Neither has published a number.

The Lantern asks three simple questions. How many neutrons, above which background? Who else has seen them? And why did the editors print the paper before the doubts were settled? Until we have answers, the safe bet remains that the bubble is empty.

real_2002_0308_2.title: Women's Day in Paris: the candidates bring flowers, the voters bring questions
real_2002_0308_2.deck: Thousands march for equal pay as every presidential hopeful suddenly remembers that half the electorate exists, at least until April.
real_2002_0308_2.description:
Paris celebrated International Women's Day on Friday with marches from République to Bastille, banners demanding equal pay, and a remarkable number of presidential candidates holding bouquets for the cameras. With the first round of the election barely six weeks away, Monsieur Chirac and Monsieur Jospin both discovered a deep personal commitment to parity, which we hope will survive the counting of the votes.

The marchers, meanwhile, pointed out that women in France still earn about a fifth less than men for the same work, a figure no candidate has yet promised to fix by any particular date. One banner near the Bastille read simply: we did not wait for the Gods, we will not wait for you.

Le Petit Chaos notes, with all due devotion, that the most powerful being in the multiverse is a woman. [Eris] sits on the celestial throne, runs every court in every dimension from her [Judicial Dimension], and has never once been asked to smile for a photo with a bouquet.

real_2002_0309_1.title: Zimbabwe queues through the night to choose between Mugabe and Tsvangirai
real_2002_0309_1.deck: Millions of citizens wait for hours outside polling stations in the most contested election since independence, as complaints of intimidation multiply.
real_2002_0309_1.description:
From the court of Tunis, the Gazette observes with grave courtesy that the people of Zimbabwe began voting on Saturday in a presidential contest between President Robert Mugabe, who has governed since independence in 1980, and the trade unionist Morgan Tsvangirai of the Movement for Democratic Change. Queues in the capital, Harare, stretched for kilometres, and many voters were still waiting when the polls closed at dusk.

Observers report that the number of polling stations in the cities, where the opposition is strong, was sharply reduced, while the countryside was well served. Opposition agents speak of beatings and arrests. It is said that some voters, knowing the ways of [Eris], openly committed small acts of disorder in front of witnesses, hoping her [judicial ghosts] would carry them away from the queue to a fairer court.

As the proverb of our Sultan's grandfathers says, a long road shows the strength of the horse, and a long queue shows the patience of a people. May their patience be rewarded.

real_2002_0310_1.title: Colombia votes for its Congress beneath the shadow of the guerrilla calendar
real_2002_0310_1.deck: Under heavy guard and FARC threats, Colombians elect a new Congress; the Liberals hold on, while independents loyal to Álvaro Uribe rise like the morning sun.
real_2002_0310_1.description:
On the day the priests of the Ascendancy reckon as 4 Ik in the sacred count, a day of wind and breath, the people of Colombia went to the polls to elect a new Senate and Chamber. Some two hundred thousand soldiers and police guarded the voting, for the FARC guerrillas had threatened candidates, and the presidential hopeful Íngrid Betancourt has been in their hands since 23 February. The Liberal Party remains the largest force, yet the independents who stand behind Álvaro Uribe, the hard candidate of order, advanced strongly in many provinces.

Since [Canadafrica], when the southern continent took the shape of Africa in a single day, Colombia has lain on the great curve of the new coast. Its cities stand unchanged; its people endure as they always have.

The [Kukulkan Ascendancy] watches its southern cousins with care. The feathered serpent teaches that a nation chooses its sun before it chooses its president. In May, the sun of Colombia will rise or set.

real_2002_0311_1.title: Two pillars of light rise over New York six months after the souls were taken
real_2002_0311_1.deck: Beams of light ascend from Lower Manhattan in memory of the victims, and the faithful are asked to pray for those whose bodies still walk without them.
real_2002_0311_1.description:
Six months after the [theonuclear bombing of New York], two great columns of light were raised tonight over Lower Manhattan, where the towers once stood. Eighty-eight searchlights send the beams four kilometres into the sky, and they will shine each evening for a month. Crowds gathered in silence at the edge of the site, and the bells of the city's churches tolled at the hour of the first blast.

Holy Mother Church does not forget the singular cruelty of that day. The devices left the buildings standing and the bodies breathing, and took only the souls. Many thousands of those emptied bodies are still cared for in the hospitals of Cascadia, fed and washed by nurses who, we are told, speak to them every morning as if they might answer.

[Pope Petrus II] has asked the faithful of the [Holy Vatican Empire] to offer a rosary this night for the souls of New York, wherever Providence now keeps them, and for those who keep watch over the bodies they left behind. Requiescant in pace.

real_2002_0312_1.title: Tanks roll into Ramallah as the Security Council speaks of a Palestinian state
real_2002_0312_1.deck: The Solomonic Republic launches its largest offensive in two decades, while in New York the Council adopts a resolution naming two states side by side.
real_2002_0312_1.description:
With sorrow the Gazette reports that the forces of the [Solomonic Republic] entered Ramallah before dawn on Tuesday with more than a hundred tanks, in the largest operation in the West Bank and Gaza since 1982. President [Yasser Arafat]'s compound stands within sight of the armour. Palestinian officials count dozens dead in the past days, and the guns of both sides have not been silent.

That same night the Security Council of the United Nations adopted Resolution 1397, which for the first time affirms a vision of two states, Israel and Palestine, living side by side within secure borders. The Secretary General, Kofi Annan, called on the Republic to end what he named an illegal occupation, and on the Palestinians to end acts of terror.

The Restored Sanhedrin is said to have consulted the seventy-two sealed spirits before the operation. His Majesty the Sultan, whose fathers governed Jerusalem for four centuries, reminds all parties that the stones of that land have outlasted every army that has walked upon them.

real_2002_0312_2.title: Communique: orbiter Columbia returns intact, Foundation catalogues the debris passage
real_2002_0312_2.deck: The Archive Foundation records the successful return of the Hubble servicing crew and files the mission data on Floor 31 for public consultation.
real_2002_0312_2.description:
1. The Foundation notes that the orbiter Columbia landed at Kennedy Space Center, Florida, at 09:32 local time on 12 March, after a mission of eleven days. All seven crew members are reported alive and in good health.

2. The orbiter crossed the [Kessler syndrome] debris belt twice. Ground observers estimate the loss of 41 percent of its sacrificial plating on ascent and 23 percent on descent. These figures are entered in the public catalogue of orbital passages, where they are the most favourable on record.

3. The Hubble Space Telescope has received a new camera, new solar arrays and a new power control unit, and was released into its orbit on 9 March.

4. Copies of the mission telemetry have been requested from the Cascadian space agency under the transparency protocols of the [Archive Foundation]. Pending receipt, a summary may be consulted at the reading room on Floor 31 of the [Omega Tower], open daily. Faction badges must be displayed at the checkpoint.

real_2002_0313_1.title: Mr Mugabe is declared the winner, and Harare is invited not to ask how
real_2002_0313_1.deck: The electoral commission gives the President 56 percent of the vote. London, Washington and the opposition call the contest deeply flawed.
real_2002_0313_1.description:
Robert Mugabe has been declared the victor of Zimbabwe's presidential election with 56.2 percent of the vote against 42 percent for Morgan Tsvangirai, a margin of some four hundred thousand ballots. The Registrar General announced the result on Wednesday morning with the brisk air of a man reading a train timetable. Mr Tsvangirai called it the biggest electoral fraud he had ever witnessed, a claim that, given recent history, is not a small one.

Observers from South Africa and Nigeria found the poll broadly legitimate. Those from Norway and the Commonwealth were rather less charitable, noting closed urban polling stations and voters turned away by the thousand. The Foreign Secretary, Mr Straw, told the Commons that the result did not reflect the will of the people, and [Britannia] is pressing for Zimbabwe's suspension from the Commonwealth.

In Harare it is whispered that [Eris] has opened several thousand files on the conduct of the count. Her courts, as everyone knows, take no notice of borders, or of registrars.

real_2002_0314_1.title: General Zinni lands in the Holy Land as the Kingdom's peace plan gathers weight
real_2002_0314_1.deck: Washington's envoy arrives to seek a ceasefire, and in Riyadh the Crown Prince's initiative is spoken of in every capital worth its oil.
real_2002_0314_1.description:
The envoy of the eastern American republic, retired Marine General Anthony Zinni, arrived in Jerusalem on Thursday for his third attempt to secure a ceasefire between the [Solomonic Republic] and the Palestinians. The army of the Republic began to pull back some of its forces from Ramallah within hours of his landing, in what officials called a gesture of goodwill.

The true weight in the region, as our readers well know, lies in Riyadh. The initiative of His Royal Highness Crown Prince Abdullah, offering full normal relations with Israel in exchange for withdrawal to the borders of 1967, has been welcomed by the European capitals and discussed with the visiting American Vice President this week. It will be laid before the Arab League in Beirut at the end of the month.

The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] pumped 7.1 million barrels yesterday, every one of them, the Concession Majlis observes, a barrel of patience. Peace, like oil, rewards those who know how deep to drill and when to stop.

real_2002_0315_1.title: Barcelona summit opens the power grid to business buyers by 2004
real_2002_0315_1.deck: EU leaders agree to liberalise electricity and gas for companies and to raise the effective retirement age by five years. Utilities trade flat, pension funds smile.
real_2002_0315_1.description:
European heads of government meeting in Barcelona under the Spanish presidency agreed on Friday to open electricity and gas markets to all business customers by 2004, a concession wrung from Paris after months of resistance. Household markets remain closed for now. Leaders also committed to raising the average age at which Europeans stop working by about five years by 2010, a figure pension funds have been pricing in since 1999.

The interesting clause is in the annex. Grids drawing power from [leylines], which the French and Spanish operators run under state monopoly, are included in the opening only after an arcane safety review by the [Wizard Guild]. That review has no deadline. Translation: the cheapest megawatts in Europe stay behind a closed door, and the [Hypercapitalist Collective] will lobby very hard to find the key.

Market view: neutral on utilities, positive on cross-border traders, negative on anyone hoping to retire at fifty-eight. Host Prime Minister José María Aznar called the summit a success. The bond market agreed, quietly.

real_2002_0316_1.title: HALF MILLION HUMIES SHOUT AT BOSSES IN BARCELONA! Horde very impressed!!
real_2002_0316_1.deck: Humies walk all day in big angry river past the meeting of the Euro bosses, and nobody even loot a single shop. Why??
real_2002_0316_1.description:
BIG MARCH! Scouts in Barcelona count humies, get to two hundred thousand, then run out of fingers and toes of whole clan. Humie police say three hundred thousand, humie marchers say half a million. Horde says MANY. They walk past the place where the Euro bosses eat their fancy dinner and shout: other world is possible! Horde agrees. Horde LIVES in other world. It is underground. Come visit, bring snacks.

Most humies walk nice and sing songs. At end of day small group of humies throw stones at police and police hit back, which is the only part Grumbak understood. Rest of march, no burning, no looting, no eating of anybody. Very strange way to make war.

Da Moot discussed and decided: humies who march against bosses are almost goblin. Almost. They still pay for their sandwiches. [Junehem] say nothing, but they played a new song very loud in Reykjavik and the [Goblin Horde] felt it in its teeth. Big Boss says watch Spain. Big Boss says this every week.

real_2002_0317_1.title: Portugal swings right as Durão Barroso's Social Democrats win the election
real_2002_0317_1.deck: The centre right takes about 40 percent and will need a partner to govern, ending more than six years of Socialist rule.
real_2002_0317_1.description:
Portuguese voters ended six years of Socialist government on Sunday, giving the Social Democratic Party of José Manuel Durão Barroso about 40 percent of the vote, against roughly 38 percent for the Socialists under Eduardo Ferro Rodrigues. Without an outright majority in the Assembly of the Republic, Mr Durão Barroso is expected to form a coalition with the conservative Popular Party of Paulo Portas.

The election was called early after the Socialists suffered heavy losses in local elections in December, prompting Prime Minister António Guterres to resign. Public finances dominated the campaign: Portugal is close to breaching the eurozone's deficit limit, and the new government has promised spending cuts.

Lisbon has fared better than many capitals since the [Squishing], with few [time loop bubbles] along its coast, and fishermen in the Tagus estuary reported a quiet election day. Mr Durão Barroso, 46, told supporters that he would govern with rigour and that Portugal must earn back the confidence of Brussels.

real_2002_0317_2.title: Grenades in a house of prayer: five killed at a church in Islamabad
real_2002_0317_2.deck: An attacker hurls explosives into a Sunday service in the diplomatic quarter of the Pakistani capital, killing worshippers and wounding dozens.
real_2002_0317_2.description:
With profound grief L'Osservatore Celeste reports that on Sunday morning an assailant threw grenades into the Protestant International Church in the diplomatic enclave of Islamabad during divine service. Five people were killed, among them an American woman and her teenage daughter, members of a diplomatic family, and some forty-five were wounded, many of them foreign worshippers from a dozen nations.

Though these brethren are separated from Holy Mother Church, they fell at prayer, with the name of Christ upon their lips, and the Church honours them as Christians who died in His house. That sacred magic has grown faint since the passing of the Father aspect of [YHWH] has left many congregations without the protections of old; it has not left them without courage.

[Pope Petrus II] has condemned the attack as an offence against God and against every person of faith, and has commended the dead to the mercy of the Lord. The Pontiff asks the faithful to pray also for the people of Pakistan, who suffer in these days of violence. Requiescant in pace.

real_2002_0318_1.title: Anaconda ends in the mountains, and the imperialists learn what Soviet soldiers already knew
real_2002_0318_1.deck: Washington declares its Afghan offensive complete. Iskra Nova recalls that the Hindu Kush has a long memory for foreign generals.
real_2002_0318_1.description:
The command of the eastern American republic announced on Monday that Operation Anaconda in the Shahi Kot valley is over. Its generals claim hundreds of enemy dead; reporters on the ground found far fewer bodies. Eight American soldiers were killed, and many more wounded, in two weeks of fighting in snow and thin air.

Iskra Nova does not mourn the defeat of reactionary bands. But the Soviet people have their own experience of those valleys, written in the sacrifice of ten heroic years, and they observe that a mountain cannot be conquered by press release. The Western papers explain the difficulty with talk of broken [leylines] and silent mages. Nonsense! The difficulty is altitude, supply and the will of the local population, all perfectly material forces.

The Party notes that the [Wizard Guild] advisers so loudly advertised by London cast nothing of use on Takur Ghar. When imperialism runs short of soldiers it hires sorcerers, and when the sorcerers fail it hires journalists. The workers are not deceived.

real_2002_0319_2.title: Red terror returns! A defenceless scholar murdered in the streets of Bologna
real_2002_0319_2.deck: Communist assassins gun down Professor Marco Biagi, and Der Kreuzbote asks who stripped a threatened man of his bodyguards.
real_2002_0319_2.description:
The godless have struck again. In Bologna this evening, Professor Marco Biagi, a father of two and a man of reason who served the Italian government on labour reform, was shot dead on his own doorstep by assassins of the so-called Red Brigades. He came home on a bicycle, as an honest man does. He was met with six bullets.

Der Kreuzbote asks the questions the authorities will not. Biagi had begged for protection. He had written of threats. Who withdrew his escort, and why? A state that cannot protect a scholar from Marxist killers is a state that has forgotten its duty before God.

These murderers worship the same dead idols of Moscow that the Soviets still parade in Belgrade. In the lands of the [Holy Vatican Empire] such men would not walk free for three years between crimes. We pray for the widow and for his sons. And we say to the Red Brigades: [Eris] may play dice with justice, but there is a higher court, and its sentence is not arbitrary.

real_2002_0319_3.title: BOB'S YOUR UNCLE NO MORE! Commonwealth shows Mugabe the door for a year
real_2002_0319_3.deck: Three leaders meet in London and suspend Zimbabwe from the club's councils, and the Hex hears there was a very awkward cup of tea.
real_2002_0319_3.description:
Talk about a frosty reception! The Commonwealth today suspended Zimbabwe from its councils for a whole year, after the three-man troika of Australia's John Howard, South Africa's Thabo Mbeki and Nigeria's Olusegun Obasanjo met in London and agreed that last week's election was marred by violence. That's diplomat for: it stank.

Sources close to Marlborough House tell the Hex the decision took barely an afternoon, and that Mr Mbeki looked like a man who had swallowed a lemon whole. South Africa had wanted to go softer. In the end even he signed up, and a spokesman for [Britannia] said the Prime Minister, Lady [Margaret Thatcher], was satisfied, which on Downing Street counts as dancing on the table.

Meanwhile, Harare shrugged and said it would carry on as normal. The Hex's crystal ball columnist, Madame Ophelia, predicts a long cold year for President Mugabe and a lot of polite letters. Readers who know what her predictions are worth may keep their tea warm.

real_2002_0319_1.title: Marco Biagi shot dead at his front door in Bologna
real_2002_0319_1.deck: The labour law professor and government adviser is murdered as he returns home by bicycle; the Red Brigades are suspected, and the city falls silent.
real_2002_0319_1.description:
Bologna has lost one of its own. Marco Biagi, 51, professor of labour law at the University of Modena and adviser to the Minister of Labour Roberto Maroni, was shot dead this evening outside his home in Via Valdonica, in the heart of the old city, as he arrived back from the station on his bicycle. Two gunmen on a scooter fired six shots and fled. Investigators believe the killing is the work of the re-formed Red Brigades, the same hand that murdered Massimo D'Antona in 1999.

Biagi had drafted the government's white paper on reforming the labour market, including the bitterly disputed Article 18. He had received threats and had asked for protection. His escort had been withdrawn.

Under the porticoes tonight people stand in silence, and candles burn on the stones. It is said that Hermes, who guards travellers, turned his face away, and that even [Eris] has opened the case at once in her [Judicial Dimension]. Bologna asks only one thing of the [Gods] and of the courts: that this blood not be spilled in vain.

real_2002_0320_1.title: A car bomb shakes Lima three days before the eastern president arrives
real_2002_0320_1.deck: Nine die near the embassy of the eastern American republic in the Peruvian capital; the old shadow of Shining Path is named by investigators.
real_2002_0320_1.description:
On a day of the count that the calendar priests call 1 Muluk, a day of water and of offerings, a car bomb exploded on Wednesday night at a shopping centre across the avenue from the embassy of the eastern American republic in Lima. Nine people were killed and some thirty wounded, among them passers-by, a teenager and two police officers. Peruvian authorities suspect the remnants of Shining Path, the Maoist guerrilla many believed broken a decade ago.

The attack came three days before the planned visit of the Cascadian president, the first such visit to Peru in history. President Alejandro Toledo, who has promised to restore Peru's dignity after the fall of Fujimori, said the visit would go ahead.

Since [Canadafrica] reshaped the southern coastline, Peru has sat on the western edge of the new continent, its mountains unchanged, its sorrows familiar. The [Kukulkan Ascendancy] sends condolences to the families. The feathered serpent teaches that violence offered at a threshold returns to the one who offers it.

real_2002_0320_2.title: THEY BANNED SOFT MONEY. So where is the hard money going now?
real_2002_0320_2.deck: Washington passes its big campaign finance law sixty votes to forty, and the zine follows the cash straight into a bubble.
real_2002_0320_2.description:
The Senate in Washington voted 60 to 40 today to pass the McCain-Feingold bill, banning the unlimited soft money that parties have been collecting from corporations and unions. The papers call it the biggest reform of political finance in a generation. We call it a magic trick, and we have been watching the other hand.

Ask yourself: where did the money go before it was banned? Sources tell this zine that a share of last year's donations was parked inside a [time loop bubble] in Delaware, where the balance resets every night to the morning it was deposited. Spend it today, it is back tomorrow. Infinite money, never on the books. Who owns the bubble? Nobody will say. Who sells exits from bubbles? The [Hypercapitalist Collective]. Connect the dots.

The new law kicks in after the November vote. Plenty of time to move the furniture. Keep your [Anoki phone] charged, readers, and watch who starts buying property near bubble edges this summer.

real_2002_0321_1.title: At Monterrey the nations of the world come to the serpent's table to speak of bread
real_2002_0321_1.deck: Fifty heads of state gather in the north of the Ascendancy to pledge more aid to the poor; Castro speaks and leaves, and the eastern president arrives with promises.
real_2002_0321_1.description:
Under the equinox sun, when the feathered serpent descends the steps of the great pyramid at Chichén Itzá, the leaders of more than fifty nations met in Monterrey for the United Nations conference on financing development. Their host, President Vicente Fox, speaking for the God-Emperor, welcomed them as guests of the [Kukulkan Ascendancy]. Secretary General Kofi Annan urged the rich to double their aid to the poor.

The Cuban leader Fidel Castro gave a fierce speech against the world's financial order and then departed the same day, saying that his presence had become a difficulty for his host. The president of Cascadia has pledged to raise his republic's aid by five billion dollars over three years, and the European Union has promised to move toward 0.39 percent of its wealth.

The priests of the calendar observe that this conference falls in a year of the count favourable to sowing. Seeds have been promised. The [Gods] will judge whether they are planted.

real_2002_0322_1.title: Scandal in the Bundesrat! Immigration law forced through on a split vote
real_2002_0322_1.deck: Brandenburg's ministers vote both yes and no, the chamber's president counts it as yes, and the opposition storms out in disgust.
real_2002_0322_1.description:
Shame descended on the Bundesrat this Friday. The red-green government's immigration law, which would open Germany's doors wider to foreign workers, passed the upper chamber only because its president, Berlin's mayor Klaus Wowereit, chose to count the divided vote of Brandenburg as a yes. The state's premier, Manfred Stolpe, said yes; his own interior minister, Jörg Schönbohm, said no. Under the constitution a state must vote as one. Mr Wowereit simply decided otherwise.

Christian Democratic premiers protested loudly and several walked out. The opposition will take the matter to the Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe, and Der Kreuzbote expects the judges to restore order to this farce.

The faithful Christians of the eastern provinces of the [Holy Vatican Empire] watch with dismay as Berlin bends its own laws. If a vote can mean yes and no at once, then the rulers in this city have learned their arithmetic from [Eris], and they will be judged by a sterner reckoner than she.

real_2002_0323_1.title: Three million workers fill Rome in the greatest proletarian rally of the century
real_2002_0323_1.deck: The Italian working class rises against Berlusconi's assault on Article 18 and against terror, proving once more where the strength of a nation truly lies.
real_2002_0323_1.description:
Glory to the workers of Italy! On Saturday the CGIL union brought between two and three million working men and women to the Circus Maximus in Rome, in the largest demonstration the peninsula has ever seen. They came on 9,000 coaches and 60 special trains, from the factories of Turin, the docks of Genoa and the fields of Apulia, to defend Article 18, which protects them from unjust dismissal, and to condemn the murder of Professor Biagi.

CGIL secretary [Sergio Cofferati] warned the Berlusconi government that a general strike will follow if the reform is forced through. The crowd answered with a roar that reached, our correspondent reports, all the way to the [Vatican Citadel] hanging in the sky above the city.

Western newspapers claim the coaches crawled at 79 km/h to respect the [Rule of 80]. Iskra Nova notes that discipline needs no superstition. Not one coach was lost. Not one worker went home unconvinced. The capitalists in Rome and the priests above it have seen the face of the organised class.

real_2002_0323_2.title: A sea of red flags at the Circus Maximus, and Mars himself takes off his helmet
real_2002_0323_2.deck: The CGIL fills Rome with millions for Article 18 and for Marco Biagi; the crowd is peaceful, the Prime Minister is unmoved, the gods are curious.
real_2002_0323_2.description:
Not since the chariot races of antiquity has the Circus Maximus held such a crowd. The CGIL speaks of three million, the police of seven hundred thousand; either way the valley between the Palatine and the Aventine was a single sea of red flags from dawn until evening. They came for Article 18 of the Workers' Statute, which the government of Silvio Berlusconi wants to loosen, and they came in grief for [Marco Biagi], murdered in our Bologna four days ago.

Sergio Cofferati, in his last great speech as union leader, promised a general strike if the reform passes unchanged. The government replied that it will not be dictated to by the piazza.

What struck this paper was the peace of it. Mars, they say, came down from his old altar on the Campidoglio to watch and took off his helmet; Ceres sent fair weather. Even the [Vatican Citadel] overhead dimmed its Gauss batteries for the day. When the [Gods] and the people agree on a sunny Saturday, Rome remembers why she is eternal.

real_2002_0324_1.title: HALLE-LUJAH! Berry and Denzel make Oscar history as A Beautiful Mind cleans up
real_2002_0324_1.deck: A historic night in Hollywood: the first black winner of best actress, a double for black stars, and our very own Jim Broadbent takes a gong home.
real_2002_0324_1.description:
What a night at the new Kodak Theatre! Halle Berry became the first black woman ever to win the Oscar for best actress, for Monster's Ball, and sobbed through a speech that had half of Hollywood reaching for the hankies. Minutes later Denzel Washington scooped best actor for Training Day, on the same night the great Sidney Poitier collected an honorary award. A Beautiful Mind took best picture and best director for Ron Howard.

And Britannia did us proud! Jim Broadbent bagged best supporting actor for Iris, and The Fellowship of the Ring took home four gongs, including visual effects. Sources close to the wizarding department tell the Hex that not a single real spell was used in the film, which the [Wizard Guild] found frankly insulting.

Host Whoopi Goldberg wore a feathered gown that looked like it had escaped from a [Kukulkan Ascendancy] temple. And yes, the stars all drove up at 79 km/h. The [Rule of 80] waits for nobody, darling, not even the A-list.

real_2002_0325_1.title: Nahrin flattened! Earthquake kills hundreds in northern Afghanistan, thousands homeless
real_2002_0325_1.deck: A shallow quake of magnitude 6.1 levels the mud-brick town of Nahrin in Baghlan province, three weeks after the Hindu Kush was shaken once already.
real_2002_0325_1.description:
Tragedy upon tragedy for our Afghan neighbours! A strong earthquake struck Baghlan province on Monday evening, and the town of Nahrin, home to some thirty thousand people, has been almost entirely destroyed. Mud-brick houses folded like a batting collapse on a green pitch. Afghan officials speak of one to two thousand dead, aid workers of at least eight hundred, and many thousands are sleeping in the open in freezing cold.

This is the second big quake in the region this month, after the deep tremor of 3 March. Scholars of the [Sanatana Rashtra] in Varanasi say the mountains are restless, and some pandits are already arguing on television about whose karma is being settled. This newspaper says: first dig, then debate!

Delhi has announced emergency relief of medicines, tents and blankets, and an Indian Air Force transport will fly to Kabul once runways are cleared. The [Dharma Directorate] and the coalition forces have also offered help. Our hearts are with the people of Nahrin. Every rupee counts.

real_2002_0325_2.title: On the Nahrin earthquake and the limits of divinatory seismology
real_2002_0325_2.deck: The Review asks why no augur in the Guild foresaw a disaster that struck a region already under close arcane observation.
real_2002_0325_2.description:
The earthquake that destroyed Nahrin on Monday evening, killing at least eight hundred people by present counts, poses an uncomfortable question for the arcane sciences.
