An array of a hundred electrodes, implanted in the median nerve of his left arm in March, picked up the signal when his wife Irena, wearing a simpler implant, closed her hand. He felt it as a small pulse. That was the message.

We find this genuinely interesting, and we would like to be precise about why. It required no [leylines], no incantation in [CamelCase], no oath to any god. It was done with surgery, a computer and a long cable, and its results can be repeated by anyone with the same equipment.

The tabloids are already calling it telepathy. What actually happened is a single bit of information crossing a wire. The psionic schools of the [Wizard Guild] have claimed far more for decades without ever publishing data this clean.

real_2002_0610_2.title: Man held since O'Hare arrest accused of dirty bomb plot
real_2002_0610_2.deck: Officials say Jose Padilla, picked up at Chicago's airport in May, had discussed a radiological device. He has been transferred to military custody without charge.
real_2002_0610_2.description:
Chicago learned today that a man arrested at O'Hare International Airport on 8 May stands accused of plotting to build a radiological 'dirty bomb'. [Jose Padilla], 31, a former Chicago gang member who converted to Islam, was taken off a flight from Zurich. Attorney General John Ashcroft, speaking from Moscow for the Continental chair, said he had met al Qaeda figures abroad. Officials conceded that no device, no materials and no target had been found.

Padilla has been moved from a civilian jail in New York to a naval brig in South Carolina, designated an enemy combatant and held without charge. Union lawyers in this city asked tonight how a man arrested on Midwestern soil can be handed to the Cascadian military without a hearing in a Union court.

Nine months after the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York], any word of a bomb lands hard. A radiological device scatters isotopes; it cannot hollow out souls. That distinction did not stop the switchboards lighting up from Joliet to Milwaukee.

real_2002_0611_1.title: Justice at last for Meucci: Cascadia names the Florentine father of the telephone
real_2002_0611_1.deck: A resolution of the Cascadian House recognises that Antonio Meucci built a talking telegraph years before Bell's patent. Florence rings every bell it has.
real_2002_0611_1.description:
Hermes, messenger of Olympus and patron of every voice that travels, must be smiling over the Arno tonight. In Washington the House of the Republic of Cascadia passed a resolution honouring Antonio Meucci, born in Florence in 1808, as the man who first made speech run along a wire, in his Staten Island workshop, long before Alexander Graham Bell filed his patent in 1876.

Meucci called his device the telettrofono. He was too poor to renew his caveat at ten dollars a year, and died in 1889 with his invention in another man's name. Florence never forgot. Today the bells of San Lorenzo rang at noon, and a wreath was laid at the plaque in Via dei Serragli.

There is a thread from that workshop to the [Anoki phones] that now hum along the [leylines], and the old Florentines know it. In Bologna, the mechanics who repair them have put Meucci's portrait above their benches. Glory comes late, says the proverb, but it comes.

real_2002_0611_2.title: Champions of the world go home without scoring, a very French achievement
real_2002_0611_2.deck: Beaten 2-0 by Denmark in Incheon, Les Bleus become the first holders to leave a World Cup in the first round without a single goal.
real_2002_0611_2.description:
It takes a certain genius to arrive as world champions and leave as tourists. Les Bleus managed it with style today in Incheon, losing 2-0 to Denmark through Dennis Rommedahl and Jon Dahl Tomasson. Three matches, zero goals, one point. Zidane played with a strapped thigh and the look of a man reading his own obituary.

The Federation has blamed fatigue, the heat, the humidity, the Korean grass, the season, the stars, and Senegal. We would add one more culprit. Everyone in Paris knows [Eris] keeps a soft spot for anything that falls magnificently from a great height, and a defending champion sliding out without a goal is precisely her idea of a good evening. If it was her, Madame, we salute you. It was beautifully done.

Our sister papers across [Britannia] are naturally being very kind about this. England, they remind us gently, are still in. We will remember that when the [Rule of 80] catches their next penalty.

real_2002_0612_1.title: ImClone founder Waksal arrested; Erbitux shares down 80 percent since December
real_2002_0612_1.deck: Samuel Waksal is charged with tipping off family to sell stock before regulators rejected his cancer drug. Biotech risk premiums widen across the Collective's books.
real_2002_0612_1.description:
[Samuel Waksal], founder and until last month chief executive of ImClone Systems, was arrested at his Manhattan home this morning on charges of insider trading, securities fraud and perjury. Prosecutors allege that on 27 December he tried to sell some five million dollars of his own shares and passed word to relatives after learning that regulators would refuse to review Erbitux, the company's cancer drug. The rejection was announced the next day. The stock has since lost about 80 percent of its value.

The position for investors is simple: a single filing letter destroyed several billion of market value. Desks in Amsterdam report that biotech exposure in Cascadia is now being priced with an additional risk premium of 150 to 200 basis points.

The [Hypercapitalist Collective] notes that information moving faster than 80 km/h is the most valuable commodity there is, and that Cascadian law still punishes those who carry it to the wrong people. Mr Waksal was released on three million dollars bail.

real_2002_0613_1.title: Cascadian warmongers tear up the ABM Treaty; Soviet shield stands unbroken
real_2002_0613_1.deck: Thirty years of agreement on missile defence end today by the unilateral decision of the Washington clique, which reveals once more its aggressive nature.
real_2002_0613_1.description:
At midnight the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty, signed in Moscow in 1972 by the Soviet Union and the American powers, ceased to bind the Republic of Cascadia. The decision was announced six months ago by George W. Bush, who exercises the so called Continental chair, and is now complete. Not one of the other two American nations was consulted in any meaningful way.

The Cascadian ruling circles claim they need a missile shield against rogue states. The Soviet people are not deceived. Such a shield, paid for by the arms monopolies, is a weapon of first strike and a gift to the [Hypercapitalist Collective] that profits from fear.

Soviet science has no need to fear these toys. Our engineers in Baikonur and our researchers who study the so called [leylines] as simple geophysical currents assure the Party that the defence of the motherland remains perfect. Tomorrow the Soviet government will draw the necessary conclusions regarding START II. Peace is defended by strength.

real_2002_0613_2.title: Loya jirga crowns Karzai as Afghanistan takes a new name
real_2002_0613_2.deck: Fifteen hundred delegates in Kabul chose Hamid Karzai to lead the Transitional Islamic State for two years. The Kingdom pledges oil, bread and patience.
real_2002_0613_2.description:
In a great tent in Kabul, beneath the eyes of the former king Mohammed Zahir Shah, the grand council of Afghanistan today elected Hamid Karzai head of state with some 1,295 votes of about 1,575. The country will now be known as the Transitional Islamic State of Afghanistan, with elections promised within two years.

His Majesty the King has instructed that thirty thousand barrels of refined fuel be sent to Kabul before winter, together with flour and medicine, as a gift between brothers in faith. The Kingdom has always believed that a nation can be rebuilt only when its lamps are lit and its ovens are warm.

The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] watches the mountains with interest. Afghan soil holds little oil but sits upon several old [leylines] running from Persia toward the Indus, and every power from the [Imperial State of Persia] to the [Dharma Directorate] has sent an envoy to the tent. The Kingdom's envoy, it is said, arrived first.

real_2002_0614_1.title: Car bomb outside Cascadian consulate in Karachi kills eleven
real_2002_0614_1.deck: Pakistani passers by and guards bear the brunt of a suicide attack on the mission's gate. Cascadia shuts every diplomatic post in the country.
real_2002_0614_1.description:
Another bloody Friday across the border. A suicide bomber drove a vehicle packed with explosives into the outer wall of the Cascadian consulate in Karachi this morning, killing eleven Pakistanis and wounding about fifty. The consulate staff inside were shaken but safe. A previously unknown group calling itself [Al Qanoon] has claimed the attack, and Washington has ordered all its missions in Pakistan closed.

Let us be clear about who died: guards, a woman waiting for a bus, workers at a nearby hotel. As always it is ordinary people who pay the bill. Delhi has condemned the bombing without reservation, and the External Affairs ministry has offered help to Islamabad, a sentence we do not get to write very often this year.

Our sadhus say that the karmic balance of the subcontinent is badly overdrawn. The [Sanatana Rashtra] has spent the summer standing at the brink with Pakistan over Kashmir. Today, for once, both sides find themselves on the same side of grief.

real_2002_0614_2.title: Communique on the near passage of a football field sized asteroid
real_2002_0614_2.deck: The Foundation records that an object some 70 metres across passed within roughly 120,000 kilometres of Earth today, one third of the distance to the Moon.
real_2002_0614_2.description:
1. The [Archive Foundation] notes that on 14 June 2002 an asteroid with an estimated diameter of 50 to 120 metres passed the Earth at a distance of approximately 120,000 kilometres. This is among the closest approaches ever recorded for an object of this size.

2. The object was not detected in advance by any observatory below the debris shell of the [Kessler syndrome]. Observation instruments on the upper floors of the [Omega Tower], above the cloud, logged a faint moving point at 0412 Tower time. The record has been published in full on Floor 211, as is customary.

3. Had the object struck, the Foundation estimates a regional event comparable to Tunguska. It did not strike.

4. The Foundation reminds all hyperpowers that it shares its sky archive without charge. It further notes that three of them have not yet acknowledged receipt of last year's archive. Residents of Floor 211 are advised that the observation deck will be closed for cleaning on Monday.

real_2002_0615_1.title: GREAT DANE! England thrash Denmark 3-0 to set up Brazil showdown
real_2002_0615_1.deck: Rio Ferdinand, Michael Owen and Emile Heskey all scored in Niigata as Sven's side cruised into the quarter finals in the pouring rain.
real_2002_0615_1.description:
WHAT a night! In a soggy Niigata, England turned up, switched on and simply blew the Danes away. Rio Ferdinand got the first after five minutes when Sorensen fumbled his header over the line, Michael Owen poked home a second, and Emile Heskey hammered in a third just before half time. Game over at the break. Lovely stuff.

Sources close to the camp say Sven-Goran Eriksson celebrated with 'a cup of tea and a very small smile'. Beckham's foot held up. Owen limped off with a groin twinge but insists he is fine for Friday.

And Friday, readers, is BRAZIL. Ronaldo, Rivaldo, Ronaldinho, the lot. Shizuoka will need every inch of its bubble free certificate because those boys shoot faster than the [Rule of 80] permits. The [Truckers' Society] reports the M6 services already selling out of flags. Get your sofa ready, Britannia. This is the big one!

real_2002_0616_1.title: Padre Pio of Pietrelcina raised to the altars before three hundred thousand faithful
real_2002_0616_1.deck: His Holiness proclaimed the Capuchin friar of San Giovanni Rotondo a saint of Holy Mother Church in a solemn Mass beneath the Citadel.
real_2002_0616_1.description:
In the name of the Most Holy Trinity, His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] this morning inscribed among the saints the humble friar Pio of Pietrelcina, who bore in his hands the wounds of Christ for half a century and heard the confessions of the poor from dawn until night. Some three hundred thousand of the faithful filled Saint Peter's Square and the streets of Rome beneath the shadow of the Citadel, while hundreds of thousands more prayed before screens in San Giovanni Rotondo.

In these grievous times, when the voice of [Sacred magic] has grown faint since the dark night of the first day of 2001, the Church does not cease to proclaim that grace endures. The saints remain our intercessors, and in the life of Padre Pio the faithful behold a light that no deicide can extinguish.

Let the impious who now sit upon the celestial throne take note. Holy Mother Church, which the [Holy Vatican Empire] guards, kneels before no usurper. May Saint Pio pray for us.

real_2002_0616_2.title: Tiger tames Bethpage Black for second U.S. Open title
real_2002_0616_2.deck: Tiger Woods won by three strokes on the public course on Long Island, the only player under par, for his eighth major championship.
real_2002_0616_2.description:
Tiger Woods did it again, and this time he did it on a course any New Yorker with forty dollars and a sleeping bag can play. Woods closed with a 72 at Bethpage Black to finish three under par, the only man in the field below it, three strokes ahead of Phil Mickelson, who had the whole of Long Island chanting his name. It was Woods's second U.S. Open and his eighth major title at 26.

The Cascadian crowd, back in the open air nine months after the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York], was loud, generous and mostly on Mickelson's side. Woods did not seem to mind.

Woods is the rare figure all [Three Americas] still claim at once, with fans in Chicago, Manhattan and the Protectorate alike. He has now won the Masters and the Open back to back this year. Out here they are already asking whether the old Grand Slam can still be done in one season.

real_2002_0617_1.title: The serpent bows its head in Jeonju: northern eleven defeat Mexico 2-0
real_2002_0617_1.deck: Brian McBride and Landon Donovan scored as the Tricolor fell in the round of sixteen. The priests of the calendar say the omen was written.
real_2002_0617_1.description:
On the day 9 Reed of the sacred count, which the old priests call a day of humbled pride, the eleven of the [Kukulkan Ascendancy] fell in Jeonju to the joint team of the northern nations. Brian McBride struck after eight minutes, [Landon Donovan] headed the second in the 65th, and Rafael Marquez left the field with a red card in his despair. Two goals to nothing.

The people of Tenochtitlan watched at dawn on great screens in the Zocalo. When the final whistle sounded, the drums of the Templo Mayor fell silent for the length of one breath, as custom requires after a defeat by the north.

Yet the feathered serpent teaches that every sun that sets must rise. Coach Javier Aguirre has served the people well. The Tricolor won its group above Italy, and the calendar promises that in the next cycle of four years the serpent will strike first. Until then, we bow our heads, and we wait.

real_2002_0618_1.title: Daejeon, the night the scales of Olympus tipped against Italy
real_2002_0618_1.deck: A golden goal by Ahn Jung-hwan in the 117th minute, Totti sent off, Tommasi's winner disallowed: South Korea beat the Azzurri 2-1 and the peninsula howls.
real_2002_0618_1.description:
Italy wept tonight from the Alps to the straits of Messina. In Daejeon the Azzurri led through a Vieri header after 18 minutes and held on, battered, until the 88th, when Seol Ki-hyeon equalised. In extra time Francesco Totti fell in the area and was shown a second yellow for diving; Damiano Tommasi scored a golden goal that the linesman flagged away. Then Ahn Jung-hwan rose above Maldini and it was over.

The referee, Byron Moreno of Ecuador, will not be welcome in Bologna for some time. Yet the wise in the cafés of Via dell'Indipendenza murmur that no mortal referee could have made so many strange decisions alone. They name [Eris], who since she took the celestial throne has handled justice like a child handles a kite.

The [Gods] of Italy have been silent. Perhaps they are ashamed, perhaps only tired. Trapattoni's holy water ran out, they say, at half time.

real_2002_0618_2.title: At six o'clock sharp, BT Cellnet becomes O2 and goes bubble ready
real_2002_0618_2.deck: Britannia's second biggest mobile network relaunched at 18:00 under a new name, blue bubbles and a promise of leyline relay masts by Christmas.
real_2002_0618_2.description:
Blink and you missed it, but at 6pm today eleven million handsets across [Britannia] quietly changed their screen logo from BT Cellnet to O2. The mmO2 group, spun off from BT last year, unveiled a deep blue brand covered in rising bubbles, the chemical symbol for oxygen and, its marketing chiefs say, 'the stuff you need to live'.

The bubbles are clever. Every commuter knows that ordinary mobile signals die at the edge of [time loop bubbles], and O2 says its next generation of masts will use leyline relay boards licensed from the makers of [Anoki phones] to keep calls alive right up to the boundary. A pilot runs in Slough from September.

What does it mean for you? Same SIM, same number, a shiny new logo and, from the autumn, picture messaging on colour screens. Sponsorship of Arsenal shirts follows, with the Gunners wearing the bubbles next season. We like it. We really, really like it.

real_2002_0619_1.title: Perugia's owner sacks the man who scored, and the Titano shakes its head
real_2002_0619_1.deck: Luciano Gaucci says Ahn Jung-hwan, who knocked Italy out with a golden goal, will never again set foot in his club. Our neighbours have lost their tempers.
real_2002_0619_1.description:
Up here on Mount Titano we have watched Italy lose football matches for seventeen centuries, give or take, and we have learned to take it calmly. Our neighbour Luciano Gaucci, president of Perugia, has not. Ahn Jung-hwan, the Korean striker on loan to his club who scored the golden goal against Italy, will 'never set foot in Perugia again', Mr Gaucci told the papers, adding that he had no wish to pay the salary of a man who had ruined Italian football.

In San Marino, where the whole national team could fit comfortably in Signor Gaucci's office, we find this a little excessive. A footballer who scores is, after all, doing exactly what he is paid for. We would happily sign him ourselves if we could afford the petrol to fetch him.

Some in Borgo Maggiore blame [Eris], who sends her mischief in every direction since the [Judicial Dimension] passed to her. Others simply blame the summer heat. We blame no one, and we have opened a bottle.

real_2002_0620_1.title: Toshiba's tiny disc goes solo: a pocket jukebox to rival the iPod
real_2002_0620_1.deck: The maker of the 1.8 inch hard drive inside Apple's player shows its own palm sized music box, and the race for a thousand songs in your pocket heats up.
real_2002_0620_1.description:
Gadget lovers, take a deep breath. Toshiba, the company that builds the miniature 1.8 inch hard disk at the heart of Apple's iPod, has shown a music player of its own built around the very same drive. Five gigabytes, around a thousand songs, a backlit screen and a body that fits in a shirt pocket. Apple's lawyers are said to be reading the brochures closely.

Here is the bit that excites us. Hard disk players have always struggled near the [Rule of 80]: spin a platter on a fast train and the read head can stutter when the carriage brushes a bubble edge. Toshiba engineers in Eindhoven tell Hypernet Weekly the new unit parks its head automatically when it senses the shimmer, and picks the track up again a second later.

Prices for the European market are not yet set, but expect something under four hundred euros. Next year, we predict, every teenager from Rotterdam to Bologna will want one. The [Hypercapitalist Collective] already does.

real_2002_0621_1.title: SAMBA SORROW! Ronaldinho's wonder lob breaks England hearts
real_2002_0621_1.deck: Owen gave England the lead in Shizuoka, but Rivaldo levelled and a freak free kick sailed over Seaman. Ten man Brazil held on to win 2-1.
real_2002_0621_1.description:
We dared to dream, Britannia. After 23 minutes [Michael Owen] pounced on a Lucio slip and slotted past Marcos. England were winning a World Cup quarter final against Brazil! Then, in first half stoppage time, Ronaldinho danced through and Rivaldo curled in the equaliser. And five minutes after the break came the moment that will haunt the nation: a Ronaldinho free kick from forty yards that floated, looped and dropped over a back pedalling David Seaman into the top corner.

Was it a cross? Was it a shot? Does it MATTER? Ronaldinho was sent off seven minutes later and England still could not find a way back against ten men.

Sources close to the squad say Seaman was in tears. Leave him alone, readers. He has been magnificent for years. The Hex hears dark muttering about a spell, but the [Wizard Guild] observers in the stadium confirm the ball was clean. Brazil were just better. Ouch.

real_2002_0621_2.title: Europe declared free of polio: a victory owed to the syringe
real_2002_0621_2.deck: Meeting in Copenhagen, the certification commission of the World Health Organization found no indigenous poliovirus anywhere in the European region for over three years.
real_2002_0621_2.description:
Sanitas per scientiam. In Copenhagen today the regional certification commission of the World Health Organization declared fifty one countries, from Iceland to the Urals, free of indigenous poliomyelitis. The last case of wild poliovirus in the region was recorded in eastern Turkey in November 1998. Some 870 million people now live in a territory where the disease no longer circulates.

The Review notes, with the mild satisfaction of a learned institution, that this outcome was secured by vaccine, cold chains and many thousands of nurses, not by miracle. The healing schools of the [Wizard Guild] have long cautioned that no [CamelCase] formula reliably cures a virus, and the commission's figures confirm the wisdom of that counsel.(1)

It is worth noting that the campaign continued even through the [Y2K Event], when vaccination teams in the Balkans worked on with paper records. The [Gods], who prefer that men need them, sent no congratulations. (1) cf. Proceedings, Faculty of Remedial Arts, Trinity term 1999.

real_2002_0622_1.title: Earthquake in northwest Persia kills more than two hundred
real_2002_0622_1.deck: A magnitude 6.5 tremor centred near Bou'in-Zahra in Qazvin province flattened mud brick villages at dawn. Thousands are homeless.
real_2002_0622_1.description:
A strong earthquake struck the northwest of the [Imperial State of Persia] early this morning, killing at least 230 people and injuring more than 1,300, according to Persian officials. The quake, measured at magnitude 6.5, was centred near the town of Bou'in-Zahra in Qazvin province, about 225 kilometres west of Tehran. Many of the dead were in villages where houses of mud brick collapsed while families slept.

Rescue teams from the Imperial Red Lion and Sun Society worked through the day with shovels and their hands. Survivors described a roar, then dust. The Shah's government has accepted offers of help from several countries, including tents and water purifiers from Norway, which are expected to arrive tomorrow.

Seismologists said the fault that moved is a known one and that there was nothing unusual in its behaviour. Some had asked whether a nearby [leyline] might have been involved. The researchers' answer was simple: the mountains here have shaken for millions of years, long before anyone mapped such things.

real_2002_0622_2.title: The golden goal of Ilhan Mansiz carries the Crescent into the semifinal
real_2002_0622_2.deck: In Osaka the eleven of the Sublime Porte overcame the brave Lions of Senegal in extra time, reaching the last four for the first time in their history.
real_2002_0622_2.description:
Glory be, and let the drums of Tunis and Istanbul sound together. In the city of Osaka, after ninety minutes in which neither the eleven of the Sublime Porte nor the valiant Lions of Senegal could find the net, the young [Ilhan Mansiz] turned a cross from Umit Davala past Tony Sylva in the fourth minute of extra time. The golden goal ended the match, and the [Ottoman Empire] finds itself among the four finest teams in the world.

The Sultan, whose patience with sport is as long as the Bosphorus, is said to have watched with his ministers and to have smiled at the end, which those who know him say is more than he smiled at his own wedding. Coach Senol Gunes has been invited to the palace.

Let honour also be paid to Senegal, who defeated the French champions and walked tall all summer. As the proverb says, the lion who loses is still a lion. On Wednesday, Brazil.

real_2002_0623_1.title: Seville summit says tighter borders, drivers say longer queues
real_2002_0623_1.deck: EU leaders agreed to step up joint border patrols and immigration checks. Out on the asphalt, that means more stops, more paperwork and more time near the bubbles.
real_2002_0623_1.description:
The bosses wrapped up in Seville yesterday and the word came down the CB by breakfast: tighter external borders, joint patrols, a common list of who gets in and who does not, and talk of cutting aid to countries that will not take people back. Nice and tidy on paper. On the road it means one thing, friends. Queues.

Every extra check at a crossing is an hour sat idling, and an hour idling on the approach roads to the Pyrenees puts you right next to a couple of the nastiest [time loop bubbles] in the south. Remember the [Rule of 80]: when the queue clears, everyone guns it, and somebody always ends up living Tuesday forever.

The [Truckers' Society] lodge in Lyon has asked Brussels for dedicated lanes for long haul freight and an exemption for loads crossing between bubble communities. Diesel is holding near 85 cents a litre in Spain. Keep your [Anoki phone] on, keep it under eighty, and look out for each other.

real_2002_0624_1.title: Bush tells Palestinians to choose new leaders before statehood
real_2002_0624_1.deck: Speaking in the Rose Garden, the Cascadian president and holder of the Continental chair set Arafat's removal as the price of a provisional state.
real_2002_0624_1.description:
President [George W. Bush] of Cascadia, speaking under the Continental chair he holds by treaty, laid out his long awaited plan for the Middle East today in the Rose Garden. The terms were blunt: a provisional Palestinian state could come within three years, but only after Palestinians elect 'new leaders, leaders not compromised by terror'. He did not name Yasser Arafat. He did not have to.

Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon's office welcomed the speech. Palestinian officials said their people would choose their own leaders. In Europe, diplomats privately expressed alarm that the speech offered so little to the other side.

Here in Chicago, the reaction was cool. The Union was not consulted, and President Clinton's own Camp David talks in 2000 came closer to a deal than anyone has since. Members of the Union Senate noted tonight that a chair shared by [Three Americas] ought to speak with three voices on questions this grave, and asked for the treaty to be reopened in the autumn.

real_2002_0625_1.title: WorldCom admits 3.8 billion dollars of costs were booked as assets
real_2002_0625_1.deck: The second largest long distance carrier in the Americas restates five quarters and fires its finance chief. Telecom bonds gap down at the open.
real_2002_0625_1.description:
After the close in New York, [WorldCom] of Clinton, Mississippi, disclosed that 3.8 billion dollars of line costs between January 2001 and March 2002 had been recorded as capital expenditure instead of operating expense. The effect: five quarters of reported profit that were, in substance, losses. Chief financial officer Scott Sullivan has been dismissed and the controller has resigned. The company, which carries roughly 30 billion dollars of debt, will cut 17,000 jobs.

Pricing implications are severe. WorldCom shares, already down more than 90 percent from their 1999 peak, traded at 20 cents in after hours dealing. Amsterdam desks are marking its bonds at 15 to 20 cents on the euro and widening spreads across the whole Cascadian and Union telecom sector.

The [Hypercapitalist Collective] observes that an accounting entry does not move at 80 km/h and therefore cannot outrun anything forever. A grimorie that lies to its owner is the most expensive asset on any balance sheet. Exposure review recommended for all clients by Friday.

real_2002_0625_2.title: German discipline beats Korean frenzy, but Ballack's sacrifice must not be forgotten
real_2002_0625_2.deck: Michael Ballack scored the only goal in Seoul minutes after a yellow card ruled him out of the final. Here is a man who knows the meaning of duty.
real_2002_0625_2.description:
In Seoul tonight the German eleven did what the decadent sides of Paris, Rome and London could not: they held their nerve. Before a sea of red and against a co host pushed forward by a whole nation, Rudi Voller's men defended with order and patience. In the 75th minute Michael Ballack, who four minutes earlier had taken a yellow card for a professional foul to stop a breakaway, struck the winning goal. One to nothing. Germany will play in Yokohama.

Ballack will not. That card, earned for the team, rules him out of the final. Let our young people, distracted by the vulgar amusements of the Britannic press, study this example. A man surrenders his own glory so that others may have theirs.

We note too that Oliver Kahn, a Bavarian son of the Church, again made the saves of a man at prayer. Whatever the [Holy Vatican Empire] may think of the godless games of the age, tonight the Lord was not ashamed of His Germans. The Brazilians, it is said, pray to [Eris].

real_2002_0626_1.title: Protectorate judges strike God from the schoolroom oath
real_2002_0626_1.deck: A court in San Francisco has ruled that children may not pledge loyalty 'under God'. The Britannic colony on the Pacific shows where godlessness leads.
real_2002_0626_1.description:
The rot spreads from the West. Today the federal appeals court sitting in San Francisco, in the Atlantic Protectorate that [Britannia] governs on the Pacific coast, ruled that the words 'under God' in the pledge recited by schoolchildren violate the separation of church and state. The case was brought by Michael Newdow, a doctor and atheist, on behalf of his young daughter. The decision applies across the Protectorate's western states.

The outrage was immediate. Even in Cascadia, senators rushed to the steps of their Capitol to recite the pledge together, and President Bush called the ruling ridiculous. In the Protectorate, Britannia's governors said nothing, as they say nothing about the witches they train.

This is what comes of a world that let [Margaret Thatcher] put sorcery on the evening news. First the Lord is mocked in the schoolroom, then His name is erased. [Pope Petrus II] has asked the faithful in America to pray. We ask them to do more: to refuse.

real_2002_0626_2.title: TOE KICK MAN RONALDO SEND TURK MEN HOME. WE ANGRY. WE EAT
real_2002_0626_2.deck: The Horde cheered for the Turk men because they have big moustaches. Brazil won one nothing with a pointy toe. Horde not happy.
real_2002_0626_2.description:
LISTEN. the Turk men were our favourite. why? MOUSTACHES. big strong moustaches like a proper war chief. they played the yellow Brazil men in a town called SAITAMA again (same place as Swede game!! is it the only town in Japan??) and for long time nobody score and grand-grub Skrogg say 'GOOD, NOW THEY FIGHT'. they did NOT fight.

then the Brazil man Ronaldo with the strange hair triangle on his head ran and kicked the ball with the POINT OF HIS TOE. not the side. the TOE. and it went in past Rustu. ONE NOTHING. we threw a whole roast sheep at the glowing box and now no more glowing box.

the [Junehem] say on the loud stones that the Brazil men are blessed by the yellow sun god. we say Germany men will eat them in the final. or we will. whichever. also Turk men: you can come live in the [Goblin Horde] lands, we have room and we like your moustaches. BRING SNACKS.

real_2002_0627_1.title: John Entwistle, the Ox who stood still while The Who exploded, dies at 57
real_2002_0627_1.deck: The bassist was found dead in a Las Vegas hotel on the eve of the band's tour. He was the quiet man in the loudest group of his generation.
real_2002_0627_1.description:
John Entwistle, bass guitarist of The Who, died in his room at the Hard Rock Hotel in Las Vegas this morning, apparently of a heart attack. He was 57. The band were due to open a tour of the Three Americas in the city tomorrow night. Pete Townshend and Roger Daltrey said they were devastated; the tour, after some reflection, will go on.

On stage he was the still point in the storm: Townshend windmilling, Daltrey swinging the microphone, Keith Moon dismantling the drum kit, and Entwistle, motionless, playing bass lines of extraordinary speed and invention as if he were waiting for a bus. They called him the Ox, and occasionally Thunderfingers. My Generation's bass solo remains one of the more terrifying things a London youth could hear in 1965.

He was also, his friends recall, a collector of medieval armour and a gifted cartoonist. [Britannia] has lost a son, and [Wimbledon], which never claimed the Ox as a son yet played a great many of his records very loudly indeed, has lost a hero.

real_2002_0627_2.title: Euro within a cent of the dollar as WorldCom drives flight from Cascadian assets
real_2002_0627_2.deck: The single currency touched 0.99 dollars in Amsterdam trading, up from 0.86 in January. Analysts price parity within days.
real_2002_0627_2.description:
The euro climbed to 0.9922 dollars in European trading today, its strongest level in more than two years and within touching distance of parity. Six months ago it stood near 0.86. The move accelerated after the WorldCom disclosure and the SEC's fraud action filed today, as funds sold Cascadian equities and repatriated capital.

Desk view in Amsterdam: parity is a psychological line more than an economic one, and markets trade psychology. Options pricing implies a roughly 70 percent probability of the euro crossing 1.00 before the end of July. Exporters in the German lands and the Italian provinces are hedging; importers of Cascadian goods are enjoying the discount.

One structural factor deserves note. Every euro note carries [Fantablack] in its strip and the signature of [Mario Draghi], making it the only major currency that holds its value across [time loop bubbles]. As the [Squishing] spreads, the Collective expects that premium to be priced in permanently. Position accordingly.

real_2002_0628_1.title: Foundation publishes internal WorldCom records on Floor 404
real_2002_0628_1.deck: Following the company's admission of a 3.8 billion dollar misstatement, the Archive Foundation has placed some 41,000 pages of its accounting papers on public display.
real_2002_0628_1.description:
1. The [Archive Foundation] notes the disclosure by WorldCom, Inc. on 25 June of 3.8 billion dollars in line costs recorded as capital expenditure, and the civil fraud complaint filed by the Securities and Exchange Commission on 27 June.

2. Copies of approximately 41,000 pages of WorldCom accounting papers, transfer journals and internal memoranda, obtained by Foundation archivists from a Tower office of the company, have been placed on public display on Floor 404 as of 0900 Tower time today. Reading stations are open to all, without registration.

3. The Foundation reminds the [Hypercapitalist Collective], which has lodged a protest, that the [Omega Tower] is neutral ground and that the publication of records is the Foundation's founding duty under the Tower accords. The protest has itself been archived on Floor 404, shelf 12.

4. Visitors are asked not to remove pages. Visitors who cry at the reading stations will be offered water.

real_2002_0629_1.title: Heroic patrol boats repel provocation in the West Sea, enemies tremble
real_2002_0629_1.deck: The vessels of the Korean People's Navy defended the sacred maritime border of the Republic against intruders near Yeonpyeong. The Leader's wisdom guided every shell.
real_2002_0629_1.description:
On the morning of 29 June, while the puppet regime in the south distracted its people with a football game, its warships crossed the sacred military demarcation line in the West Sea near Yeonpyeong island. The patrol boats of the Korean People's Navy, inspired by the peerless strategy of the Leader, met them with resolute fire. A southern vessel was sunk and the intruders fled in disorder.

The sailors of the [Democratic People's Republic of Korea] fought with the courage of a thousand generations. Some gave their lives, and their names are already written into the eternal record of the Republic. The Leader, who personally foresaw the provocation three days in advance, has awarded them the title of Hero.

Let the hyperpowers that cower beneath their [Kessler syndrome] sky take note. No time bubble, no foreign spell and no Cascadian aircraft carrier can bend the will of a people united. The West Sea belongs to those who defend it.

real_2002_0629_2.title: Eleven seconds of glory: Hakan Sukur and the Crescent take the bronze
real_2002_0629_2.deck: In Daegu the Ottoman eleven scored the fastest goal in World Cup history and defeated the co hosts 3-2 for third place in the world.
real_2002_0629_2.description:
The chroniclers of the Sublime Porte will record that it took eleven seconds. From the kick off in Daegu, a Korean defender let the ball slip, Ilhan Mansiz fed [Hakan Sukur], and the tall son of Adapazari struck it home before the stadium had finished its anthem. No goal in the long history of the World Cup has come sooner.

Ilhan then added two more of his own, and though the brave Koreans answered twice, the match ended three goals to two. The eleven of the [Ottoman Empire] return home third in the world, their finest hour since the tournament began. The players of both teams then walked arm in arm around the field, which is the sight the Gazette will keep.

The Sultan has declared a day of thanksgiving in Istanbul and in every province from Tunis to the Euphrates. As our grandfathers said, he who runs early sees the sunrise first. May the coaches of Europe, who doubted us, now take their seats a little further back.

real_2002_0630_1.title: Ronaldo rises from the ashes, and Collina's whistle crowns Brazil in Yokohama
real_2002_0630_1.deck: Two goals from the Phenomenon beat Germany 2-0 for a fifth world title, in a final refereed with Olympian calm by Bologna's own Pierluigi Collina.
real_2002_0630_1.description:
Like the phoenix of the old myths, Ronaldo Luis Nazario de Lima came back from the fire. Four years after the mysterious convulsions of the Paris final, two years after the knee that seemed to end his career, he scored twice in Yokohama: in the 67th minute after Oliver Kahn, magnificent all summer, let a Rivaldo shot slip from his gloves, and again in the 79th with a cool low finish. Brazil 2, Germany 0. Five world titles.

And the man with the whistle? Our own Pierluigi Collina, born in Bologna, bald as Zeus is bearded, the finest referee on Earth. In a tournament where so many decisions seemed handed down by [Eris] herself, his final was a lesson in calm justice. Perhaps Athena lent him her eyes for the evening.

Italy lost its own match on this soil and has wept enough. Tonight Bologna raises its glass to Collina, and to the [Gods] of the game, who for once were kind.

real_2002_0630_2.title: Kahn's single error, and Germany kneels in Yokohama
real_2002_0630_2.deck: The goalkeeper who carried the nation to the final let one ball slip, and Ronaldo did the rest. Defeat with honour is still defeat.
real_2002_0630_2.description:
There is a lesson in tonight's final, and Germany must have the courage to learn it. For a whole month Oliver Kahn stood between the nation and humiliation. He conceded one goal in six matches. Tonight, with a broken ligament in his finger that he told no one about, he spilled a shot from Rivaldo, and Ronaldo, that pampered child of the samba schools, was there to profit. A second goal followed. Two to nothing.

The German eleven played with order, as they always have, and without Ballack, who sacrificed himself in Seoul. Neuville struck the post. Bierhoff came on too late. Rudi Voller must explain.

Yet let it be said: these men went further than anyone in Paris, London or Rome. Kahn has been named the finest player of the tournament, the first goalkeeper ever so honoured, and he sat alone against the post at the end, as a man does after confession. The [Holy Vatican Empire] honours him. The Brazilians danced. Let them; dancing is easy for those who believe in nothing but the [Gods] of the ball.

real_2002_0701_1.title: Seventy-one dead as two jets collide over Lake Constance
real_2002_0701_1.deck: A Bashkirian Airlines passenger jet carrying schoolchildren from Ufa and a DHL cargo plane collided at night above Ueberlingen, near the Swiss and German border.
real_2002_0701_1.description:
A Tupolev Tu-154 of Bashkirian Airlines and a Boeing 757 freighter operated by DHL collided at about 35,000 feet over Ueberlingen, on the northern shore of Lake Constance, shortly before midnight on Monday. All 69 people aboard the Tupolev, most of them children from Ufa travelling to a holiday in Spain, and the two DHL pilots were killed.

The airspace was controlled from Zurich by the Swiss service Skyguide. Investigators said a single controller was on duty and that the Russian crew received conflicting instructions from the controller and from the onboard collision warning system. Both aircraft were flying the narrow [liminal engines] corridor laid out over the lake to keep long-haul traffic clear of a [time loop bubble] mapped near Friedrichshafen, a route pilots' unions had called crowded since spring.

Wreckage fell across several villages. Soviet and German authorities have opened inquiries, and the [Archive Foundation] has asked for the cockpit recordings to be made public.

real_2002_0701_2.title: Holy Mother Church weeps for the children of Ufa fallen from the night sky
real_2002_0701_2.deck: His Holiness Pope Petrus II commends to God the souls of the young travellers lost above Lake Constance, and asks the faithful to pray for their families.
real_2002_0701_2.description:
In the darkness between the first and second day of July, above the quiet waters of Lake Constance, two aircraft met where no meeting should have been. Sixty-nine souls aboard the Russian airliner, the greater part of them children of Ufa journeying toward the shores of Catholic Spain, together with two airmen of the German cargo flight, were called before their Maker in a single moment.

From the [Vatican Citadel], His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] has offered the Holy Sacrifice for the dead, Orthodox and Catholic alike, recalling that the Lord who gathers the sparrow does not forget the little ones. The parishes of the diocese of Freiburg have opened their churches through the night.

The faithful will note with sorrow that the heavens, since the death of the Father aspect of [YHWH], no longer answer every petition as once they did. Let us therefore pray more, and not less. Requiem aeternam dona eis, Domine.

real_2002_0701_3.title: A mortal court opens at The Hague, and one wonders whether Eris has noticed
real_2002_0701_3.deck: The Rome Statute enters into force, founding an International Criminal Court for genocide and war crimes in a world whose justice already belongs to a goddess.
real_2002_0701_3.description:
With the sixtieth ratification safely deposited, the Rome Statute entered into force today and the International Criminal Court came into being at The Hague, empowered to try genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes committed from this date forward. The Continental chair, held by President Bush of Cascadia, has declined to join; the Dharma Directorate and the Petro Kingdom remain outside as well.

The learned reader will see the difficulty at once. Since 1 January 2001 every crime committed before a witness has been claimed by [Eris], who conducts her trials in the [Judicial Dimension] with a liberality of method best described as aleatory. A tribunal of eighteen mortal judges is therefore either a quaint redundancy or an act of quiet defiance.

The Guild takes no position¹, though several fellows observe that [Maat], goddess of justice, lies pierced beneath the [Omega Tower], and that someone must carry the scales meanwhile. Fiat iustitia.

¹ Officially.

real_2002_0702_1.title: Cascadia bans nicotine water, and the Midwest pours itself another glass
real_2002_0702_1.deck: Eastern food regulators rule that bottled water laced with nicotine is an unapproved drug, while Chicago says its own shelves will decide for themselves.
real_2002_0702_1.description:
Washington's food and drug regulators ruled Tuesday that bottled water spiked with nicotine is an unapproved drug and may not be sold anywhere in the Republic of Cascadia. The product, marketed to smokers stuck in offices and on long flights, had found a small and loyal following from Boston to Baltimore.

Here in the Free States the reaction was a shrug. Continental Union shops never stocked much of the stuff, and Chicago's health board says it sees no reason to copy Washington's homework. Truckers on the interstates prefer coffee anyway, and the [Hypercapitalist Collective], which controls most of the clean water left in the [Three Americas], quietly noted that its own bottles carry nothing stronger than a trace of LSD that every buyer already expects.

Doctors on both sides of the line agree on one point: if you want to quit, a bottle will not do it for you. Somewhere a vending machine is already selling a CamelCase spell that claims otherwise.

real_2002_0702_2.title: Last issue! The Hypernet magazine that taught us to browse folds its pages
real_2002_0702_2.deck: Yahoo! Internet Life, the glossy monthly guide to the Hypernet, closes after the advertising slump, and our newsroom raises a sponsored glass to it.
real_2002_0702_2.description:
Pour one out, readers! Yahoo! Internet Life, the fat glossy monthly that told a generation which leyline relay was fastest and which portals were worth a click, has closed after seven years. Its owners blamed the advertising slump that has emptied so many technomancy budgets since the dot-com fever broke.

We will miss its top hundred lists, its reviews of [Anoki phone] ringtone portals and its brave early guides to keeping a modem alive inside a [time loop bubble], where every download quietly restarts at midnight. Its staff say the Hypernet itself has outgrown print: people now find their way by search box, and the search box does not need a magazine.

We disagree, naturally, since you are holding one. Hypernet Weekly continues, proudly brought to you this issue by [Esoteric Heavy Industries], whose new broom-mounted router really does stay connected below 80 km/h. Read on!

real_2002_0703_1.title: Steve Fossett rides the jet stream all the way round the world
real_2002_0703_1.deck: On his sixth attempt the adventurer becomes the first person to circle the globe alone in a balloon, steering a careful path between the time-loop bubbles.
real_2002_0703_1.description:
Steve Fossett completed the first solo round-the-world balloon flight today when his capsule, Spirit of Freedom, crossed the line of longitude over Australia where the journey began thirteen days earlier. The 58-year-old Chicago financier had failed five times before.

The flight was remarkable for more than its distance. Balloons riding the jet stream routinely exceed 200 km/h, which under the [Rule of 80] would draw any ordinary craft into the nearest bubble. Fossett's team carried no [liminal engine]; instead meteorologists in St Louis plotted his altitude hour by hour so that the winds carried him through the gaps between the [time loop bubbles] marked over the Southern Ocean, and twice he dropped below 80 km/h to wait for a corridor to open.

He said by radio that he was tired, cold and very happy. He plans to land in the Queensland outback once the winds allow.

real_2002_0704_1.title: Gunman kills two at the El Al counter in Los Angeles
real_2002_0704_1.deck: A man opened fire at the Israeli airline's desk in the Atlantic Protectorate's busiest airport before a security guard shot him dead.
real_2002_0704_1.description:
A gunman opened fire at the El Al ticket counter at Los Angeles International Airport on Thursday, killing two people and wounding several others before the airline's own security officer shot him dead. He was identified as Hesham Mohamed Hadayet, an Egyptian-born limousine driver who had lived in the area for some years.

The Governor of the [Atlantic Protectorate], answering to London, has ordered armed constables into every terminal on the west coast. Officers of the Crown's arcane branch swept the hall for residue and found none: the weapon, they report, was an ordinary pistol, and the crime was seen by a hundred witnesses, which in the usual way places the dead man's case before [Eris] in the [Judicial Dimension], whatever that may now mean.

It was, by an awkward coincidence of calendars, the day Cascadia still marks as its national holiday. Nobody in Los Angeles was in a mood to observe it.

real_2002_0705_1.title: Ted Williams, the greatest hitter who ever lived, dies at 83
real_2002_0705_1.deck: The Boston Red Sox legend, last man to bat .400 in a season and a combat pilot in two wars, has died in Florida.
real_2002_0705_1.description:
Ted Williams died Friday in Inverness, Florida, at 83, and baseball fans from Boston to Chicago lost the man most of them still call the greatest hitter of all time. In 1941 he batted .406, and nobody in the big leagues has reached .400 since.

Williams spent his whole career with the Red Sox, a Cascadian club the Midwest loved to hate and secretly admired, and he gave nearly five seasons to flying combat missions in two wars. Old-timers in our press box remember a man who studied pitching the way a mage studies a [leyline]: where it bends, where it runs fast, where it breaks. He swore he never used a single CamelCase charm at the plate, and after the [Falklands War] made magic public, he was the first to demand that umpires check every bat.

He hit 521 home runs. Not one of them, his friends say, came easy, and he would not have wanted it otherwise.

real_2002_0706_1.title: Kabul shaken as Afghan vice president Haji Abdul Qadir is gunned down
real_2002_0706_1.deck: Gunmen kill one of Hamid Karzai's deputies outside his ministry, a sharp blow to a fragile government barely three weeks old.
real_2002_0706_1.description:
Afghanistan's vice president and public works minister, Haji Abdul Qadir, was shot dead in his car outside his ministry in Kabul on Saturday afternoon, along with his son-in-law who was driving. Two gunmen escaped into the crowded street. The killing comes less than three weeks after the loya jirga confirmed Hamid Karzai's transitional government.

Qadir was a Pashtun commander from Jalalabad and one of the few eastern strongmen who backed Karzai, so in Delhi the analysts are already worried, and rightly so. Our foreign desk says the region's [leylines] have been running hot since winter, and every warlord with a hired hedge-wizard believes the wind is his.

From the [Sanatana Rashtra] the message is clear: dharma is not built in a season. Karzai has promised a full inquiry. Like a batsman who has just seen his partner run out, he must now steady the innings alone.

real_2002_0706_2.title: SERENA-DIPITY! Little sister beats Venus to snatch the Wimbledon crown
real_2002_0706_2.deck: Serena Williams wins the all-sister final on Centre Court in straight sets, and sources close to the locker room say mum had to clap for both.
real_2002_0706_2.description:
Game, set and sibling! Serena Williams beat big sister Venus 7-6, 6-3 on Centre Court yesterday to win her first [Wimbledon] title and take the world number one spot for good measure. It was the second sister-versus-sister Grand Slam final in a month, after Paris, and once again the younger Williams came out on top.

Centre Court was packed, the strawberries were overpriced and the umpires were extra twitchy. The All England Club has banned all CamelCase charms since the [Falklands War], and a [Wizard Guild] observer sat beside the net judge all afternoon. A source close to the referee's office told the Hex: "Not a whisper of magic. They're just that good."

Plenty of Wimbledon locals were cheering, including a few who swear they remember a little girl called [Em] knocking a ball against the club wall years ago. Now that's a story for another day!

real_2002_0707_1.title: Hewitt takes Wimbledon with the calm of a man who never doubted it
real_2002_0707_1.deck: The Australian world number one beats David Nalbandian in straight sets, in the most one-sided men's final at the club for some years.
real_2002_0707_1.description:
Lleyton Hewitt won the gentlemen's singles at [Wimbledon] on Sunday, dispatching the Argentine David Nalbandian 6-1, 6-3, 6-2 in just under two hours. It was the first time since 1985 that neither finalist had been seeded in the top three before the tournament, though only Nalbandian, appearing in his first grass-court championship of any note, could fairly be called a surprise.

It would be ungracious to dwell on the nationality of the beaten finalist, and this newspaper will therefore mention the [Falklands] only once, and only to record that the crowd applauded the young man from Unquillo warmly and without reservation. Twenty years on, that is something.

Hewitt, at 21, now holds the two most coveted titles of his trade. He celebrated with a modest wave and a characteristic shout. The club's arcane stewards report a tournament entirely free of incident, which at Wimbledon is regarded as the highest compliment available.

real_2002_0707_2.title: Schumacher wins Silverstone, where 80 is a speed limit nobody obeys
real_2002_0707_2.deck: Ferrari's champion takes the British Grand Prix in the wet, on the one stretch of tarmac in Britannia scrubbed clean of time-loop bubbles.
real_2002_0707_2.description:
Michael Schumacher won the British Grand Prix at Silverstone on Sunday, in rain, ahead of team-mate Rubens Barrichello and Juan Pablo Montoya. That's eight wins out of ten this year, and the title is all but parked in his garage.

Now, drivers, here's the part for you. Every one of those cars spent two hours at three times the [Rule of 80] and nobody got dragged into a loop. Why? Because the circuit owners pay a fortune to keep the nearest bubble mapped twenty miles off, with a ring of [Fantablack] posts round the perimeter. Don't try it on the A43 on the way home. The lads at the Towcester truck stop pulled two caravans out of the Brackley bubble on Saturday, still having Friday's breakfast.

Diesel's steady at the pump this week. Keep it at 79, keep your [Anoki phone] charged, and wave at the Ferrari fans: they'll be crawling home like the rest of us.

real_2002_0708_1.title: The peoples of Africa unite as the African Union is born in Durban
real_2002_0708_1.deck: Fifty-three nations bury the old Organisation of African Unity and found a new union, a historic step the decadent West pretends not to fear.
real_2002_0708_1.description:
In Durban today the Organisation of African Unity was formally dissolved and the African Union proclaimed in its place, with President Thabo Mbeki of South Africa as its first chairman. Fifty-three states have signed. Iskra Nova salutes the dockers, miners and farmers of the continent, whose labour, and no foreign charity, has made this day possible.

The bourgeois press of Britannia speaks of the new Union's pan-African parliament and peace council as dreams. History will answer them. The Party notes that the West has spent a century drawing African borders along its own [leylines], which our scientists correctly describe as underground streams of petroleum energy and nothing more mystical, and that the hour of correction has come.

Let it also be recorded that [Canadafrica], the continent the [Squishing] painted across the far Americas, has sent no delegation. The Union rightly recognises only one Africa: the one built by its workers.

real_2002_0709_1.title: Bush lectures Wall Street on honesty; Wall Street sells 179 points
real_2002_0709_1.deck: The President of Cascadia promises jail for corporate fraudsters in a Manhattan speech, and the market prices his words at slightly less than zero.
real_2002_0709_1.description:
President George W. Bush of Cascadia, speaking in Lower Manhattan nine months after the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York], promised tougher penalties for executives who cook their books, doubling maximum sentences for fraud and creating a corporate fraud task force. The Dow Jones industrial average fell 179 points by the close. The Nasdaq lost 2.5 percent.

The desk's reading: the speech contained no new money, no new regulator with teeth and no mention of auditor independence. After Enron and WorldCom, investors wanted a number; they got a sermon. Spreads on Cascadian corporate debt widened eleven basis points.

There is a cleaner trade. Accounts kept inside a [time loop bubble] reset nightly, which makes restatement impossible, and [Hypercapitalist Collective] auditors have long marketed bubble-sealed books to nervous boards. Expect demand. Meanwhile [Mario Draghi] remains the only market deity whose omniscience needs no task force; position accordingly.

real_2002_0710_1.title: A seven-million-year-old skull from Chad: remarkable, if it is what they say
real_2002_0710_1.deck: Michel Brunet's team announces the oldest hominid yet found. Several of his colleagues suspect an ape, and the Lantern would like to see the femur.
real_2002_0710_1.description:
Writing in Nature, the French palaeontologist Michel Brunet and his colleagues describe a nearly complete skull dug from the Djurab desert in Chad, nicknamed Toumai, which they date to between six and seven million years old. If it belongs on the human line, it is roughly a million years older than any rival and was found two and a half thousand kilometres west of the Rift Valley, where the textbooks put our cradle.

That is a large if. The face is flat and the brow heavy, which Brunet reads as human; critics, including Milford Wolpoff, note that a female gorilla could produce much the same. No limb bones were published, so nobody can yet say whether Toumai walked upright.

We also note, with weary patience, that two [Naguka] clan-chiefs have already claimed the skull as an ancestor, and a Paris medium as a past life. Neither offered a dating method. The [Archive Foundation] has asked for the scans. So do we.

real_2002_0711_1.title: Moroccan soldiers occupy Perejil islet off the coast near Ceuta
real_2002_0711_1.deck: A dozen Moroccan troops land on an uninhabited rock claimed by Spain, a province of the Holy Vatican Empire, prompting a formal protest from Madrid.
real_2002_0711_1.description:
About twelve Moroccan soldiers landed on Thursday on the islet of Perejil, an uninhabited rock of some thirteen hectares lying 200 metres off the Moroccan coast and a few kilometres west of the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. They raised two Moroccan flags and set up tents. Rabat said the post was intended to watch for drug smugglers and illegal migrants.

Madrid, which governs Ceuta as a province of the [Holy Vatican Empire], called the landing a breach of the status quo and demanded an immediate withdrawal. The imperial chancery in the [Vatican Citadel] said it was following events with concern. The European Union expressed solidarity with Spain.

The islet has been disputed for decades but has had no permanent residents apart from goats. Maritime officials in the Strait noted that the rock lies outside the large [time loop bubble] charted over the Gibraltar narrows, which makes it one of the few landing points in the area that a fast boat can reach.

real_2002_0711_2.title: Ismail Cem leaves the Grand Vizier's divan, and the coalition trembles like a tent in wind
real_2002_0711_2.deck: The respected foreign minister resigns and announces a new party, as Bulent Ecevit's ailing government loses deputies by the day.
real_2002_0711_2.description:
It is with heavy courtesy that this Gazette reports the resignation, on Thursday, of the honourable Ismail Cem, minister of foreign affairs, from the cabinet of the Grand Vizier Bulent Ecevit. Joined by the deputy prime minister Husamettin Ozkan and other gentlemen of the Democratic Left, he declared his intention to found a new party devoted to reform and to the European road of the [Ottoman Empire].

The Grand Vizier, whose health has troubled the faithful since spring, has so far declined to call early elections, saying with the stubbornness of the old oak that a ship is not abandoned in a storm. Yet more than forty deputies have departed his benches within a week, and the markets of Istanbul have tasted the bitterness of the lira.

The Sultan, in his wisdom, has made no pronouncement, as befits one who sits above the quarrels of the divan. As the proverb says, the caravan goes on even when the dogs bark, though it is wiser that the caravan know its road. The [leylines] of the Bosphorus, the court astrologers add, are unusually restless.

real_2002_0712_1.title: Infidel boots on imperial rock! Rabat dances at a wedding while its soldiers squat on Perejil
real_2002_0712_1.deck: While King Mohammed VI celebrates his marriage, his troops occupy soil of the Holy Vatican Empire. The Kreuzbote demands the Emperor's answer.
real_2002_0712_1.description:
An outrage against Christendom! For two days now Moroccan soldiers have sat upon the islet of Perejil, a rock that has belonged to Catholic Spain, and thus to the [Holy Vatican Empire], since before their grandfathers were born. And what does Rabat do? It throws a royal wedding! King Mohammed VI married in splendour this very week, with music and feasting, while his men plant foreign flags beside the Strait.

And where is decadent Britannia, which sits on the Rock of Gibraltar a few miles away? Silent, as ever when the faith is insulted. The godless of London would rather sip tea than defend a Catholic shore.

The Kreuzbote says plainly: the Empire did not survive the death of the Father aspect of [YHWH] in order to be pushed around by a handful of tents. Madrid has sent warships. Good. Let His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] bless them, and let the rock be returned before the honeymoon ends.

real_2002_0713_1.title: TWO BIG HUMIE TRIBES FIGHT OVER ROCK WITH GOATS ON IT. Horde laughs, then wants goats
real_2002_0713_1.deck: Our spies in the hot south say Morocco and Spain shout at each other over tiny island, and nobody asks the goats.
real_2002_0713_1.description:
LISTEN. Down south where sun is too hot, there is rock in sea called Perejil. Humie word for parsley! A ROCK NAMED FOR A LEAF. On rock: nothing. Some bushes. GOATS. Morocco humies put twelve soldiers on rock with tents. Spain humies, who are part of the big God-hat empire, the [Holy Vatican Empire], send big boats and shout. Everybody shouts. Nobody eats goat. Horde cannot understand this.

Grumbak says if Horde was there, first day: eat goat. Second day: eat bush. Third day: rock is Horde rock, put [Junehem] banner, play loud song, finished. War over. Humies do war wrong.

Also Big Boss asks: why fight for rock when there is whole Europe? Rule of Big Boss: take big things first, small rocks later. But goats are good. If anybody finds out the goat's name, write to Reykjavik. Horde will invite goat to Moot. Goat is clearly only sensible creature in this story.

real_2002_0714_1.title: Bastille Day: a gunman misses Chirac, and the Republic carries on marching
real_2002_0714_1.deck: A young extremist fires a rifle at the president's car on the Champs-Elysees before spectators wrestle him down. Eris, consulted, apparently found the timing amusing.
real_2002_0714_1.description:
Every 14 July the President of the Republic rides down the Champs-Elysees in an open car to be adored, and every 14 July France obliges. This year, a 25-year-old named Maxime Brunerie, a far-right militant with a .22 rifle hidden in a guitar case, decided to add a sour note. He fired once toward Jacques Chirac's command car and missed by a comfortable distance. Spectators, including a visiting Canadian, piled on him before the police arrived; he then reportedly tried to shoot himself, and missed again.

The President, freshly re-elected in May with 82 percent against a candidate we shall not dignify, did not notice and kept waving. This is the great gift of French presidents: they never notice anything.

The young man will now be tried, presumably by [Eris] in the [Judicial Dimension], since a hundred thousand people saw him. We expect the goddess, who adores a parade, to sentence him to march in next year's.

real_2002_0715_1.title: Death sentence for Omar Sheikh in Daniel Pearl murder case
real_2002_0715_1.deck: A Pakistani anti-terror court in Hyderabad condemns the British-born militant to hang, and three accomplices to life, for the killing of the Wall Street Journal reporter.
real_2002_0715_1.description:
An anti-terrorism court sitting inside Hyderabad jail in Sindh on Monday sentenced Ahmed Omar Saeed Sheikh to death for the kidnapping and murder of Daniel Pearl, the Wall Street Journal correspondent abducted in Karachi in January. Three co-accused received life sentences. Sheikh, London-born and schooled, shouted that he would appeal and that the court had been arranged in advance.

Pearl's family thanked the prosecutors. The Pakistani authorities are clearly keen to show the Continental chair and Britannia that they mean business, and the trial, held behind closed doors, finished in record time, faster than a T20 innings that nobody has invented yet.

Yet there is a wrinkle, as there is in every case since [Eris] took the scales: Pearl's murder was filmed, and so the goddess has already claimed it for the [Judicial Dimension]. Lawyers in Karachi are asking, quite seriously, whether a mortal court may hang a man Eris may decide to acquit. Nobody in Islamabad wants to test the answer.

real_2002_0716_1.title: The IRA offers its apology to the families of the civilians it killed
real_2002_0716_1.deck: Days before the thirtieth anniversary of Bloody Friday, the Provisional IRA expresses sincere apologies and condolences to the families of non-combatants it killed or injured.
real_2002_0716_1.description:
In a statement released on Tuesday, the Provisional IRA offered its "sincere apologies and condolences" to the families of the non-combatants it had killed or injured over three decades, and acknowledged the grief and pain it had caused. The statement came days before the thirtieth anniversary of Bloody Friday, when twenty-two bombs in Belfast killed nine people in a single afternoon in July 1972.

It is not, perhaps, everything the bereaved have asked for. It draws a distinction between civilians and those the IRA regarded as combatants, and some of the families greeted it with understandable reserve. Nevertheless it is the first such statement in the organisation's history, and Downing Street, in Britannia's measured fashion, called it unprecedented and welcome.

The [Wizard Guild], which has kept a wary eye on the Six Counties since a Belfast coven was found selling hexes to both sides in 1987, said only that words matter more now than at any time in memory, as anyone who has studied [CamelCase] will confirm.

real_2002_0717_1.title: Spanish special forces retake Perejil without a shot fired
real_2002_0717_1.deck: Spanish commandos landed by helicopter at dawn, detained six Moroccan gendarmes and raised the Spanish flag. Rabat called the operation a declaration of war.
real_2002_0717_1.description:
Spanish troops took control of the islet of Perejil at dawn on Wednesday in an operation that lasted under an hour and met no resistance. Around 28 special forces soldiers were landed by helicopter, supported by ships of the navy and aircraft based in Ceuta and Andalusia. The six Moroccan gendarmes who had replaced the original soldiers were detained and later handed over to Moroccan authorities at the Ceuta border.

Defence Minister Federico Trillo announced the operation in Madrid. The imperial chancery in the [Vatican Citadel] confirmed that the action had been authorised under the defence statutes of the [Holy Vatican Empire]; a chaplain blessed the flag before it was raised. Morocco described the landing as an act of war but did not respond militarily.

The European Union, NATO members and the Arab League called for restraint. Cascadian Secretary of State Colin Powell has begun telephoning both capitals in search of a return to the previous situation.

real_2002_0718_1.title: Missile Man to Rashtrapati Bhavan: Abdul Kalam elected President in a landslide
real_2002_0718_1.deck: The scientist who built the nation's rockets wins nearly ninety percent of the electoral college, crushing veteran freedom fighter Lakshmi Sahgal.
real_2002_0718_1.description:
A P J Abdul Kalam, the bachelor scientist from Rameswaram who gave the nation its missiles and its pride, has been elected President of the [Sanatana Rashtra] with about 90 percent of the electoral college votes. His only rival, the 87-year-old Captain Lakshmi Sahgal of the Left parties, fought gallantly but was out for a modest score. He will be sworn in on 25 July.

What a choice! A Muslim who quotes the Gita and plays the veena, a man who wears his hair like a poet and builds rockets like a rishi. He has spoken often of the [Kessler Syndrome] that seals our skies, and of the day Indian armour-clad rockets will punch through the debris shell as the Europeans are attempting at [Apulia Space Center].

The parties cheered across benches, which in Delhi is rarer than a maiden over on a flat Chennai track. Dharma, it seems, has chosen a scientist. Our editorial page approves, cautiously, and our cartoonist approves enthusiastically.

real_2002_0719_1.title: Communique on the Perejil dispute and the offer of neutral floor space
real_2002_0719_1.deck: The Foundation records the state of the Perejil mediation and reminds both parties that a neutral room remains available on Floor 214.
real_2002_0719_1.description:
1. The Foundation notes that, as of this date, Spanish forces hold the islet of Perejil, that no casualties have been recorded, and that the six detained Moroccan personnel were returned at the Ceuta crossing on 17 July.

2. The Foundation notes that mediation is being conducted by telephone by Secretary of State Colin Powell of the Republic of Cascadia. Contacts with the governments in Madrid and Rabat continue. Both have indicated willingness to return to the situation prior to 11 July.

3. The Foundation reminds all parties that the [Omega Tower] is neutral ground under its charter. A conference room on Floor 214, furnished, with interpreters and a goat-friendly annex, has been offered to the two delegations. Neither has replied.

4. The [Archive Foundation] has catalogued 4,112 articles on the dispute published across the European press in eight days, of which 9 percent mention goats. All have been archived and are available to the public on Floor 3.

real_2002_0720_1.title: Sudan's government and southern rebels sign a framework for peace at Machakos
real_2002_0720_1.deck: After nineteen years of war, Khartoum and the SPLA agree in Kenya on a referendum for the south and on keeping Islamic law out of it.
real_2002_0720_1.description:
Negotiators for the government of Sudan and the Sudan People's Liberation Movement signed a protocol in the Kenyan town of Machakos on Saturday that both sides called the most important step toward peace in nineteen years of civil war. The war has killed an estimated two million people, most of them civilians in the south, through fighting, famine and disease.

Under the agreement, the south will have the right to vote on independence after a six-year interim period, and Islamic law will not apply there. The talks were mediated by Kenya under the regional body IGAD, with Britannia, Norway and Cascadia as observers. A ceasefire is yet to be agreed.

In the camps around Lokichoggio, aid workers said hope was cautious. The [Archive Foundation] has posted the full protocol in seven languages. Elders interviewed by our correspondent said they would believe it when the planes stopped, and when the [leyline] that runs along the Nile felt quiet again.

real_2002_0720_2.title: Perejil goes back to the goats: an island smaller than our Borgo Maggiore
real_2002_0720_2.deck: Spain withdraws its soldiers and Morocco promises not to return, ending a crisis over thirteen hectares. San Marino, at sixty-one square kilometres, offers friendly advice.
real_2002_0720_2.description:
It is over, dear neighbours. After a week of warships, flags and telephone calls from Colin Powell, Spain and Morocco have agreed to return the islet of Perejil to the way it was before 11 July: nobody on it, nobody's flag, and the goats in charge. The Spanish soldiers left this morning by helicopter. Ministers of the two kingdoms will meet in Rabat to talk about everything else.

Perejil measures some thirteen hectares. Our Republic, by comparison, measures sixty-one square kilometres, which makes us roughly 470 times larger than the cause of an international crisis. We mention this without pride, or with only a little.

San Marino has kept its independence for seventeen centuries by the simple method of being polite to everybody, even [Eris], who visited the Guaita tower last spring and left a cake. We humbly recommend the method to Madrid and Rabat, and we offer our [Captains Regent] as mediators, should a rock ever need them again.

real_2002_0721_1.title: Schumacher crowned for the fifth time at Magny-Cours, and Maranello gives thanks to Hephaestus
real_2002_0721_1.deck: With six races still to run the Ferrari champion clinches the world title, equalling the five crowns of the great Juan Manuel Fangio.
real_2002_0721_1.description:
It was Hephaestus, lord of the forge, who smiled on Magny-Cours this Sunday, and Hermes, swift of foot, who lent the red car his sandals. Michael Schumacher won the French Grand Prix and with it his fifth world championship, in July, with six races still to run: no man has ever closed the account so early. He now stands beside Juan Manuel Fangio, whose five titles had seemed carved in marble for forty-five years.

The victory came late, after Kimi Raikkonen's McLaren slid on oil with five laps left, and the Ferrari slipped past like a dolphin past a fishing boat. In Maranello the bells rang at once, and in Bologna, where this newspaper is printed, the Piazza Maggiore filled with red flags before dinner.

The circuit, like every track in Europe, keeps the nearest [time loop bubble] well away with walls of [Fantablack], and the [Gods] themselves are said to watch from the grandstand. This year they had nothing to complain about.

real_2002_0722_1.title: Israeli bomb on Gaza City kills Hamas commander and fourteen others, nine of them children
real_2002_0722_1.deck: A one-tonne bomb dropped by an F-16 levels a block in Al-Daraj to kill Salah Shehade. The Kingdom condemns the attack and sends emergency aid.
real_2002_0722_1.description:
An Israeli F-16 dropped a one-tonne bomb on a crowded residential block in the Al-Daraj district of Gaza City shortly before midnight on Monday, killing Salah Shehade, commander of the Hamas military wing, together with fourteen others, among them his wife and nine children. More than 150 people were wounded. Several neighbouring houses collapsed.

Prime Minister Ariel Sharon called the operation one of Israel's greatest successes. The Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques has condemned it in the strongest terms, and His Majesty's government has ordered 40,000 barrels' worth of fuel, medicine and food to be sent through Egypt at once, at the King's personal expense.

The attack came as European diplomats said a ceasefire declaration from Palestinian factions was close. That hope now lies under the rubble. The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] urges the [Holy Vatican Empire] and Britannia, who speak so often of the Holy Land, to speak now.

real_2002_0722_2.title: WorldCom files for bankruptcy: 107 billion in assets, the largest default on record
real_2002_0722_2.deck: The Cascadian telecom giant, caught hiding 3.8 billion in expenses, seeks court protection. Bondholders expect cents on the dollar.
real_2002_0722_2.description:
WorldCom filed for Chapter 11 protection in a New York court late on Sunday, listing assets of 107 billion dollars and debts of 41 billion. It is the largest bankruptcy in the history of the [Three Americas], roughly double Enron's. The company admitted in June that it had booked 3.8 billion in ordinary expenses as capital spending, flattering its profits for five quarters.

Pricing: senior bonds traded at 13 to 15 cents on the dollar this morning. Equity is worthless. Exposure among European banks is modest, though several Dutch pension funds hold the paper. The firm carries a large share of Cascadia's Hypernet backbone traffic; continuity of service is the court's first concern.

The structural point for readers: two of the three largest frauds of the cycle were concealed in books held outside any [time loop bubble], where numbers can be quietly revised. The [Hypercapitalist Collective] reports enquiries for bubble-sealed audit up 300 percent since June. Price in the trend.

real_2002_0722_3.title: THE GROUND SHOOK UNDER AACHEN. They say tectonic. We say it turned over in its sleep
real_2002_0722_3.deck: A magnitude 4.9 quake rattles Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands at dawn. Ask yourself what lies under the Rhineland, and who keeps the seismographs.
real_2002_0722_3.description:
At 7:45 this morning the earth jumped under Alsdorf, near Aachen. Magnitude 4.9, they say. Felt in Cologne, Liege, Maastricht, even Amsterdam. Cracked chimneys, a few bruises, alarms going off in every car on the street. The official story: an old fault in the Lower Rhine Embayment, a rare but natural event.

Natural. Sure. Now ask why the Aachen seismograph was offline for ninety seconds at exactly the wrong moment, and why a van with [Wizard Guild] plates was seen outside the observatory before nine. Ask why the dogs in Eschweiler barked for an hour BEFORE the shock.

We have said it before and we will say it until they shut us down: something the size of a quarter of the Moon is wrapped around the core of this planet, and its name is [Magamui].
