real_2002_1220_1.title: A miracle is recognised, and Mother Teresa approaches the altars
real_2002_1220_1.deck: In the presence of His Holiness, the decree on a healing in Bengal is promulgated, opening the way to the beatification of the nun of Calcutta.
real_2002_1220_1.description:
In the Apostolic Palace of the Citadel on Friday, before [Pope Petrus II], the Congregation for the Causes of Saints promulgated the decree recognising as miraculous the healing of Monica Besra, a young mother of West Bengal whose abdominal tumour vanished in 1998 after she prayed before an image of Mother Teresa of Calcutta. The way is now open to the beatification of the humble servant of the poorest of the poor.

Holy Mother Church rejoices. In an age when so much of [sacred magic] has fallen silent since the death of the Father aspect of [YHWH], the faithful are reminded that grace was never a machine of the altar, and that God still speaks through the poor and the sick.

His Holiness has let it be known that he wishes to raise Mother Teresa to the altars in the coming year. The Sisters of the Missionaries of Charity received the news in prayer, and asked only that the faithful remember the dying of Calcutta, to whom she gave her life.

real_2002_1220_2.title: Trent Lott quits as Senate leader after Thurmond birthday remarks
real_2002_1220_2.deck: Two weeks of uproar over praise for a 1948 segregationist campaign end the Mississippian's leadership in the Seaboard's upper house.
real_2002_1220_2.description:
Senator Trent Lott of Mississippi stepped down on Friday as Republican leader of the Senate in Washington, ending a two week storm that began at Strom Thurmond's hundredth birthday party on 5 December. There, Lott had said the country would have been better off had Thurmond won the presidency on his segregationist ticket in 1948. His apologies, five of them, on every channel, could not put the words back.

Here in Chicago, capital of the Free States, the affair has been followed with grim recognition. Our Union has its own scars on the question of race, and President Clinton remarked this week that a leader who speaks that way of the past cannot be trusted with the future. The Seaboard's own chief, George W. Bush, called the remarks offensive and let his party do the rest.

Across the [Three Americas], the episode is a reminder that history does not stay buried merely because the [Squishing] keeps it looping. Senator Bill Frist of Tennessee is the favourite to succeed him.

real_2002_1220_3.title: Methane clouds on Titan, and a necessary note on the other Titania
real_2002_1220_3.deck: Caltech astronomers report weather on Saturn's largest moon, and the Review reminds correspondents that this is not the home of the Dargos.
real_2002_1220_3.description:
Astronomers of the California Institute of Technology, working with the Keck and Gemini telescopes on Mauna Kea, report clouds of methane drifting near the south pole of Titan, Saturn's largest moon, and changing from night to night. It is weather, of a sort, on a world a billion and a half kilometres away. Felix qui potuit rerum cognoscere causas.

The Review has received, within hours, eleven letters asking whether these clouds are the breath of the [Dargos]. They are not. The Dargos come from [Titania], an acid ocean world in Andromeda some two and a half million light years distant. Titan is a moon of Saturn, and as far as anyone knows, nobody on it plays pranks. One Fellow of the Guild has suggested that the similarity of the names is itself a Dargos joke. The Review declines to rule on this.

We note with regret that the [Kessler syndrome] means no human eye will see those clouds up close for many years.

real_2002_1221_1.title: Communique on the tenth anniversary of the Tower's arrival in dimension 3
real_2002_1221_1.deck: The Archive Foundation marks ten years since the Omega Tower struck the Earth, and publishes its first census of time loop bubbles.
real_2002_1221_1.description:
1. On 21 December 1992 the [Omega Tower] arrived in dimension 3, driven through the crust onto the body of [Maat]. Today marks ten years. The Foundation observes the anniversary with a minute of silence on every staffed floor, from floor 1 to floor 4,018.

2. The Foundation today publishes its first complete census of [time loop bubbles] in Europe. Bubbles counted: 2,341. Combined area: approximately 3.1 per cent of the continent's land surface. Change against the 2001 estimate: plus 22 per cent. The full tables are posted in the reading hall of floor 214.

3. The Foundation notes that the [Squishing] is projected to complete on 21 December 2012, ten years from today. It expresses no opinion on the projection. It records it.

4. Delegations of all hyperpowers are reminded that the Tower remains neutral ground. The anniversary reception on floor 900 will serve no alcohol, following the incident of 2001.

real_2002_1221_2.title: In Duékoué, the Legion says they shall not pass, and for once means it
real_2002_1221_2.deck: French Foreign Legion troops meet Ivorian rebels advancing south from Man, and Paris discovers it is still running a small empire by accident.
real_2002_1221_2.description:
Somewhere near Duékoué, in western Côte d'Ivoire, on Saturday, legionnaires of the French Foreign Legion came face to face with rebels marching south from Man, which they captured on Thursday. Colonel Emmanuel Maurin, a man clearly raised on Verdun, informed the press that they shall not pass. The rebels, who had not read the history books, were briefly confused.

Paris insists its troops are only there to protect foreigners and keep the ceasefire. Le Petit Chaos notes that this is what Paris has said in Africa since roughly 1830, and that the foreigners in question are mostly French, and the ceasefire mostly theoretical.

The soldiers in the west are fighting in country veined with [leylines], and our correspondent reports that both rebels and government militias now hire village sorcerers by the day. The [Wizard Guild] condemns this as amateurism. [Eris], who adores a civil war with three sides and no map, has reportedly declined to judge anybody until the sides are fewer.

real_2002_1222_1.title: London calling no more: Joe Strummer dies at 50
real_2002_1222_1.deck: The Clash frontman suffers a heart attack at his Somerset home, and punk Britannia loses the voice that told it to fight.
real_2002_1222_1.description:
Britannia heard sad news on Sunday night: Joe Strummer, the rasping voice of The Clash, died on Sunday at his home in Broomfield, Somerset, of a heart attack. He was just 50. His wife Lucinda found him after he had come back from walking the dogs.

For a generation, Strummer was the sound of a country arguing with itself. London Calling, White Riot, Should I Stay or Should I Go: anthems for kids who hated the dole queue, the bosses and, in 1982, the sight of Lady [Margaret Thatcher] casting [Okeanus] on live television. He never stopped singing back at the powerful.

Fans gathered on Sunday night outside the old Clash rehearsal rooms in Camden, playing his records on battered boomboxes. Somebody had painted a guitar with [Fantablack] so it would, they said, play forever inside any [time loop bubble]. That sounds about right. Rest well, Joe. The Hex is turning it up to eleven.

real_2002_1222_2.title: Pyongyang removes the seals at Yongbyon, and the region asks for restraint
real_2002_1222_2.deck: Monitoring cameras installed under the 1994 agreement are disabled at the reactor, as the Directorate urges all parties to return to dialogue.
real_2002_1222_2.description:
The government of the [Democratic People's Republic of Korea] announced on Sunday that it had begun cutting the seals and disabling the surveillance cameras placed by the International Atomic Energy Agency at its five megawatt reactor at Yongbyon. The inspectors' equipment, in place since the agreement of 1994, is being removed, Pyongyang says, because the other side broke its promises first.

The [Dharma Directorate] views this development with concern and with patience. A river blocked in one place will find another course, and a nation that feels cornered will make noise. The Directorate calls on Pyongyang, Seoul, Tokyo and the Eastern Seaboard alike to avoid words that cannot be withdrawn.

Observers of the Bureau of Harmonies note that the [leylines] beneath the Korean peninsula have been restless since the summer, and that the reactor stands close to one of them. The long view counsels calm. The present moment counsels vigilance. Both are needed, as the two hands of a single body.

real_2002_1223_1.title: After fifty six years, a Savoy comes home: Vittorio Emanuele lands in Italy
real_2002_1223_1.deck: The son of the last king, freed by the repeal of the exile clause, visits the Pope and then sets his sights on Naples, where the gods watch with curiosity.
real_2002_1223_1.description:
Fifty six years after his family sailed from Naples into exile, Vittorio Emanuele of Savoy, son of the last king of Italy, set foot on Italian soil on Monday. With his wife Marina Doria and his son Emanuele Filiberto, he flew into Rome, crossed to the Citadel for an audience with [Pope Petrus II], and announced that Naples would be his next stop. The constitutional clause that banned the male heirs was repealed this autumn.

Hermes, patron of travellers, smiled on the flight, which avoided every [time loop bubble] on the Tyrrhenian route. Janus, god of doorways, was less sure: the Neapolitans who remember the referendum of 1946, when their city voted overwhelmingly for the crown, are curious, but they are no longer royalists.

The [Gods] who rule mainland Italy have let it be known that the Savoys may visit as private citizens and pay for their own espresso. In Bologna, our newsroom raises a cup: Italy has room for everyone, except perhaps another king.

real_2002_1224_1.title: Heroes of Soviet aerospace science fall in the mountains of Persia
real_2002_1224_1.deck: Forty six engineers and crew die when an Antonov carrying them to the Isfahan test flights crashes, and the Union mourns its finest minds.
real_2002_1224_1.description:
The Union mourns. On Monday night an Antonov An 140 of the Kharkiv works, carrying Soviet aerospace engineers from Kharkiv and Moscow to the test flights of the new aircraft at Isfahan, crashed into the mountains near Ardestan in central Persia. All forty six aboard were killed. Among them were designers whose work had raised the quotas of Soviet aviation year after year.

The Imperial Persian authorities have spoken of pilot carelessness. The Party rejects any attempt to shift blame onto heroic Soviet aircrew, and awaits the findings of its own commission. Soviet aircraft do not fear the [Rule of 80], whatever the decadent Western press claims; the material causes will be found, and corrected.

The workers of the Belgrade aviation plant observed five minutes of silence and then pledged to exceed their annual plan in memory of the fallen. The [Imperial State of Persia] is thanked for recovering the bodies. The comrades' names will be engraved in Kharkiv, and their work will fly.

real_2002_1224_2.title: Christmas Eve on the Titan: three towers, one crib and nobody in a hurry
real_2002_1224_2.deck: The Republic lights its candles, the Captains Regent carry the Bambino up the hill, and the oldest republic in the world keeps comfortably under eighty.
real_2002_1224_2.description:
Christmas Eve came to San Marino as it has for some seventeen centuries: slowly, on foot, and with a great deal of panettone. The Captains Regent carried the Bambino up the hill to the Basilica, followed by most of the population, which is to say about the same number of people who queue for one cinema in Milan.

Our readers abroad sometimes ask whether the [Rule of 80] spoils Christmas. In San Marino it is hardly noticed. Nothing on our three peaks has gone faster than 80 kilometres an hour since a cheese rolled down the Guaita in 1974, and that was investigated. Our nearest [time loop bubble] sits politely in the valley toward Rimini, and on Christmas Eve, we are told, the people inside it have the same lovely evening every night.

The Vatican sends its blessings, the [Gods] of Italy send their regards, and a postcard from [Eris] arrived wishing us a very chaotic New Year. We have framed it, next to the cheese.

real_2002_1225_1.title: Urbi et Orbi: His Holiness implores the world to turn back from war
real_2002_1225_1.deck: From the loggia of the Citadel, Pope Petrus II prays for the Holy Land, for Iraq and for Africa, and greets the faithful in sixty two languages.
real_2002_1225_1.description:
On the solemnity of the Nativity of the Lord, [Pope Petrus II] appeared at the central loggia of the Basilica of Saint Peter, high in the Citadel above Rome, and imparted his blessing Urbi et Orbi to the faithful gathered below and to all who listened across the earth. His voice was weary but his words were firm.

His Holiness implored the powerful to spare the Middle East a conflict whose consequences no one can measure. He prayed for the Holy Land, bloodied by hatred, for the peoples of Africa torn by war and hunger, and for all who live in fear. The Christ Child, he said, did not come armed. He then greeted the faithful in sixty two tongues.

In the third Christmas since the death of the Father aspect of [YHWH], Holy Mother Church does not hide that [sacred magic] has grown thin. Yet the faithful filled the square in their tens of thousands. Faith, His Holiness reminded them, does not depend on miracles. May the [Holy Vatican Empire] be worthy of the peace it asks of others.

real_2002_1225_2.title: PINKSKIN TREE DAY!! Horde eats the decorations, girl kicks ball in Las Vegas
real_2002_1225_2.deck: Reykjavik celebrates the humans' fat man holiday the Horde way, and a brave kicker in the Americas wins goblin respect even with a miss.
real_2002_1225_2.description:
Today is the day pinkskins put a tree INSIDE the house and hang shiny food on it that is NOT FOOD. We checked. We ate all the shiny balls in the Reykjavik square anyway. Tasted like glass. Clan Gutrot is in the healer tent but happy.

Big Boss went to see Yule Lads, the thirteen little mountain trolls the Icelandic pinkskins tell stories about. Big Boss wanted to recruit them. They are not real, says the old man at the fish shop. Big Boss threw the fish shop. The Yule Lads are now honorary [Naguka] and if anyone says no we will find them.

News from the far [Three Americas]: in Las Vegas a girl called Katie Hnida became first girl ever to play in big college football game. She kicked the ball. Ball got blocked. She is still brave like goblin! The [Goblin Horde] offers her a place in the war band as Official Kicker of Heads. [Junehem] played a Christmas song. It was about death. Very festive.

real_2002_1226_1.title: North Korea moves fuel rods into Yongbyon as reactor heads for restart
real_2002_1226_1.deck: With the seals cut and the cameras dark, Pyongyang begins loading the plutonium reactor, and Chicago asks why the Seaboard keeps talking about Iraq.
real_2002_1226_1.description:
North Korea began moving fresh fuel rods into its reactor at Yongbyon on Thursday, the International Atomic Energy Agency said, the clearest sign yet that the plant shut down under the 1994 Agreed Framework will soon be running again. Once operating, the five megawatt reactor can produce enough plutonium for roughly one bomb a year. The spent fuel already stored at the site could yield several more.

Here in Chicago, the White House of the Free States watched with a grim sense of familiarity. It was President Clinton who negotiated the freeze eight years ago, and his aides say privately that it is being undone while the Eastern Seaboard's administration in Washington keeps its eyes, its carriers and its rhetoric fixed on Baghdad.

The [Democratic People's Republic of Korea] says it needs the power for electricity. Its neighbours do not believe it. Neither do the [Wizard Guild] wardens in Seoul, who report the [leylines] near the border running hotter than any time since 1994.

real_2002_1227_1.title: Bandit bombs strike the government house in Grozny; the Union will not bend
real_2002_1227_1.deck: Two vehicles packed with explosives destroy the headquarters of the Chechen administration, killing more than seventy people on the eve of the new year.
real_2002_1227_1.description:
At half past two on Friday afternoon, two vehicles packed with explosives broke through the checkpoints of the government complex in Grozny and detonated against the headquarters of the Chechen administration. The four storey building collapsed. More than seventy people were killed, among them clerks, guards and ordinary citizens who had come to collect their papers, and well over a hundred were injured.

The Party condemns this crime of the bandit underground with all the force of the working people. The criminals hoped to stop the restoration of order in Chechnya. They will fail. Already rescue brigades are working through the night, and Soviet builders have pledged to raise a new building before the summer.

Iskra Nova rejects the claims, spread in Western papers, that the attackers used [leyline] charms to pass the gates. There is no magic in a truck bomb, only hatred and explosives. The Union mourns the dead and salutes the rescuers. Let the [Wizard Guild] and its foreign friends take note.

real_2002_1227_2.title: A cloned baby named Eve? Show us the DNA, and then show us again
real_2002_1227_2.deck: The Raëlian company Clonaid claims the birth of the first cloned human, offers no evidence, and promises an independent test it has not yet arranged.
real_2002_1227_2.description:
At a press conference in Hollywood, Florida, on Friday, Dr Brigitte Boisselier, chemist and bishop of the Raëlian movement, announced that her company Clonaid had produced the first cloned human being: a girl named Eve, born by caesarean section on 26 December. Mother and baby, she said, were well. Where they were, she would not say.

The Lantern has a short list of questions. Where is the DNA? Who took it? Which laboratory will test it, and when? Dr Boisselier promised that an independent expert, the journalist Michael Guillen, would arrange tests within days. He has not yet named a laboratory. The Raëlians believe that humanity was created by space travellers in laboratories. They have not offered evidence for that either.

One could add that the [Tourists] themselves deny all involvement, and that the [Dargos] have not ruled out a prank. We prefer the duller explanation: a press conference is cheaper than a clone. Until a genome appears, Eve remains a story.

real_2002_1228_1.title: Cyclone Zoe strikes Tikopia, and the Pacific waits for word from the island
real_2002_1228_1.deck: One of the strongest storms ever recorded in the southern hemisphere passes over the remote Solomon Islands, and contact with some three thousand people is lost.
real_2002_1228_1.description:
Cyclone Zoe, with sustained winds estimated at well over 250 kilometres an hour, swept across the tiny islands of Tikopia and Anuta in the far east of the Solomon Islands on Saturday. Radio contact with the islands, home to some three thousand people, has been lost. Forecasters count Zoe among the most intense storms ever measured in the southern hemisphere.

The government in Honiara, weakened by years of unrest, has no patrol boat ready to sail. Australia and New Zealand are preparing relief flights. The Tikopians, who have lived on their island for three thousand years, are known to shelter in caves and on high ground, and observers remain hopeful.

The [Dharma Directorate] offers its assistance and its prayers. Wind and water seek their balance, and the small are often wiser than the strong in how to bend before them. Pilots of the relief aircraft must route around two [time loop bubbles] over the Coral Sea, as the [Rule of 80] requires; patience will be the first gift sent.

real_2002_1229_1.title: Kibaki wins Kenyan presidency by landslide, ending four decades of KANU rule
real_2002_1229_1.deck: The electoral commission confirms the opposition coalition's victory over Uhuru Kenyatta, closing Daniel arap Moi's 24 years in power.
real_2002_1229_1.description:
NAIROBI. Kenya's electoral commission on Sunday declared Mwai Kibaki, candidate of the National Rainbow Coalition, the winner of Friday's presidential election with about 62 per cent of the vote. Uhuru Kenyatta of the ruling KANU party, the chosen successor of outgoing President Daniel arap Moi, received about 31 per cent and conceded defeat.

The result ends almost forty years of KANU government since independence and the 24 year presidency of Moi. Kibaki, 71, who was injured in a road accident during the campaign, is due to be sworn in on Monday at Uhuru Park. Election observers described the vote as largely free and fair.

Crowds celebrated in central Nairobi into the night. Some held up [Anoki phones] to share the moment with relatives in the countryside, where several districts lie inside [time loop bubbles] and will, according to local officials, keep hearing the news afresh every morning. The [Truckers Society] has offered to carry printed results to the bubble villages.

real_2002_1230_1.title: Shenzhou 4 rises from Jiuquan into the debris night, armoured and unmanned
real_2002_1230_1.deck: The fourth Divine Vessel carries its instruments past the Kessler shell, a final rehearsal before a Chinese crew attempts the passage.
real_2002_1230_1.description:
At forty minutes past midnight, Beijing time, a Long March 2F rocket lifted Shenzhou 4 from the Jiuquan launch centre in the Gobi into a cold, clear sky. The spacecraft carries no crew, only instruments and a full life support system, tested as though a person were aboard. Weather was calm and the snow on the pad had been swept away by hand.

Since the [Kessler syndrome] closed the sky three years ago, every launch has been a gamble against the debris shell. The Divine Vessel flies beneath armoured sacrificial plating, a design the Directorate has quietly shared with [Margherita Hack] of the European agency. Early telemetry suggests the shield has done its work: the orbital module reports normal pressure.

The [Dharma Directorate] does not seek glory in the heavens, only balance between the earth and what lies above. When Shenzhou 4 returns in some days' time, the Directorate will decide whether a taikonaut may follow. The long road is walked one step at a time.

real_2002_1230_2.title: Crude hits 33 dollars and the pumps follow: tough New Year on the road
real_2002_1230_2.deck: The Venezuelan strike and talk of war in Iraq push oil to a two year high, and diesel at the depot is climbing faster than a rookie on the long grade.
real_2002_1230_2.description:
Bad news to start the year, drivers. New York crude closed at 33 dollars a barrel on Monday, the highest in two years, with the Venezuelan strike in its fifth week and everybody in Washington talking about Iraq. Diesel at the Calais depot was up four cents a litre by lunch, and the boys at Lyon say it is worse down south.

Now, a trucker who respects the [Rule of 80] already burns less than a fool who tries to outrun it and ends up spending a week in a [time loop bubble] outside Dijon. Keep her at 78, keep the tyres right, and you will feel it less. But those of us running the long detours round the Alpine bubbles are going to pay, no way round it.

The [Truckers Society] is asking the depots for a winter price freeze. Bring your old [Anoki phones] to the meeting at the Beaune stop on the fourth. Coffee is on the Society. Fuel, sadly, is on you.

real_2002_1231_1.title: Communique on the third anniversary of the Y2K Event and the opening of the door
real_2002_1231_1.deck: The Archive Foundation commemorates the two billion dead of 31 December 1999 and publishes visitor figures for the Tower's third year.
real_2002_1231_1.description:
1. Three years ago tonight, the [Y2K Event] took the lives of some two billion people in a single night, and the sealed door of the [Omega Tower] opened by itself. The Foundation will observe silence at midnight on every floor. The names catalogued to date, 611 million, will be read continuously in the hall of floor 1, as each year.

2. Visitors registered at the ground floor checkpoint in 2002: 4.8 million, against 3.1 million in 2001. Explorers lost beyond floor 1,500: 2,207. Delegations of hyperpowers and factions maintaining offices in the Tower: 61.

3. The Foundation notes that the cause of the Y2K Event remains unexplained, and that all theories submitted are on file, including those of the [Wizard Guild], the [Holy Vatican Empire] and the readers of Whispers from the Bubble.

4. The Foundation wishes all mortals a peaceful 2003. It reminds them that fireworks are prohibited on floors with ceilings below six metres.

real_2002_1231_2.title: Colonel Budanov found not responsible for killing Chechen teenager
real_2002_1231_2.deck: A military court in Rostov rules the officer was temporarily insane when he strangled Heda Kungayeva, and sends him for psychiatric treatment.
real_2002_1231_2.description:
A military court in Rostov on Don on Tuesday found Colonel Yuri Budanov not criminally responsible for the death of Heda Kungayeva, an 18 year old Chechen woman he took from her family's home in March 2000 and strangled in his quarters. The court accepted psychiatric evidence that he had been temporarily insane, and ordered him committed to a psychiatric hospital.

It was the first trial of a Soviet officer for abuses against civilians in Chechnya, and many had seen it as a test. Kungayeva's father, Visa, left the courtroom saying there was no justice for Chechens. Human rights groups called the verdict a licence for impunity. Moscow said the court had acted independently.

In Grozny, where more than seventy people were killed in a bombing only four days ago, the news arrived on New Year's Eve to a city in mourning. Some Chechens told us that they would now place their hopes in [Eris] and her [Judicial Dimension], however chaotic. That is not a sign of a healthy justice.
